# Luuna Missions

Git-native tickets and structured work plans. This is Luuna's maintained MIT-licensed fork of Seeds, imported from upstream version **0.6.0**. The Luuna package identity is **@luuna/missions-cli** in the independent public repository [luuna-ai/luuna-missions](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions). The package remains private and unpublished.

## Run from a checkout

Use Bun **1.4.3** and Go **1.22 or newer**. Keep `go` on `PATH`, or set `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` to the Go executable. The package bin at `src/index.ts` is a Bun compatibility launcher: it builds the matching native executable on first use, caches it under `dist/`, and forwards arguments, standard streams, signals, and the exit code to Go.

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun src/index.ts --help
bun run verify
```

`bun run build:native` builds the native cache without running a command. A compiled executable can also run directly without Bun; `go run ./cmd/luuna-missions --help` runs it from source. The cache is local and ignored by Git, so a fresh checkout or package install needs Go for the first launch.

The primary command is `luuna-missions`. Package bin aliases are `lms`, `lm` (compatibility), and `missions`; the consuming Luuna launcher exposes `luuna missions <args>`. Its current pinned Bun entrypoint can continue to use the shim. Updating Luuna's exact submodule pin and installer is a separate reviewed integration, and changes in this repository do not update that consumer automatically.

## What it manages

`init` creates `.luuna/missions/` with `issues.jsonl`, `plans.jsonl`, `templates.jsonl`, and `config.yaml`. Use `create`, `ready`, `update --claim`, and `close` for tickets; `dep`, `label`, `block`, and `unblock` manage relationships; `plan` manages structured plans and child tickets. `tpl` creates reusable issue convoys. `config`, `doctor`, `sync`, `prime`, `onboard`, `setup claude`, `guard`, and `completions` provide project and agent tooling. Run `luuna-missions --help` or see the [full CLI and system map](/docs/components-missions-docs-cli-system-map) for every command, option family, side effect, and integration.

Project discovery walks upward from the working directory. A legacy `.seeds/` directory may be moved to `.luuna/missions/` on first access; see [MIGRATION.md](/docs/components-missions-migration). Environment variables use the `LUUNA_MISSIONS_` prefix. The Go implementation preserves the JSON and JSONL contracts, advisory locks, atomic writes, and existing project schemas. Luuna owns runtime policy and approval enforcement; Atlas supplies optional plan prior art and decision recording, while Beacon owns reusable prompts.

`sync` stages `.luuna/missions/` and commits the current Git index, including unrelated paths that were already staged. Use `git diff --cached --name-only` to inspect other staged paths before committing. Self-upgrade remains disabled while the package is unpublished. Never replace this fork with a similarly named registry package; update through a reviewed commit and an exact Luuna submodule pin. Dependency installation does not alter root Git hooks.

## Development and releases

The runtime is in `cmd/` and `internal/`. `src/index-legacy.ts` and the TypeScript modules under `src/` remain as the compatibility oracle for the differential test corpus. `bun run verify` runs the TypeScript type check, instruction check, Bun tests, Go tests, and Go-versus-TypeScript CLI parity cases. CI declares this surface on Linux and Windows using Bun 1.4.3 and the Go version in `go.mod`. See [AGENTS.md](/docs/components-missions-agents) for repository rules and [the system map](/docs/components-missions-docs-cli-system-map) for validation limits.

The repository is maintained by the luuna-ai organization. Registry publishing is disabled and requires no npm token. Luuna pins a reviewed commit, never a floating branch; update its submodule only after CI and a consumer smoke pass. Read [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-missions-upstream) for provenance and [the original README](/docs/components-missions-docs-upstream-readme) for inherited command examples. Upstream release/runbook documents are historical references and do not authorize publication.

## Origin and attribution

Luuna Missions is derived from [Seeds](https://github.com/jayminwest/seeds) 0.6.0 by Jaymin West (MIT). The original license is preserved in [LICENSE](/docs/components-missions-license), and provenance is recorded in [UPSTREAM.md](/docs/components-missions-upstream). Seeds is independent; Luuna Missions is not affiliated with or endorsed by its authors.

title: Missions: Changelog
description: All notable changes to Seeds will be documented in this file.
text:
# Changelog

All notable changes to Seeds will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed
- Removed references to unrelated upstream ecosystem tools from comments, schema descriptions, specs and test fixtures. Wording only; no CLI or JSON contract changes.

### Fixed
- `luuna-missions guard` and `luuna-missions plan submit --plan -` read piped stdin on Windows. `Bun.stdin.text()` let the process exit 0 before the read finished, so `guard` allowed every edit and `plan submit` did nothing.

### Changed
- The test suite passes on Windows, and CI runs `bun run verify` on `windows-latest`. Fake `luuna-atlas` executables use a `.cmd` launcher there, and a test preload puts Git for Windows' POSIX tools on PATH.
- Atlas coupling now shells out to `luuna-atlas` (resolved on PATH; absent remains a soft no-op) instead of `ml`, and passes `--evidence-missions`. Module `plan-mulch.ts` is now `plan-atlas.ts`. Plan-template section key `mulch_source` is now `atlas_source`; the old key is still read from existing configs (and rewritten on `config set`) via `src/legacy-layout.ts`.
- Project data moved from `.seeds/` to `.luuna/missions/`. A legacy `.seeds/` directory is renamed automatically the first time any command (including `init`) runs, with one notice line on stderr; managed `.gitattributes` / `.gitignore` lines are rewritten. If both layouts exist the command fails and asks the user to resolve it; symlinked `.luuna` or `.seeds` is refused. The legacy-name handling lives in `src/legacy-layout.ts`.
- Removed the `sd` and `seeds` bin aliases; `luuna-missions` and `lm` remain. Help, usage and error text, `onboard` / `prime` snippets and shell completions use `luuna-missions`.
- Environment variables renamed `SEEDS_*` to `LUUNA_MISSIONS_*` (for example `LUUNA_MISSIONS_DEBUG`, `LUUNA_MISSIONS_LOG_LEVEL`). Internal identifiers renamed to match.
- `setup claude` writes hooks that call `luuna-missions prime --compact` and `luuna-missions guard`, and replaces hooks installed by earlier versions. Default project name and onboard/plan-backref markers use `missions` instead of `seeds`.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-09-29

### Added
- `sd update <id> --claim [--as <agent>]`: atomic claim under the issues lock. Succeeds only when the issue is `open` and unassigned (or already assigned to the caller); sets `in_progress` + `assignee`. Otherwise exits 1 with a clear error, so two agents can never both claim. Identity defaults to `$USER`; rejects `--status` / `--assignee` alongside. (seeds-8ade)
- `sd create --from <id>`: records `discoveredFrom` provenance (non-blocking; shown by `sd show` as `From:`). The source issue must exist. (seeds-8ade)
- `sd create` / `sd update --intent <r-id>` (repeatable, comma-separated ok): stores linked roots idea id(s) in the top-level `intent` field — a string for one id, `string[]` for several — which roots reads directly. Ids must match `r-` + 4–8 hex. `sd update --intent` replaces the list. (seeds-8ade)
- `sd prime` appends live state: in-progress issues (with assignee) and the top 5 ready issues. `--json` adds a `state` object. Skipped by `--export`; best effort (never fails the command). (seeds-2d9d)
- `sd setup claude [--remove]`: installs Claude Code hooks in `<project>/.claude/settings.json` — SessionStart `sd prime --compact` and PreToolUse `sd guard` on Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit. Idempotent; keeps unrelated settings and hooks. (seeds-2d9d)
- `sd guard`: PreToolUse hook handler that denies hand edits to `.seeds/*.jsonl` with a reason naming the `sd` command to use. Unparsable input fails open. (seeds-2d9d)
- `seeds` long bin alongside `sd`. (seeds-2d9d)

### Changed
- `sd prime` static text trimmed (~half the size). Close checklist runs `bun run verify` when package.json defines it (else a generic gates step), no longer demands `git push` as critical ("push per repo conventions"), and allows in-session TodoWrite checklists. Claim step uses `sd update <id> --claim`. (seeds-2d9d)
- `sd onboard` snippet is shorter and uses `sd update <id> --claim`; points at `sd setup claude`. Schema bumped 7 → 8, so existing snippets report outdated. (seeds-2d9d)
- README drops the "Replaces beads" framing. (seeds-2d9d)

## [0.5.15] - 2026-07-17

Nightwatch patrol fix (plan pl-dcda): render plan-membership suffix in `sd blocked` human output.

### Fixed
- `sd blocked` now renders the plan-membership suffix in both plain and default (ANSI) output, mirroring what `sd list` and `sd ready` already do. Previously an issue that belonged to an approved plan showed no plan hint in `sd blocked`. The plain branch now appends `planLineSuffix(planForIssue(...))` to the stripped one-liner; the default branch passes it to `printIssueOneLine`. `ids` / `compact` / `--json` output is unchanged (JSON was already routed through `issueJsonWithPlan`).   - `Step.existing_seed?: string` on the `sd plan submit` JSON schema — a step with `existing_seed: "<seed-id>"` adopts the named open seed at that index instead of spawning a fresh child. Mutually exclusive with `plan_template` on the same step. Title mismatch (`seed.title !== step.title`) emits a `⚠` warning to stderr and keeps the seed's title. (seeds-7002, seeds-24c6)
  - `sd plan adopt <plan-id> <seed-id...> [--step <i>]` — post-submit adoption. `--step` is the 1-based blueprint step index to anchor against; omit it for a loose adoption (no `plan_step_index` is recorded and the backref reads `Adopted into plan <pl-id>`). Adopting an in-progress seed is allowed and intentional. (seeds-2b93)
  - `sd plan release <plan-id> <seed-id...>` — detach one or more seeds without closing. `stripPlanBackref` removes only the marker block from the seed's description (returns the field as `undefined` when nothing else remained), `plan_id` + `plan_step_index` are cleared, the parent↔child edges are unwired, and the seed is dropped from `plan.children` (and `plan.adoptedChildren` if present). The seed itself remains open. (seeds-2b8a)
  - `applyOverwrite` matches existing plan children by `step.existing_seed` id first, then by `step.title` — id-first precedence keeps adopted children stable across overwrites and prevents title-match races with id-pinned steps. Pre-existing overwrite-by-title behavior is unchanged when no step uses `existing_seed`; the same-plan-adoption shortcut allows the overwrite path to refresh an already-attached child without tripping the cross-plan rejection. (seeds-99ae)
  - `Plan.adoptedChildren?: string[]` — adopted seed ids tracked on the plan row, persisted only when non-empty so plans that never use adoption produce byte-identical `plans.jsonl` output. `sd plan show` renders adopted entries with a trailing muted `(adopted)` tag in human output (top-level and nested sub-plans); `--json` adds `adopted: true` on each child summary listed in `plan.adoptedChildren`. (seeds-a3ab)
- Rejections (fail-fast, pre-write): adopting a seed that is closed, missing, attached to a *different* plan, or equal to the plan's parent seed; listing the same seed twice in one command or two `steps[]` in one submit; combining `existing_seed` with `plan_template`; releasing a seed that isn't attached to the named plan or equals the plan's parent; `--step <i>` out of range on `sd plan adopt`. Cross-plan reassignment is two explicit commands: `sd plan release <other-pl> <seed>` then `sd plan adopt <new-pl> <seed>` (a future `--reassign-from <pl>` flag is deferred).
- PLAN_SPEC.md gains an "Adoption and Release" section documenting the lifecycle (per-field add/remove on each side), validation tables, lock order, and edge cases (loose adoption, JSONL byte stability, manual notes around the backref markers).

## [0.4.4] - 2026-05-13

### Changed
- **BREAKING (plan submit wire format)**: `steps[].blocks` in `sd plan submit` payloads now uses **1-based** step indices (step 1 is the first step, step N is the last). Previously 0-based. LLMs — the primary authors of plan files — consistently produced 1-based blocks, so the wire format moves to match. Concretely: a two-step plan where step 1 blocks step 2 is now `[{ title: "...", blocks: [2] }, { title: "...", blocks: [] }]`. The validator rejects `0` and out-of-range values with `step indices are 1-based; valid range 1..N`; the self-reference check is now "step n cannot have `n` in its own blocks". The internal `Issue.plan_step_index` back-link stored on each spawned child stays 0-based — it's not author-facing. `sd plan show` renders stored 1-based values verbatim (no offset shift), so output is unchanged for plans submitted under the new format. Plans stored before this change (`.seeds/plans.jsonl` rows with the old 0-based values) are not migrated; the stored numbers are display-only after spawning since children already carry resolved seed-id `blocks`/`blockedBy` edges. PLAN_SPEC.md, the `sd plan prompt` INSTRUCTIONS string, and the README example all reflect 1-based indexing. (seeds-185f)

### Added
- `Plan.name?: string` — optional short human-readable label so `sd plan list` and `sd plan show` carry semantic signal beyond opaque `pl-*` ids. `sd plan submit` resolves the name in priority order: `--name <text>` flag > top-level `name` field in the plan JSON > parent seed's title (fallback). `sd plan show` renders a `Name:` header line; `sd plan list` shows the name (or `(unnamed)`) in a fixed-width column between `rev` and `template`, truncated with `…` at ~40 chars. `--json` payloads gain the field additively — existing plans without a `name` row continue to deserialize. `--overwrite` preserves the existing name unless `--name` or the plan JSON supplies a new one. (seeds-5640)

## [0.4.3] - 2026-05-10

### Added
- `sd show <id> [<id2> ...]` accepts multiple ids in one call; agents reviewing related issues (blockers, deps, plan children) no longer pay one shell-out per id. Each output format gets a per-format separator: default human uses a 60-char `─` divider between entries, `--format plain` uses a blank line, `--format compact` and `--format ids` print one entry per line, `--json` returns an `issues` array (with optional `errors` for unknown ids). Single-id behavior — including the `{issue, plan, plan_children}` JSON shape and the `pl-*` → `sd plan show` routing — is preserved exactly; plan ids in multi-id mode are reported as per-id errors pointing at `sd plan show`. Unknown ids do not abort the rest of the call (mirroring `sd close`); the command exits non-zero when any id fails. (seeds-4eba)
- `sd config` command tree — schema-driven read/write surface for `.seeds/config.yaml` aimed at warren V2's per-tool config UI (warren ROADMAP R-10). `sd config schema [--json]` emits the JSON Schema; `sd config show [--path <p>] [--json]` reads the whole config or a value at a dot-path; `sd config set <path> <value>` validates + writes atomically (`<value>` is YAML-parsed); `sd config unset <path>` removes a value. Writes hold the `config.yaml` advisory lock and validate the post-write file against the schema; partial writes that would leave the file inconsistent are rejected. The schema covers `project`, `version`, `max_plan_depth`, and the nested `plan_templates` editor (with built-in template defaults in `examples`). Locked with a golden test in `src/commands/config.test.ts` so any wire-format change is intentional. (seeds-ac83)
- `sd doctor` adds a `closed-fields-consistency` check (`--fix`-able): non-closed issues with stale `closedAt`/`closeReason` fail (fix clears both); closed issues missing `closedAt` warn (fix sets it to `updatedAt`). Doctor pass count bumped 11 → 12. (seeds-8526)

### Fixed
- `sd show <pl-id>` now shows the plan instead of erroring `Issue not found`. When the requested id starts with `pl-` and isn't in `issues.jsonl`, `sd show` routes to the same renderer as `sd plan show` for both default and `--json` output. `--format compact|plain|ids` on a plan id errors with a hint pointing to `sd plan show`. Issue lookup happens first, so projects literally named `pl` (whose issue ids share the `pl-XXXX` shape) still resolve normally. (seeds-66de)
- `sd update --status open` (or any non-closed status) now drops stale `closedAt` / `closeReason` from the record. Previously a close→reopen cycle left phantom close metadata so `sd show` displayed a "closed at" timestamp on an open issue. (seeds-8526)

## [0.4.2] - 2026-05-10

### Added
- `Issue.extensions?: Record<string, unknown>` — optional, opaque-to-seeds field for runtime metadata that consumers (warren, greenhouse, overstory) own under namespaced keys. Seeds performs no schema validation on the value; it round-trips byte-for-byte through `.seeds/issues.jsonl`. (seeds-f35a, plan pl-c195)
- `sd show` renders an `Extensions: key=value ...` line when the field is present and non-empty; each value is JSON-encoded so strings stay quoted and nested objects/arrays/null are unambiguous. JSON output is unchanged — extensions already serialized as part of the issue payload. (seeds-e7ea)
- `sd update --extensions <json>` shallow-merges (`{...existing, ...incoming}`) a JSON object into `Issue.extensions`. `--clear-extensions` removes the field. The two flags are mutually exclusive; arrays, `null`, scalars, and malformed JSON are rejected with a clear error. Merge is one level deep — consumers needing nested structure should keep keys flat (e.g. `lastRunId`, `lastRunAt`) rather than nesting under `lastRun`. (seeds-be14)
- `sd ready --respect-schedule` (opt-in) excludes issues where `extensions.queued === true` (strict equality) or `extensions.scheduledFor` parses to a future ISO8601 timestamp. Default `sd ready` behavior is unchanged — agents still see queued items unless they ask for the schedule-aware view. Designed for warren's cron-driven dispatch. (seeds-614b)
- `sd doctor` adds an `extensions-schema` check that flags non-object `extensions` values (null, arrays, scalars). `sd doctor --fix` drops malformed values. (seeds-56ff)

### Convention
- **Extension namespacing.** Each consumer owns a top-level prefix on `Issue.extensions` (e.g. `extensions.warren_*`, `extensions.greenhouse_*`) or a single namespaced sub-object. The two well-known keys consumed by `sd ready --respect-schedule` are `extensions.queued` (boolean) and `extensions.scheduledFor` (ISO8601 string). Other keys are opaque to seeds.

## [0.4.1] - 2026-05-08

### Added
- `sd plan show|validate|outcome|review` now accept a seed ID in addition to a `pl-*` plan ID — resolves via `seed.plan_id`, removing the round-trip through `sd plan list` when an agent already has the seed in hand. (seeds-51bc)
- `sd plan submit` prints a Next-action block to stderr on success (`sd plan show`, `sd ready`, conditionally `sd plan review`) and surfaces the recorded mulch decision id on the `--record-decision` success path. JSON output is untouched: `--json` mode suppresses the Next block so stdout stays parseable. (seeds-d6cb)
- Child seeds spawned by `sd plan submit` carry a marker-delimited "plan backref" block in their description with the step number, plan id, parent seed id+title, template, an excerpt of `sections.approach`, and a `sd plan show <pl-id>` link. `--overwrite` refreshes just the marker section in place; assignee, labels, and any manual notes outside the markers survive the rewrite. (seeds-76af)
- `sd onboard` snippet surfaces the installed seeds version as both a `<!-- seeds-onboard:v$VERSION -->` marker and inline body text. A separate `<!-- seeds-onboard-schema:N -->` marker drives outdated-snippet detection so patch releases don't mark every existing snippet as outdated; legacy `seeds-onboard-v:N` markers auto-upgrade on next run. `VERSION` extracted to `src/version.ts` so it can be imported without triggering `index.ts` CLI side-effects. (seeds-3da2)

### Fixed
- `sd plan submit`: `step.blocks=[j]` now correctly means "this step blocks step `j`" (matching the PLAN_SPEC.md natural-language example). Previously the indices were written into each child's `blockedBy`, inverting the chain so `sd ready` surfaced trailing steps first. Both fresh-submit and overwrite paths now wire bidirectional edges (`source.blocks += target`, `target.blockedBy += source`) with dedupe; overwrite handles matched-source as well as matched-target, fixing a pre-existing case where edges added in a revision didn't update existing children. Inverted plans submitted before this fix are not auto-corrected (tracked separately in seeds-1c38). (seeds-4a54)
- `sd plan show` no longer `JSON.stringify`s structured list entries into the user-facing review surface for `steps` and `alternatives`. Dispatch on the section spec: `kind=steps` formats step titles with indented `blocks`/`requires_plan`/`plan_template` sub-lines, `kind=list` with an object item schema renders each named field per line, and plans whose template is no longer registered fall back to a JSON dump rather than crash. (seeds-7d17)
- `sd show <child-seed>`: the plan block now labels the step list "Plan steps" rather than "Children (N)" — the list is the seed's siblings, not its descendants. `sd plan show` keeps "Children" since the heading is correct from the plan's perspective. (seeds-b2d7)

## [0.4.0] - 2026-05-06

### Added
- `sd plan` command tree — structured planning facilitation that decomposes a seed into child seeds via an LLM-driven walkthrough. Designed for work that's large or ambiguous enough to benefit from upfront decomposition; for small, well-scoped tasks just `sd create` directly. Full design in [PLAN_SPEC.md](/docs/components-missions-plan-spec).
  - `sd plan templates` — list available plan templates
  - `sd plan prompt <seed-id> [--template <name>] [--domain <name>]` — emit structured `plan_request` JSON the LLM fills out; default template inferred from seed type. `instructions` and `--help` document the submit reply shape so the prompt → submit transformation is explicit. `prior_art` is enriched from mulch (`approach` ↔ pattern+decision, `risks` ↔ failure, `acceptance` ↔ guide) when mulch is on PATH.
  - `sd plan submit <seed-id> --plan <file|->` — validate via AJV + structural `steps[].blocks` index check, spawn one child seed per step with `blockedBy` id remap, append the plan row to `.seeds/plans.jsonl`, and update the parent seed (`plan_id` back-pointer + `blockedBy = [children]`). `-` reads from stdin. Validation failures emit a partial-state diff JSON to stderr. `--overwrite` replaces an existing non-draft plan, matches steps by title, preserves child IDs, and prints obsolete-child close suggestions to stderr (never auto-closes). `--record-decision` writes the approach to mulch as a decision record after success (best-effort, never rolls back the plan). `--domain` forces the mulch domain.
  - `sd plan show <pl-id>` — display sections, child summaries, status, and a "review suggested" hint when status is `approved`/`active` and no reviewer is recorded. Recurses through nested sub-plans up to `max_plan_depth` (default 3, configurable).
  - `sd plan list [--seed --status --outcome --template]` — query plans with combinable filters; default sort `createdAt` desc.
  - `sd plan validate <pl-id>` — re-run validation against the current template definition.
  - `sd plan outcome <pl-id> --result success|partial|failure [--note <text>]` — record a plan outcome (storage-only; never gates child progress).
  - `sd plan review <pl-id> --by <name>` — record a reviewer (informational; not a state transition).
- **Config-driven plan templates.** Custom templates under `plan_templates:` in `.seeds/config.yaml` override the built-ins. Built-in templates: `feature` (default for `task`/`feature`/`epic`; sections: `context`, `approach`, `alternatives`, `steps`, `risks`, `acceptance`), `bug` (default for `bug`; adds `reproduction`, `root_cause`), `refactor` (opt-in via `--template refactor`; adds `behavior_invariant`).
- **Plan lifecycle auto-transitions.** `draft` → `approved` → `active` → `done` driven by child seed status changes (hooked from `update.ts` and `close.ts` under outer plans-lock + inner issues-lock); `done` → `active` reopen path supported. `Plan.revision` increments on `--overwrite`.
- **Nested sub-plans.** A template step can declare `plan_template: <name>` to spawn a child seed that requires its own sub-plan. The child gets `requires_plan: true` and is hidden from `sd ready` until its plan reaches `approved+`. `sd plan prompt` on the spawned child inherits the parent step's `plan_template` unless `--template` overrides. Submit-time validation rejects unknown `plan_template` names.
- `Plan` type and plan storage layer (`readPlans`/`writePlans`/`appendPlan`/`plansPath`) mirroring the issue/template helpers and lock model. `.seeds/plans.jsonl` is created on `sd init` and added to `.gitattributes` with `merge=union`.
- `Issue.plan_id`, `Issue.plan_step_index`, `Issue.requires_plan` (additive optional fields; existing rows remain valid).
- Plan-awareness in `sd ready`, `sd show`, and `sd list`: ready surfaces seeds whose plan is in `draft` even if otherwise blocked, and excludes seeds with `requires_plan` until their sub-plan is approved+; show inlines child seeds for approved/active/done plans; list adds a `[plan <status>]` indicator. `--json` parity (`plan_status`, `plan_children`).
- `src/validation.ts` AJV-based validation foundation (sole AJV-importing module): `compileSchema` returns a `ValidatorFn`; `formatErrors` maps AJV `ErrorObject` to the documented `PartialStateDiff` shape.
- Extended in-tree YAML parser (`src/yaml.ts`) supporting nested maps, block sequences, inline flow maps/seqs, and typed scalars — keeps the minimal-runtime-deps posture (no new YAML dep).
- `sd onboard` snippet refresh — added `sd search`, the global `--format` flag, and the full `sd plan` surface (templates, prompt, submit, show, validate, list, outcome, review). Snippet version bumped to `v:3` so existing CLAUDE.md installs auto-update via the marker.
- `sd prime` includes plan-aware quick reference.

### Fixed
- `sd list` / `sd ready` / `sd blocked` / `sd show` (compact) / `sd search` / `sd dep` / `sd tpl` no longer render `[blocked]` when all of an issue's blockers are closed. Formatters now accept an optional `closedBlockerIds` set; callers compute it once from the unfiltered issue list and thread it through.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-05-04

### Added
- `sd search <query>` command — case-insensitive substring search on issue title + description, with the same filters as `sd list` (`--status`, `--type`, `--assignee`, `--label`, `--label-any`, `--unlabeled`, `--priority`, `--priority-max`) and shared `--limit`/`--sort`/`--format`/`--json` output flags. Includes closed issues by default; pass `--status open` to restrict.
- `--sort <mode>` flag on `sd list` and `sd ready` (`priority|created|updated|id`)
- `--format <mode>` flag on `sd list`, `sd ready`, `sd show`, `sd blocked`, and `sd stats` (`markdown|compact|plain|ids|json`). `--json` is preserved as an alias for `--format json`. The `ids` mode emits issue IDs one per line for shell pipelines: `sd list --label bug --format ids | xargs sd close`.
- `sd ready` now accepts the same filters as `sd list`: `--type`, `--assignee`, `--label`, `--label-any`, `--unlabeled`, `--limit`. Shared filter logic lives in `src/filter.ts`.
- `--priority <levels>` and `--priority-max <n>` filters on `sd list` and `sd ready`. `--priority` matches an exact comma-separated set (e.g. `--priority 0,1` or `--priority P0,P1`); `--priority-max` keeps issues at or below a ceiling (e.g. `--priority-max 1` = P0+P1). Both accept numeric (0-4) and P-prefixed (P0-P4) forms consistent with `sd create` / `sd update`.
- `--body` as alias for `--description` on `sd create` and `sd update`

### Changed
- `sd list` and `sd ready` now sort by priority ascending (P0 first) by default, tie-broken by `createdAt` desc, instead of JSONL file order
- Tightened lint and typecheck strictness (Biome `noNonNullAssertion=error`)

### Fixed
- `isInsideWorktree` submodule false positive — now compares resolved git-dir vs git-common-dir instead of path heuristics
- `process.exit()` replaced with `process.exitCode` in version-json handler

## [0.2.5] - 2026-03-04

### Added
- `sd block <id> --by <blocker-id>` command — mark an issue as blocked by another
- `sd unblock <id> --from <blocker-id>` command — remove a specific blocker (`--all` to clear all)
- `sd label` subcommand group — `add`, `remove`, `list`, `list-all` for issue labels
- Labels field on issues — optional `string[]` for categorization and filtering
- `sd list --label <label>` filter — list issues by label
- `--all` flag on `sd list` — show all issues including closed (default now filters to open/in_progress)

### Changed
- `sd list` now defaults to showing only open and in_progress issues (use `--all` for previous behavior)

## [0.2.4] - 2026-02-25

### Added
- `sd completions <shell>` command — output shell completion scripts for bash, zsh, and fish
- `--timing` global flag — show command execution time on stderr
- Typo suggestion tests for misspelled command names
- Tests for `--timing` flag and shell completions

### Fixed
- `sd init` now derives project name from directory name instead of hardcoding "seeds"

## [0.2.3] - 2026-02-24

### Added
- Worktree root resolution — `findSeedsDir()` resolves to the main repo's `.seeds/` when running inside a git worktree
- `isInsideWorktree()` helper in `config.ts` for worktree detection
- Worktree guard in `sd sync` — skips commit with warning when running from a worktree (supports `--json`)
- Tests for worktree resolution (`config.test.ts`) and sync worktree guard (`sync.test.ts`)
- Custom branded help formatting for `sd --help` — colored commands, aligned options, branded header

### Changed
- Lock retry interval increased from 50ms to 100ms with random jitter to reduce contention
- Lock timeout increased from 5s to 30s for better multi-agent reliability

## [0.2.2] - 2026-02-24

### Added
- `sd upgrade` command — check for and install latest version from npm (`--check` for version check only)
- `--quiet` / `-q` global flag — suppress non-error output
- `--verbose` global flag — extra diagnostic output
- `--dry-run` flag on `sd sync` — preview what would be committed without committing
- `printWarning()` helper in `output.ts`

### Changed
- Applied os-eco forest branding palette: `brand` (green), `accent` (amber), `muted` (gray) replace raw chalk colors across all commands
- Status icons updated to ASCII-safe set: `✓` (pass), `!` (warn), `✗` (fail), `>` (in-progress), `-` (open), `x` (closed)
- Version flag changed from `-V` to `-v` (standard convention)
- `--version --json` now returns structured `{name, version, runtime, platform}` object
- npm publish workflow: switched from `--provenance` to token-based auth via `NPM_TOKEN` secret

## [0.2.1] - 2026-02-24

### Changed
- Migrated CLI parsing from manual switch/case to Commander.js — proper subcommands, built-in help, and option validation
- Replaced manual ANSI escape codes with chalk for output formatting
- Use `process.exitCode = 1` instead of `process.exit(1)` for graceful shutdown
- Replaced auto-tag workflow with unified publish workflow for npm

### Fixed
- `--desc` flag silently dropped descriptions in `create` and `update` commands

### Added
- chalk and commander as runtime dependencies
- `--desc` as explicit alias for `--description` in `create` and `update`

### Removed
- `.beads/` directory — seeds is now the sole issue tracker
- Manual ANSI color helpers (`c.red`, `c.green`, etc.) in `output.ts`

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-23

### Added
- `sd doctor` command — validates project health: config, JSONL integrity, field validation, dependency consistency, stale locks, gitattributes, and `.gitignore`. Supports `--fix` for auto-fixable issues
- `sd prime` command — outputs AI agent context (PRIME.md or built-in reference). Supports `--compact` for condensed output
- `sd onboard` command — adds seeds section to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with marker-delimited sections for idempotent updates
- `src/markers.ts` utility for marker-delimited section management (used by `onboard`)
- CODEOWNERS file for branch protection

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-23

### Added
- Initial release
- Issue CRUD: `sd create`, `sd show`, `sd list`, `sd update`, `sd close`
- Dependency tracking: `sd dep add/remove/list`, `sd blocked`, `sd ready`
- Templates/molecules: `sd tpl create/step/list/show/pour/status`
- Advisory file locking for concurrent multi-agent access
- Atomic writes (temp file + rename) with dedup-on-read
- YAML config (`config.yaml`), JSONL storage (`issues.jsonl`, `templates.jsonl`)
- `--json` flag on all commands for structured output
- Migration from beads: `sd migrate-from-beads`
- `sd sync` to stage and commit `.seeds/` changes
- `sd stats` for project statistics
- Zero runtime dependencies — Bun built-ins only
- `merge=union` gitattribute for git-native parallel branch merges

text:
# Contributing to Missions

Thanks for your interest in contributing to Missions! This guide covers everything you need to get started.

## Getting Started

1. **Fork** the repository on GitHub
2. **Clone** your fork locally:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/missions.git
   cd missions
   ```
3. **Install** dependencies:
   ```bash
   bun install
   ```
4. **Create a branch** for your work:
   ```bash
   git checkout -b fix/description-of-change
   ```

## Branch Naming

Use descriptive branch names with a category prefix:

- `fix/` -- Bug fixes
- `feat/` -- New features
- `docs/` -- Documentation changes
- `refactor/` -- Code refactoring
- `test/` -- Test additions or fixes

## Build & Test Commands

```bash
bun test              # Run all tests
bun run lint          # Biome check
bun run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
```

Always run all three before submitting a PR.

## Coding Conventions

- **Tab indentation** (enforced by Biome)
- **100 character line width** (enforced by Biome)
- Strict TypeScript with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` — always handle possible `undefined`
- No `any` — use `unknown` and narrow, or define proper types
- All imports use `.ts` extensions
- Minimal runtime dependencies (chalk + commander only)
- Tests use real filesystems (temp dirs via `mkdtemp`), never mocks

## Testing

- **Framework:** `bun test` (built-in, Jest-compatible API)
- Tests colocated with source: `src/foo.test.ts` next to `src/foo.ts`
- Use real I/O with temp directories, no mocks

## Pull Request Expectations

- **One concern per PR.** Keep changes focused.
- **Tests required.** New features and bug fixes should include tests.
- **Passing CI.** All PRs must pass CI checks before merge.
- **Description.** Briefly explain what and why. Link relevant issues.

## Reporting Issues

Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions/issues) for bug reports and feature requests. For security vulnerabilities, see [SECURITY.md](/docs/components-missions-security).

By contributing, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the [MIT License](/docs/components-missions-license).

# Missions: git-native tickets and work plans

Missions is Luuna's maintained, MIT-licensed fork of Seeds. It provides local, Git-native tickets, dependencies, structured plans, and reusable work templates. Its package identity is `@luuna/missions-cli`; run it as `luuna-missions` or the short alias `lm`. The legacy `sd` and `seeds` aliases remain for existing integrations.

## Records and workflow

Missions stores project work in `.seeds/` and preserves the upstream configuration, JSONL records, markers, and environment variables. Issues carry intent and acceptance criteria; dependencies describe ordering; reusable templates can create structured plans and coordinated work. Review the current [Missions specification](/docs/components-missions-spec) for the data model, CLI, JSON output, concurrency behavior, and migration details.

The core runtime may call Missions through the CLI/JSON boundary. It becomes the ticket authority only after explicit activation. Merely installing it does not change how Luuna records work. Runtime approval, candidate identity, validation, and publication policy remain in Luuna.

## Run from source

Use the repository's documented Bun 1.4.3 toolchain:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
bun src/index.ts --help
bun run verify
```

Start with the [Missions README](/docs/components-missions-readme), then use the [specification](/docs/components-missions-spec) for the command and record details. Review the [migration guide](/docs/components-missions-migration) before moving existing Seeds data. The fork keeps `.seeds/` data compatible and does not silently rewrite it.

## Maintenance and provenance

Missions is consumed by Luuna at a reviewed Git submodule commit from [`luuna-ai/luuna-missions`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions). In the core Luuna source snapshot documented here, the integration pin is [`e1b5db1`](https://github.com/luuna-ai/luuna-missions/tree/e1b5db171892de653e7462e630d64d4964d01422); the reference pages below follow a newer component-repository head. Check the pin before relying on newer behavior in core Luuna. Its npm package remains private and unpublished. The original Seeds documentation is retained as attributed historical reference. Follow the component's current changelog and migration notes when upgrading; do not assume a floating branch or registry version is the version used by Luuna.

# Luuna Missions CLI and system map

This is the command, tooling, data, and integration map of the maintained Missions fork. The live CLI implementation is Go: `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go` registers the built-in commands in `internal/cli/` and the plan family in `internal/plan/`. `src/index.ts` is a Bun launcher for the existing package and Luuna entrypoints. `src/index-legacy.ts` plus the TypeScript modules under `src/` remain a differential behavior oracle. This map describes write and Git side effects; reading it does not authorize running those commands in a user's project.

## Place in Luuna

Missions owns Git-native tickets and structured plans. Atlas owns structured expertise and project memory, and Beacon owns reusable prompts. The Luuna runtime owns policy, permissions, and approval enforcement. Missions is a separate public repository consumed by Luuna at an exact submodule commit; it communicates with Luuna through command-line arguments, exit codes, JSON output, and `.luuna/missions/` data. A Missions change does not alter the consuming Luuna checkout until that pin and installer are updated in a separate reviewed integration.

```text
user / agent / Luuna launcher (`luuna missions`)
                  |
                  v
  package bin: luuna-missions / lms / lm / missions
                  |
                  v
   Bun compatibility launcher (`src/index.ts`)
                  |
       cached Go executable (`cmd/luuna-missions`)
                  |
        +---------+---------+------------------+
        |                   |                  |
  issues + dependencies   plans + templates  config + tooling
        |                   |                  |
        +-------------------+------------------+
                            |
                   .luuna/missions/ (Git files)
                            |
         optional: luuna-atlas query/record; Claude hooks; Git
```

The package is `@luuna/missions-cli` version 0.6.0 and remains private and unpublished. Its bin entries are `luuna-missions`, `lms`, `lm`, and `missions`, all pointing to `src/index.ts`. The consuming Luuna `components/manifest.json` still pins that Bun path, and its Windows installer writes Bun launchers. These files live in the parent repository. The shim makes that path dispatch to the Go implementation in this checkout; changing this repository alone does not move Luuna's exact submodule pin.

## Runtime, build, and test tooling

The Bun launcher calls `scripts/native-build.ts`, which hashes the package version, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and all files under `cmd/` and `internal/`, including embedded help, completion, schema, and prompt assets. It builds a matching binary once with `go build -trimpath` and injects the package version into `internal/cli.CurrentVersion`. The binary is stored under ignored `dist/<platform>-<architecture>/<digest>/` and is reused for that source revision. The launcher passes CLI arguments, standard streams, signals, working directory, and exit status to the child. Direct native execution needs no Bun after the binary is built.

| Tool or entry | Role | Requirement / output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/index.ts` | Compatibility entry for package bins and Luuna's existing pin | Bun 1.4.3; builds native binary on a cache miss |
| `scripts/native-build.ts` / `bun run build:native` | Source-keyed native build | Go 1.22+ on `PATH`, or `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` set to its executable; writes ignored `dist/` |
| `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go` | Native entry and command registration | Direct `go run ./cmd/luuna-missions <args>` or compiled binary |
| `internal/cli`, `internal/plan` | Parser, commands, plan lifecycle, help and completion text | Go runtime implementation; `internal/plan` registers through `cli.App` |
| `internal/model`, `internal/store`, `internal/config` | Wire records, JSONL/locking/atomic persistence, YAML schema/discovery/migration | Preserve existing project files and public JSON keys |
| `src/index-legacy.ts`, `src/register-all.ts`, `src/commands/` | Previous TypeScript command implementation | Oracle for command parity; not the package bin implementation |
| `scripts/parity.mjs` | Differential CLI corpus in isolated temporary Git projects | Compares Go and TypeScript exit codes, stdout/stderr, JSON values, ordered JSONL records, and non-JSON files |
| `scripts/verify-native.ts` / `bun run verify` | Run Go tests, build native, then run all parity suites after Bun checks | `verify` also runs type checking, instruction checks, and Bun tests |

The Go CLI embeds help snapshots, shell completions, and some `prime` content derived from the TypeScript oracle. Changes to those public strings require updating the Go fixtures and parity cases. `--version --json` deliberately retains `runtime: "bun"` and Node/Bun-style platform names as a wire-compatibility label, even when Go runs directly. `LUUNA_MISSIONS_DEBUG=1` enables a separate diagnostic JSON line on stdout for top-level errors unless a valid `LUUNA_MISSIONS_LOG_LEVEL` overrides it; leave it off when consuming a single JSON response. Go diagnostic stack text is a summary rather than a byte-for-byte Bun stack.

## Project data and invariants

`init` creates `.luuna/missions/config.yaml`, `issues.jsonl`, `plans.jsonl`, `templates.jsonl`, and a local `.gitignore` for `*.lock`. It adds three `merge=union` lines for the JSONL files to the project's `.gitattributes`. Commands discover the nearest initialized project by walking up from the current directory; a linked Git worktree resolves its main checkout's store. The first access to a legacy `.seeds/` layout may move it to `.luuna/missions/` through `internal/config/legacy.go` and rewrite relevant `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` references. That migration refuses to merge two stores or follow a linked old/new directory; `src/legacy-layout.ts` is the reference implementation.

| File | Record or purpose | Main owners |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issues.jsonl` | One issue per line: ID, title, status, type, priority, optional assignee/description/labels/dependencies/plan links/intent/extensions, timestamps | `create`, `update`, `close`, `dep`, `label`, `block`, `unblock`, template pour, plan child operations, Beads migration |
| `plans.jsonl` | Plan ID, parent seed, template, status, revision, sections, ordered children, adopted-child subset, optional outcome/reviewer, timestamps | `plan` family; child status transitions from `update` and `close` |
| `templates.jsonl` | Named issue template with ordered steps; pouring creates a convoy of issues | `tpl` family |
| `config.yaml` | Project name, schema version, nested plan display depth, optional custom plan templates | `init`, `config`, plan validation and prompts |

An issue has required `id`, `title`, `status`, `type`, `priority`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. Optional fields are `assignee`, `description`, `closeReason`, `closedAt`, `blocks`, `blockedBy`, `labels`, `convoy`, `plan_id`, `plan_step_index`, `requires_plan`, `discoveredFrom`, Roots `intent`, and `extensions`. Status is `open`, `in_progress`, or `closed`; type is `task`, `bug`, `feature`, or `epic`; priority is 0 (critical) through 4 (backlog). `blocks` and `blockedBy` are reciprocal issue ID relationships. `discoveredFrom` is provenance, not a blocker. Unknown record fields are preserved. A plan stores `id`, parent `seed`, `template`, `name`, lifecycle `status`, `revision`, validated `sections`, ordered `children`, optional `adoptedChildren`, `outcome`, `outcomeNote`, `reviewedBy`, and timestamps. A template stores `id`, `name`, and ordered `steps`; each step has a title and optional type, priority, and `plan_template`. Config has `project`, `version`, optional `max_plan_depth`, and optional `plan_templates`; `config schema` emits the full JSON Schema.

Writes use advisory per-file `.lock` files, atomic replacement, and JSONL deduplication by ID. Multi-file plan operations acquire the plans lock before the issues lock. JSONL is meant to be mutated through commands, not by hand. IDs, timestamps, human output, JSON field names, and exit behavior are command contracts.

Plan status starts at `approved` after submission or adopt-only creation. A child entering progress makes the plan `active`; all children closed makes it `done`; reopening a child returns it to `active`. A `draft` stays draft, and `outcome` records an assessment without changing status. `plan show` can recurse into child plans up to `max_plan_depth` (default 3). Built-in plan templates are `feature`, `bug`, and `refactor`; custom templates in YAML may override them.

## Full command inventory

Options in the table are command-specific. `--json` is available on most data and mutation commands and yields a stable object with `success` and `command`; list/show/ready/search/blocked/stats also support `--format markdown|compact|plain|ids|json`. `--format` is not a universal option. Top-level flags are `-h/--help`, `-v/--version`, `-q/--quiet` (suppress human status output), `--verbose` (extra diagnostics where supported), and `--timing` (elapsed time on stderr after success); `--version --json` emits version metadata. A command failure returns a nonzero exit and either a JSON error object in JSON mode or an `Error:` line on stderr. Run `<command> --help` (and `<command> <subcommand> --help`) for exact argument ordering and option text.

| Environment variable | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `LUUNA_MISSIONS_GO` | Go executable used by the Bun native builder and native verification script; defaults to `go` on `PATH` |
| `LUUNA_MISSIONS_DEBUG=1` | Enables debug records for top-level command errors unless a valid explicit log level takes precedence |
| `LUUNA_MISSIONS_LOG_LEVEL` | `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`, or `silent`; controls those error diagnostics |
| `USER` | Default identity for `update <id> --claim` if `--as` is omitted |

| Command | Use and notable options | Writes / side effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `init` | Initialize current project; `--json` | Creates data files and updates `.gitattributes` |
| `create` | Add a ticket; required `--title`; `--type task|bug|feature|epic` (default task), `--priority 0..4` or `P0..P4` (default 2), `--assignee`, `--description`/`--desc`/`--body`, comma-separated `--labels`, `--from`, repeatable `--intent`, `--json` | Appends issue |
| `show <id> [ids...]` | Inspect one or more issues (and linked plan details); `--format`, `--json` | Read only |
| `list` | List/filter issues; `--status`, `--type`, `--assignee`, `--all` (include closed), `--label` (all), `--label-any`, `--unlabeled`, `--priority`, `--priority-max`, `--limit` (default 50), `--sort priority|created|updated|id`, `--format`/`--json` | Read only |
| `ready` | Unblocked open work; the type/assignee/label/priority/limit/sort/format filters from `list`; `--respect-schedule` excludes queued or future scheduled extensions | Read only |
| `search <query>` | Case-insensitive title/description search; status/type/assignee/label/priority/limit/sort/format filters from `list`, without `--all` | Read only |
| `update <id>` | `--status`, `--title`, `--assignee`, `--description`/`--desc`/`--body`, `--type`, `--priority`, `--add-label`, `--remove-label`, `--set-labels`, `--extensions <json>` (shallow merge), `--clear-extensions`, repeatable replacing `--intent`, `--json`; `--claim --as <agent>` atomically claims open work (`USER` fallback) | Rewrites issue; status may transition parent plan |
| `close <id> [ids...]` | Close one or more issues; optional `--reason`, `--json` | Rewrites issues; may transition parent plan |
| `dep add <issue> <depends-on>` | Add reciprocal dependency links; `--json` | Rewrites issues |
| `dep remove <issue> <depends-on>` | Remove reciprocal dependency links; `--json` | Rewrites issues |
| `dep list <issue>` | Show dependencies; `--json` | Read only |
| `label add <issue> <labels...>` | Normalize and append one or more labels; `--json` | Rewrites issue |
| `label remove <issue> <labels...>` | Remove one or more labels; `--json` | Rewrites issue |
| `label list <issue>` | Show labels on one issue; `--json` | Read only |
| `label list-all` | Show labels across issues; `--json` | Read only |
| `blocked` | List blocked issues; `--format`, `--json` | Read only |
| `stats` | Aggregate project issue counts; `--format`, `--json` | Read only |
| `sync` | `--status` inspects changes, `--dry-run` previews, `--json`; default stages `.luuna/missions/` and runs `git commit`; skips commit from a Git worktree | Default commits the current index, including unrelated paths already staged |
| `doctor` | Check config, issue/template JSONL integrity and duplicates, issue schema, dependencies, labels, extensions, closed metadata, locks, and Git attributes; `--fix`, `--verbose`, `--json` | `--fix` may remove malformed JSONL lines, repair issue/template records and `.gitattributes`, and remove stale locks |
| `tpl create` | Create an issue template; required `--name`, optional `--json` | Appends template |
| `tpl step add <id>` | Add ordered template step; required `--title`, optional `--type`/`--priority`, `--json` | Rewrites template |
| `tpl list` | List issue templates; `--json` | Read only |
| `tpl show <id>` | Inspect one issue template; `--json` | Read only |
| `tpl pour <id>` | Instantiate template steps as linked issues; required `--prefix`, optional `--json` | Creates issues/convoy |
| `tpl status <id>` | Inspect convoy status; `--json` | Read only |
| `migrate-from-beads` | Import `.beads/issues.jsonl` and skip already-present IDs; `--json` | Adds issues |
| `prime` | Emit agent workflow context and live work state; `--compact`, `--export`, `--json` | Read only |
| `onboard` | Add/update a marked Missions snippet in `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or `AGENTS.md`; `--check`, `--stdout`, `--json` | Default edits one guidance file |
| `upgrade` | `--check`, `--json`; self-upgrade is disabled while unpublished and returns an unavailable error | No registry update |
| `completions <shell>` | Print bash, zsh, or fish completion script | Read only |
| `block <id> --by <blocker-id>` | Add one blocker; `--json` | Rewrites issues |
| `unblock <id>` | `--from <blocker-id>` or `--all` closed blockers; `--json` | Rewrites issues |
| `plan` | Structured plan subcommands below | Depends on subcommand |
| `config schema` | Emit full config JSON Schema; `--json` selects compact one-line output (default pretty JSON) | Read only |
| `config show` | Show all YAML config or `--path <dot.path>`; `--json` | Read only |
| `config set <path> <value>` | YAML-parse and schema-validate the value; `--json` | Atomically writes `config.yaml` |
| `config unset <path>` | Remove a config field after validation; `--json` | Atomically writes `config.yaml` |
| `setup claude` | Install or `--remove` Missions-owned Claude hooks; `--json` | Edits `.claude/settings.json` |
| `guard` | Claude `PreToolUse` hook; reads JSON from stdin and denies supported direct edits to managed JSONL | No project write; hook decision on stdout |

### Plan subcommands

Every plan leaf accepts `--json`; commands that take `<id>` generally accept either a plan ID or its parent seed ID. The leaf help text remains the exact option and argument reference.

| Command | Use and important options | Writes / effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan templates` | List built-in plus configured plan templates | Read only |
| `plan prompt <seed-id>` | Emit a template-shaped planning request; `--template`, `--domain`; optional Atlas prior art | Read only; optional Atlas queries |
| `plan submit <seed-id>` | Validate plan JSON via required `--plan <file|->` (stdin with `-`); `--overwrite`, `--name`, `--record-decision`, `--domain` | Writes plan, parent and child issues; optional Atlas decision write after success |
| `plan show <id>` | Show plan by plan ID or seed ID with child summaries and nested plans | Read only |
| `plan validate <id>` | Recheck stored sections against current template; emits structured diff on stderr when invalid | Read only |
| `plan outcome <id>` | Required `--result success|partial|failure`, optional `--note`; warns about open children | Updates plan assessment only |
| `plan review <id>` | Required `--by <name>`; reviewer is informational | Updates plan |
| `plan edit <id>` | `--name`, text `--section <name> <text>`, or `--step <i>` with `--title`/`--priority`/`--type`; bumps revision and propagates step metadata | Rewrites plan and possibly child issue |
| `plan create <seed-id>` | Adopt-only approved plan with zero children; `--name`, `--template` | Writes plan and parent link |
| `plan adopt <plan-id> <seed-ids...>` | Attach existing open missions; optional `--step`, one of `--at`/`--before`/`--after` | Writes plan and issues; keeps seed status/type/priority |
| `plan reorder <plan-id> <seed-ids...>` | Require an exact permutation of existing children | Rewrites plan order only |
| `plan release <plan-id> <seed-ids...>` | Detach children without closing them | Rewrites plan and issues |
| `plan list` | Filter by `--seed`, `--status`, `--outcome`, `--template` | Read only |

The plan submission shape is `{ "template": "feature", "name": "optional label", "sections": { ... } }`. `plan prompt` wraps the form in a `plan_request` envelope; remove that envelope when submitting. Submit validates text/list/step shapes and step dependencies before writing. A step may spawn a child from `title` or adopt an existing child with `existing_seed`. `blocks` contains 1-based step indices, while stored `plan_step_index` is 0-based. Step `labels` are normalized and merged onto adopted children. Child descriptions carry a marked plan back-reference; releasing a child strips that marked block while preserving manual description text.

## Typical workflow and integrations

Run ticket commands from an initialized project, not from this component's own checkout. For example:

```bash
luuna-missions init
luuna-missions create --title "Add import validation" --type feature --priority P1 --json
luuna-missions ready --json
luuna-missions show <issue-id> --json
luuna-missions update <issue-id> --claim --as <agent> --json
luuna-missions close <issue-id> --reason "Verified" --json
```

1. `luuna-missions init` in a Git project, then `create --title ...` to capture work.
2. `ready --json` or `list --json` to select work. `update <id> --claim --as <agent>` claims it atomically; `close <id>` finishes it. Dependencies and plan drafts affect readiness.
3. For larger work, create a parent issue, run `plan prompt <id> --json`, fill the resulting plan template, then `plan submit <id> --plan plan.json --json`. Use `plan show`, `validate`, `edit`, `adopt`, `reorder`, `release`, `review`, and `outcome` as the work evolves.
4. `prime` emits context for agents. `setup claude` installs a SessionStart `luuna-missions prime --compact` hook and a PreToolUse `luuna-missions guard` hook with a `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` matcher. The guard reads Claude's hook JSON on stdin and emits a deny decision for direct edits to `.luuna/missions/*.jsonl`; other tools and targets pass through. `onboard` writes a marked Missions block in a project instruction file without owning the rest of that file.
5. `sync --status` or `sync --dry-run` shows Missions changes; plain `sync` stages Missions files and commits the current index. Run `git diff --cached --name-only` to inspect unrelated staged paths first. Luuna's policy and approval mechanism is outside this component.

Atlas enrichment is optional: `plan prompt` can query `luuna-atlas` for matching domain records; `plan submit --record-decision` may write an Atlas decision after the local plan is saved. Failures do not roll back the local plan. Beacon has no direct data store integration in this component. `migrate-from-beads` is an explicit import from a prior issue tracker; legacy `.seeds/` layout movement is a separate automatic compatibility path.

## Development and evidence boundaries

Supported component validation is `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` followed by `bun run verify`. That script runs `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:agents`, `bun test --timeout 30000`, `go test ./...`, a native build, and `scripts/parity.mjs --suite all --require-go`. The differential corpus runs the `smoke`, `core`, `relations`, `config`, `templates`, `misc`, and `plans` suites in temporary stores. It normalizes generated IDs, temporary paths, line endings, and timestamp milliseconds; it compares JSON semantically and ordered JSONL records by value while keeping human output, stderr, exit codes, and other files exact. The inherited `check:all` and quality-budget scripts compare against upstream maintenance and are not the supported CI contract. The GitHub workflow declares the supported `verify` surface on Linux and Windows with Bun 1.4.3 and Go from `go.mod`; a configured workflow is not proof of a completed run on every host or Go version.

For a focused differential run, use `bun scripts/parity.mjs --go <native-binary> --suite <name|all> --require-go`. The harness also accepts `--self-check` to compare the oracle with itself, `--keep` to retain its temporary fixtures, and `--oracle-entry <path>` or `MISSIONS_ORACLE_ENTRY` to select another TypeScript oracle. `MISSIONS_GO_BIN` and `MISSIONS_BUN_BIN` select executables; these `MISSIONS_*` variables configure the harness, not the public CLI. Never aim a parity run at an imported or live project store.

Current limits matter when operating or integrating this component:

- The package bins still require Bun, and a fresh checkout or package install needs a Go compiler for the first native build. No prebuilt binaries or registry release are shipped here. The cached native executable itself can run without Bun.
- The TypeScript oracle remains in the repository to check command behavior. The parity corpus covers representative success, failure, mutation, help, and output paths; it cannot prove every input or environment. Debug stack text differs from the Bun stack.
- `doctor` currently checks malformed and duplicate issue/template JSONL records; it does not perform the same integrity scan of `plans.jsonl`. `plan validate <id>` rechecks a stored plan against its current template, but is not a whole-store repair command.
- `setup claude` and `guard` cover the registered Claude hook and supported direct edit tool events. They are not Luuna runtime policy or a universal filesystem permission system. Atlas lookups and decision recording require an available `luuna-atlas` executable; Beacon has no direct store integration.
- Changes in this component do not update the consuming Luuna submodule or installer. An exact pin update, consumer smoke test, and any release or publication need a separate reviewed process. Do not load imported stores, session histories, or upstream skills as Luuna work records for validation.

Sources for this map: `cmd/luuna-missions/main.go`, `internal/cli/`, `internal/plan/`, `internal/model/`, `internal/store/`, `internal/config/`, `scripts/native-build.ts`, `scripts/verify-native.ts`, `scripts/parity.mjs`, `src/index.ts`, `src/index-legacy.ts`, `src/register-all.ts`, `src/types.ts`, `src/commands/`, `README.md`, `MIGRATION.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the consuming Luuna component manifest and Windows installer.
