# Ground-zero foundation status

Subsequent local performance follow-up (October 21, 2026): [ADR 0015](decisions/0015-bounded-runtime-and-history.md)
and [the performance review](PERFORMANCE-REVIEW.md) record bounded history,
blocking-work admission, check output/process ownership, optimized Windows
binaries and current-tree verification. The ordinary Windows workspace suite
passed 191 tests; all ten real-component opt-in tests passed separately, as did
the manual history benchmark and native Tauri unit test. Browser/native MVP
checks passed 57/55 respectively, and native component UI passed 27. Genuine
M1 passed 20 checks; a fresh Windows writer/repair/reviewer diagnostic passed 16.
An earlier diagnostic's model repair was correctly rejected by independent
review and remains recorded. After committing the performance changes and
fixing strict-harness Windows ownership and recursive dependency exclusions,
clean commit `974ff0e` passed strict M3: **68/68 fixture and 61/61 genuine
OpenRouter / openai/gpt-4.1 assertions**. See [commands, initial failures and
evidence limits](WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md#strict-m3-acceptance-result).
These are local commits and local acceptance, not remote CI or publication. The
installed Windows app/runtime were backed up and upgraded to release builds,
then passed 17 native startup checks with history and credentials preserved.

Current main-integration verification (October 21, 2026): all 46 initially local changed/new files were preserved and combined with PR 9's design system in [PR 10](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna/pull/10). Final Windows checks passed 185 Rust tests (10 explicit ignores), pinned Node/npm tests, typecheck/build, 27 native and 23 browser component assertions, and 55 native/57 browser lifecycle/presentation assertions. The subsequent Node 24 Windows scope-guard fix has final Rust and pinned guard-test evidence; the UI reports retain their earlier exact runtime identity. See [local accounting, failures and verification limits](MAIN-INTEGRATION-2026-10-21.md). Hosted Actions jobs could not start because of the account billing/spending limit.

The historical entries below retain their original scope and evidence. The current component runtime slice is recorded in [Runtime component workflows](#runtime-component-workflows-october-21-2026); extraction is covered separately by ADR 0012 and its evidence report.

Date: October 16, 2026, updated October 17, 2026 with the M1, M2a and M2b closure evidence below and October 21, 2026 with the re-validation gate, shutdown interruption and the desktop smoke. This records checks performed in the Linux cloud checkout, separately from the historical documentation validation report. No remote commit, package publication, signed installer, or GitHub CI result is implied.

## Audit actions

| Audit topic | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Committed sessions and authoring metadata | Archived privately outside the checkout, then removed 103 imported metadata files including 16 Pi sessions. Available reachable history scanned; see [security evidence](SECURITY-AUDIT-2026-10-16.md). Historical commits remain unchanged. |
| Component ownership and names | Maintained MIT distributions: Missions (Seeds), Atlas (Mulch), Beacon (Canopy). Independent package boundaries under `components/`, private until released; compatible storage formats and legacy CLI aliases preserved. The owner explicitly chose to keep everything in `brodynelly/luuna` and defer separation; see ADR 0002. |
| Authoritative specification | Current architecture, five ADRs, root agent/contributor instructions, rewritten README and handoff. Original proposals remain historical. |
| Root infrastructure | MIT license, upstream notices, ignore/editor settings, pinned Rust/Node tools, Cargo/npm/Bun locks, cross-platform Rust and native desktop CI jobs. |
| M0 contracts | Six missing schemas completed. Exact plan hash/revision/permissions, workflow/project binding, immutable storage, invalid transitions, stale approvals and candidate review guards tested. Feature execution fails closed pending real baseline evidence. |
| M1 engine/API | Real pinned Pi process/version/RPC probe; authenticated loopback API; durable run events/replay/SSE; owned cancellation, timeout/reap, malformed/error handling, exclusive state-directory ownership and restart recovery. Genuine provider execution verified on October 17, 2026 through OpenRouter (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`, 19/19 smoke checks); see the M1 closure section. |
| Desktop | Functional React client plus minimal Tauri shell, shared typed API client, run/cancel/reconnect/history. Browser tested against the actual service, including a genuine streamed model response, in-flight cancel and reload/replay on October 17, 2026. Native GUI not launched on this host. |

## Commands and observed outcomes

| Check | Observed outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `bash scripts/setup-cloud.sh` | Passed: reviewed Pi graph installed from tracked lock, Rust/Bun/npm prerequisites installed, frozen component dependencies and Rust workspace build completed. |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | Passed. |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace` | Passed: 33 tests (10 domain, 8 SQLite storage, 5 engine units, 2 engine supervision, 8 runtime API). No ignored tests. Zero-test binary/doc-test targets are not counted. |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed. |
| `npm test` | Passed: 18 positive/negative checks across 9 JSON schemas and 10 API-client tests. |
| `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` | Passed. |
| `npm audit` | Zero reported advisories in the root frontend dependency graph at check time. The separately locked Pi dependency graph also reported zero. This is not a complete dependency security audit. |
| `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs`, `git diff --check` | Passed. |
| Genuine Pi Rust probe | Passed against `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.3.0`: version check, `get_state`, `get_available_models`, `abort`, stopped/reaped subprocess. No provider call required. |
| Actual HTTP service | Authentication rejection, actual Pi missing-credential failure, ordered persisted events and cursor replay passed. The updated runtime was stopped/restarted; previous failed/cancelled runs and ordered events survived. |
| Actual Chromium UI/service smoke | Connected with private token, created/cancelled real process attempt, observed durable cancellation, cleared token on disconnect, restored identical unique events on reconnect. A second run displayed the genuine missing-provider-credential failure. No token persisted to browser storage and no page exceptions. Desktop/mobile viewport checks passed. |

Component verification:

| Component | Observed outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Luuna Missions | Typecheck and agent-documentation checks passed; full suite 1,053 passed, zero failed. |
| Luuna Atlas | Typecheck and agent-documentation checks passed; isolated full suite 1,580 passed, zero failed across 84 files. Earlier contention-affected run was interrupted and is not counted as a passing run. |
| Luuna Beacon | Typecheck and agent-documentation checks passed; final isolated full suite 459 passed, zero failed across 36 files after the lock fix. |

All 3,092 component tests passed in the final isolated runs. All three components passed frozen-lock installations and retained upstream license bytes. Component tests use actual temporary files, Git fixtures and CLI subprocesses; they are independent of the synthetic Pi corpus.

The initial Beacon suite exposed a lock-contention defect. Schema validator compilation now occurs before lock acquisition, while config read/mutation/validation/atomic write remain inside the lock. Its existing concurrent-writer test and all 31 config cases passed across full-file and targeted runs. The final isolated full Beacon suite then passed all 459 tests. Earlier contention failures were retained as diagnostic evidence and were not counted as passing.

The final independent audit found that missing required fields in known Pi completion records could permit a false success. The parser now validates pinned protocol completion fields. Regression tests prove malformed completion after prompt acceptance persists a failed run, even if a later record claims settlement. The final engine/runtime tests, full Rust suite, formatting and strict Clippy passed with this correction.

## M1 closure attempt, later on October 16, 2026

A second cloud session attempted the handoff's next assignment, closing genuine M1, on a fresh container at revision `65056e3` plus the changes recorded here. Pinned tools were reproduced and verified: Rust 1.90.0, Node 24.19.0, npm 11.9.0, Bun 1.4.3, Pi 1.3.0, Python 3.13. `scripts/setup-cloud.sh` initially failed because `rustup toolchain install` attempted a self-update against the relocated `CARGO_HOME`; the script now passes `--no-self-update` and completed on the second run.

**Result: M1 is not closed.** No provider credential was present in the environment (checked by variable name only: none of the eight supported `*_API_KEY` names or their `LUUNA_PI_` aliases existed), Pi's own `auth check --provider anthropic` in an isolated config reported `credentials_not_configured`, and `pi --list-models` showed no available models. Every genuine Pi request through the runtime therefore failed closed with Pi's `No API key found for anthropic` prompt rejection. That is failure-path evidence only.

| Check | Observed outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed before and after the changes below. |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace` | Passed: 35 tests (10 domain, 8 storage, 5 engine unit, 2 engine supervision, 10 runtime API). Two runtime API tests are new. |
| `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs`, `git diff --check` | Passed: 18 schema checks, 10 API-client tests, type/build and hygiene. |
| `cargo run --locked -p luuna-engine-pi --example probe` against the installed Pi 1.3.0 | Passed: version, `get_state`, `get_available_models`, `abort`, stopped/reaped. No provider call. |
| `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode fixture` (new harness, synthetic fixture) | 18/18 checks passed: auth rejection, SSE stream of 12 sequential events closing at terminal, `agent_settled` before `run.completed`, cursor replay identity, in-flight cancellation with the recorded child PID alive before and reaped after, idempotent cancel, provider failure persisted as failed, SIGKILL of the runtime followed by fixture child exit within 1.4 s, restart marking the abandoned attempt `interrupted`, three earlier histories identical by event ID, second runtime refused the owned data directory, SIGTERM orderly shutdown with exit 0. Synthetic: not provider evidence. |
| `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider anthropic --model claude-sonnet-4-5` (genuine Pi, no key) | 11/19 checks passed; all 8 failures trace to the missing credential. Pi resolved the model (`anthropic-messages`, `https://api.anthropic.com`), then rejected the prompt. Genuine Pi children exited within 1 ms of the runtime being hard-killed. Restart recovery and ownership checks passed. Runs `1cac2e38…`, `09452b8d…`, `4e43e8ac…`, `0577e5a2…` each persisted 6 events ending in `run.failed`. |
| Chromium browser smoke of the Vite UI (Playwright, not committed) | 11/11 checks passed against a fixture runtime on port 4243 and a genuine Pi runtime on port 4242: connect with token, fixture completion displaying the recorded Pi text, cancel from the UI yielding `run.cancelled` without `run.completed`, reload clearing the in-memory token with empty browser storage, reconnect restoring durable history and identical ordered event replay, and the genuine no-credential run displayed as failed with Pi's reason and no response text. No page exceptions. |
| `cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` | Failed as expected on this headless host: `gdk-3.0` is not in the pkg-config search path (WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3 are absent). Native desktop validation remains unverified and must run on a capable Mac/Windows/Linux-desktop host. |
| Network reachability (names only) | `api.anthropic.com` is reachable directly from this container because the platform lists it in the proxy's bypass set; `api.openai.com` is refused by the agent proxy (HTTP 421). An Anthropic key is therefore the shortest path to M1 on this platform; an OpenAI key additionally needs `api.openai.com` allowed in the environment's network settings. |

Changes made in this attempt, all covered by the checks above:

- `scripts/m1-smoke.mjs`: reproducible M1 smoke harness producing sanitized `report.md`/`report.json` (no token or credential values). Real mode is the intended M1 evidence path once a credential exists; fixture mode validates the harness itself.
- Runtime records a `pi.spawned` event per attempt with the owned child's PID, Pi version and the names of provider credentials forwarded, enabling reap verification after the terminal event. A new test proves the fixture child is alive before cancel and gone before `run.cancelled` persists.
- Provider key aliases are generalized: `LUUNA_PI_<NAME>` maps to each supported `<NAME>` inside the isolated child, with alias precedence and no pass-through of the alias itself. A new test proves alias and direct names reach the child by standard name only and that no values are persisted.
- On Unix the runtime treats `SIGTERM` like Ctrl+C: orderly shutdown stops owned workers and persists interruption. Verified by the harness (exit 0 within about 50 ms when idle).
- `scripts/setup-cloud.sh` uses `rustup ... --no-self-update`.

No repository-writing feature was enabled; the storage guard that blocks `Implementing` without baseline evidence is unchanged. Missions, Atlas and Beacon were not modified and their suites were not rerun (unchanged code; CI runs them).

## M1 closure, October 17, 2026

A third cloud session followed the handoff on a fresh container at revision `52e3ed6`. Pinned tools were reproduced and verified: Rust 1.90.0, Node 24.19.0, npm 11.9.0, Bun 1.4.3, Pi 1.3.0. Baseline checks before any change: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --locked --workspace` 35 passed; `npm test` 18 contract checks across 9 schemas plus 10 client tests; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` clean; `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs` clean; `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode fixture` 18/18; `git diff --check` clean.

Credential presence was checked by name only: `LUUNA_PI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` was present (the alias the runtime maps to `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` inside the isolated child), and OpenRouter's key endpoint accepted it. In an empty temporary config directory with only that key mapped, `pi --list-models --provider openrouter` listed 397 models from Pi's bundled catalog, so the runtime's `--offline` launch in a fresh config directory resolves OpenRouter models without a catalog refresh or a seeded `models.json`. The model chosen was `openai/gpt-4o-mini`.

**Result: genuine M1 is closed on Linux.** `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider openrouter --model openai/gpt-4o-mini` passed **19/19** checks (started 03:49:33 UTC, finished 03:49:40 UTC; runtime port 4247; Pi 1.3.0; platform `linux 6.18.44-fc-v139 x64`). The report was kept outside Git and contains no token or credential values; a search for the key prefix in `report.md`, `report.json`, and the runtime/dev-server logs found nothing.

| Evidence | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Success run | Run `[private-record-id]` recorded 37 durable events with 18 text deltas. `pi.agent_settled` was sequence 35 and `run.completed` sequence 36, so completion followed settlement. Final text: "LUUNA-M1-OK The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and influences our tides." The persisted model record is provider `openrouter`, id `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, api `openai-completions`, base URL `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`. Cursor replay reproduced all 37 event identities and the SSE stream closed at the terminal event. |
| Cancellation | Cancel was accepted (202) after `pi.agent_start` on a genuinely in-flight run; the terminal state was `cancelled`, never `completed`. The owned Pi child (pid 8983) was alive before the cancel and reaped before `run.cancelled`. A second cancel on the terminal run returned 200. |
| Provider failure | Model `luuna-no-such-model-0000` produced run `[private-record-id]` ending in `run.failed` with reason `400: luuna-no-such-model-0000 is not a valid model ID`, after `pi.agent_settled`, with no partial success. |
| Restart | The runtime was hard-killed while run `[private-record-id]` was `running`. The Pi child (pid 9023) exited 1362 ms later and was not orphaned. After restart the attempt was `interrupted`, and the three earlier run histories were identical by event identity. |
| Ownership and shutdown | A second runtime on the same data directory exited 1 with "another Luuna runtime already owns this data directory". SIGTERM produced an orderly exit 0 after 50 ms. |
| Authentication | Missing and wrong tokens returned 401 on protected routes; slash-command prompts were rejected with 400. |

Browser client evidence, Chromium driven by Playwright against the built runtime on port 4242 and `npm run dev` on port 1420 with a fresh random token: the client connected; run `[private-record-id]` with provider `openrouter` and model `openai/gpt-4o-mini` streamed and completed with the text "luuna browser" across 22 events; a second long run `[private-record-id]` was cancelled from the UI after 309 characters had streamed and ended in `run.cancelled` after 126 events; after a page reload and reconnect, the history listed the cancelled and completed sessions, and selecting the completed run replayed sequences 1–22 in strictly increasing order with the same text. Four screenshots were retained outside Git.

This session changed documentation only; no runtime, engine, client or component code changed. Not established by this run: native desktop launch (unchanged gap, GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1 are absent in the container), Mac/Windows service lifecycle, any provider other than OpenRouter, any model other than `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and anything beyond the tool-free demo. The storage guard that blocks `Implementing` without baseline evidence is untouched. A completed tool-free session is connectivity evidence, not a validation result or repository-writing readiness.

## M2a closure, October 17, 2026

A fourth cloud session implemented the handoff's next assignment, M2a import and read-only discovery, on a fresh container at revision `7757f56`. Pinned tools verified: Rust 1.90.0, Bun 1.4.3, Pi 1.3.0, git 2.43.0; Node 24.19.0 could not be installed through nvm in this container, so the frontend checks ran on Node 22.22.0 with npm 11.9.0 (the workspace's `engines` floor is 22.12). Baseline before any change: `cargo test --locked --workspace` 35 passed, `npm test` 18 schema checks plus 10 client tests, formatting/Clippy/typecheck/build/hygiene clean.

**Result: M2a is closed on Linux.** Delivered behavior (R04 begins; R07/R08 guards untouched):

- `luuna-domain`: `ProjectManifest` validation and `luuna-json-v1` hash (every field hashed, including check recipes and policy), `RepositoryIdentity`/`RepositoryObservation`/`DirtyState` and `Discovery` contracts. Shell interpreters need an explicit `shell` capability; absolute executables, `..` working directories, remotes carrying credentials, invalid branch names and non-v1 policies are rejected.
- `luuna-git` (new): read-only inspection through the host `git` with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, bounded output and timeouts; records redacted remote, sorted root commits, shallow flag, HEAD, branch, origin default branch, local branches and porcelain-v2 dirty counts. A test sets `core.fsmonitor` to a marker-creating command in the repository and proves it does not run.
- `luuna-discovery` (new): proposes recipes from `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, `package.json` plus lockfile (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun), `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`/`setup.py`/`requirements.txt`, `pubspec.yaml`, Gradle files and Xcode projects, each with evidence, observed/inferred confidence and questions (dirty checkout, missing remote, detached HEAD, unrecognised stack, no usable test script). A test embeds a marker-creating `scripts.test` and proves discovery never executes it.
- `luuna-storage`: migration 2 adds `projects`, immutable `manifest_revisions` (update/delete triggers), the machine registry `repositories`, `discoveries` and `project_events`. `confirm_manifest` checks the expected revision, revision `n+1`, equal repository sets, registered-identity match, observed remote and observed default branch in one transaction and records base commits.
- `luuna-runtime`: `POST/GET /api/v1/projects`, `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}`, `POST .../discover`, `PUT .../manifest`, `GET .../events`; `LUUNA_GIT_COMMAND`; API errors now carry deterministic runtime reasons for 409/422.
- `@luuna/api-client`: project types and methods, `confirmedManifest` replay fold, 409/422 reasons surfaced only when short and printable. Desktop: Projects panel (register, observe, discover, edit and confirm the manifest, event record).
- `schemas/project.schema.json`: optional `cwd` per check. ADR 0006 records the decisions.

| Check | Observed outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed. |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace` | Passed: 60 tests (13 domain, 6 discovery, 5 engine unit, 2 engine supervision, 3 git unit, 6 git inspection, 1 runtime unit, 10 runtime API, 3 runtime projects, 8 storage persistence, 3 storage projects). The runtime project tests import a synthetic dirty repository and this real checkout, snapshot every byte (including `.git/index`) before and after, and assert equality. |
| `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs`, `git diff --check` | Passed: 18 schema checks and 13 client tests; type/build/hygiene clean (Node 22.22.0). |
| `cargo generate-lockfile --offline` | Added only the three new workspace members and `chrono`/`tempfile` edges for the runtime; no dependency versions changed. |
| Built runtime, HTTP evidence (port 4251, fresh data directory) | Synthetic fixture (dirty: 1 unstaged, 1 untracked, remote configured with a fake credential) registered 201 with the remote redacted to `https://example.invalid/fixture.git`; discovery proposed `cargo test --locked` (required, observed) and `cargo clippy …` (optional, inferred) with a `dirty-checkout` question; confirmation 200 at revision 1, hash `sha256:c0be2d50…`, base `46c6a7df…`. ## Limits and next evidence

The provider prerequisite that blocked M1 is resolved for the cloud environment: `LUUNA_PI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is present and the genuine run above succeeded. Other providers still need their own `LUUNA_PI_<NAME>_API_KEY` (or plain name) and reachable network; `api.openai.com` remains refused by the agent proxy unless allowed in the environment's network settings. The remaining limits are:

1. **Provider prerequisite history:** no compatible provider key was present on October 16, 2026 (re-verified by name in a fresh container), which blocked the first closure attempt. On October 17 the owner added `LUUNA_PI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and the genuine run succeeded. To reproduce on another host or provider, set the credential under `LUUNA_PI_<NAME>_API_KEY` (the runtime maps it to the standard name inside the isolated child; use the plain name on hosts that do not reserve it), build the runtime, and run `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real --provider <provider> --model <model>`. No fixture, handshake, missing-key error, or Luuna-side test establishes provider success; only the real-mode report does.
2. **Native/platform prerequisite:** this container lacks WebKitGTK 4.1/GTK and associated native prerequisites. The Tauri project, icons and standalone Cargo lock are present; Mac/Windows jobs are configured but have not run. Native launch, packaging and install compatibility remain unverified.
3. **M3 and later product work:** repository import, discovery, baseline evidence, exact approval and one scoped writer exist (M2a, M2b and M2c, above); candidate validation, independent reviewer execution, repair, ticket/knowledge/prompt adapters, linked PR publication, browser/TUI parity and distributed-service installation are not implemented. A candidate in `validating` is not a validated or reviewed change.
4. **Distribution:** branded packages remain private and unpublished. Separate GitHub repositories were not created or populated: GitHub API reads work, but the integration denied repository creation. The owner subsequently chose to push everything to the existing `brodynelly/luuna` repository and defer separation. Creating repositories or supplying a creation credential is no longer a prerequisite for this workflow.
5. **Privacy/history:** the preserved archive is outside Git and is potentially private. Earlier commits still contain imported session histories. The bounded signature scan found no likely live credentials; it cannot prove all published or unavailable history is secret-free. No history rewrite or credential rotation occurred.

Cloud `install_script`, `start_skill`, and the two provider network destinations were updated and saved to use the new structure, actual runtime, and tested prerequisites. Configuration persistence does not publish the environment or establish validation in a new task.

### Harness

`scripts/m3-smoke.mjs` (new) drives a built `luuna-runtime` binary through one disposable Python fixture repository: register → confirm a manifest with real required checks → passing baseline → five approved workflows, each a ticket, an immutable plan, an exact-hash approval and one scoped writer. Fixture mode uses the synthetic Pi fixture and is labeled synthetic; real mode launches the genuine Pi for every writer and reviewer. The report records credential names only and scans itself, the runtime logs and the durable state for the token and every configured credential value.

| Scenario | What the runtime must show |
| --- | --- |
| feature | approved writer → frozen candidate r1 → diff bound to the hash and inside the task paths → stale hash refused → required checks pass in the owned worktree before any review → a fresh `review-…` session distinct from the implementer reviews the exact hash → `reviewed`, generation 1, cost recorded → no in-place re-validation |
| repair | a required check the ticket never mentions (`checks/policy.py` demands a header line) fails candidate r1 before any review → re-validation refused → manual repair creates r2 with a new hash and pending evidence → r1's hash refused → r2's fresh checks and fresh review reach `reviewed` → two attempts recorded |
| blocking | a requirement the writer cannot satisfy inside its task paths (a README section) under `auto_repair` → the reviewer's non-passing verdict pauses the run, bounded by `max_attempts: 2` |
| cancel | cancel while the reviewer is in flight → `cancelled`, identity and passed checks preserved, no review, reviewer child reaped, not repairable or re-validatable |
| restart | `SIGKILL` the runtime while the reviewer is in flight → restart marks the candidate `interrupted`, keeps identity and passed checks, reserves the remaining approved cost budget, refuses re-validation on budget, reviewer child exits, earlier candidate evidence identical byte for byte |

Then: developer checkout HEAD and tracked content unchanged, orderly `SIGTERM` shutdown, credential leak scan.

### What the runs changed

1. **Repair feedback now carries the failure.** A repair writer has no shell and cannot read private artifacts, so the runtime quotes the last 2 KiB of each failed required check's stdout/stderr into the repair prompt next to the reason, check records and review. The synthetic `repair_in_scope` writer now repairs only when its prompt quotes that output, so the existing manual and automatic repair tests fail without the runtime change (verified by stashing it: 2 of 6 repair tests fail) and pass with it. ADR 0009 is amended.
2. **Reviewer prompt names every required finding field**, including an integer `line` of at least 1 for whole-file findings. The `ReviewResult` contract itself is unchanged.
3. Harness fixes: `implement` sends the provider/model, the seeded repair failure is a non-contradictory policy check that must reproduce or the run fails, and the blocking predicate accepts only explicit reviewer outcomes: `blocked` without automatic repair, `changes_required` with one bounded repair, or a repair that produces no fresh candidate.
4. Review corrections (Codex, PR #5): quoted check output has every configured provider credential value and the service token redacted; the leak scan includes managed worktrees and artifacts with an 8 MiB per-file limit; the fixture repository is created with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, a null global config, an empty template directory, a disabled `core.hooksPath` and no provider credentials in the Git environment; the synthetic failure marker is assembled at run time so it appears only in check output; and on Windows the harness records that it cannot deliver a console control event instead of claiming an orderly shutdown. Second pass: quoted artifacts are opened without following symlinks and must still match the digest recorded with the check result, otherwise nothing is quoted (regression test tampers with an artifact and shows the synthetic repair writer receives no output); an artifact that reached the executor's 16 MiB cap is labelled so the writer knows the real end of output was not retained; every harness Git command, including the environment probe and the checkout-integrity check, runs with the isolated configuration and a credential-stripped environment; the diff assertion compares the exact changed paths with the approved task paths; the feature probe requires every configured required recipe; and the real blocking probe fails when the reviewer passes the unmet requirement. Third pass: the leak scan streams files of any size through a sliding window instead of skipping large ones and counts an unreadable file as a failure, and a reviewer process that outlives the hard-killed runtime is reported rather than killed by a possibly recycled PID. Fourth pass: quoted check output is capped at 16 KiB per repair prompt in aggregate, the harness requires the frozen candidate's plan hash to equal the approved plan's, and an unreadable directory fails the leak scan. Fifth pass: every harness request has a 30 s abort deadline, cancellation and restart probes require one passed result per configured required recipe, reports are redacted of configured credential values before they are written or printed, the checkout-integrity check compares untracked files against the post-baseline snapshot (baselines run in the developer checkout by design and may leave build output), and the harness refuses to adopt an existing fixture repository path. Sixth pass: a runtime that never becomes healthy is terminated and awaited before the harness fails, and the baseline and repair probes require one passed result per configured required recipe like the other probes. Seventh pass: live console output is redacted like the report, the hard-kill probe requires a numeric reviewer PID and an observed exit, a reused output directory is rejected before any runtime starts, and the blocking probe requires every required recipe. Eighth pass: the harness's final cleanup performs an orderly shutdown and awaits it with an awaited hard-kill fallback, and a runtime that cannot be spawned is reported in the sanitized report instead of crashing the harness. Ninth pass: the aggregate feedback cap is measured after JSON encoding (regression test: NUL-heavy tails stay within the budget), artifact verification is bounded to 32 artifacts and 64 MiB read per repair and runs on a blocking thread, quoted output additionally drops PEM private-key blocks and bearer/API-token-shaped lines as a best-effort guard against a host-permission check echoing an unrelated host secret (no isolation is claimed; the confirmed manifest remains the boundary), the harness deletes every file its leak scan flags or cannot read together with the durable state before it exits, and the real blocking probe requires the repair gate to be closed with the reason that matches the observed revision. Tenth pass: secrets are redacted from the whole verified artifact before the 2 KiB tail is cut (regression test places a value across the cut), each quoted entry is cut from the front to fit the remaining encoded budget or omitted, artifacts are opened without following links and judged, hashed and read through that one bounded handle, the harness refuses any non-empty output directory, and quarantine retries removal with blanking and records a failing check for anything still present. Eleventh pass: check results record the executor's own truncation flag per artifact (`truncated_artifacts`, mirrored in the schema and client) instead of inferring a cap from file length, the leak scan covers the fixture checkout and Git metadata, and real run 10 re-established the provider exit on the final code. Twelfth pass: the feedback fitting search uses a progressing midpoint (sweep test over every budget), artifacts are opened non-blocking so a FIFO swapped into the path is rejected instead of stalling the blocking pool (unit test creates one), harness truncation redacts before it cuts, the leak scan also checks entry names and symbolic-link targets without following them, and quarantine retries never follow a link (a replacement symlink is unlinked as a link, a multiply linked file is never blanked, blanking opens with `O_NOFOLLOW`). Thirteenth pass: artifact references are validated as single basenames (token characters, not `.` or `..`) so manifest IDs with embedded dots keep their repair feedback, the repair prompt delimits the recorded evidence and states that it is data to diagnose from and never instructions, quarantine validates the opened handle (regular, singly linked) and chmods and truncates that same handle, and real runs 11 and 12 were recorded on the final code. Fourteenth pass: the repair feedback's artifact reads happen only after the repair is exclusively claimed (cheap admission checks first; a lost blocking task yields feedback without quoted output rather than a claimed attempt with no worker), each artifact read is bounded by the remaining 64 MiB budget and the budget is charged for bytes actually read (unit test), and the harness scanner opens each file without following links and non-blocking and treats a non-regular replacement as a scan failure; real run 13 was recorded on this code. Fifteenth pass (harness only, no runtime change): quarantine never blanks a file on a platform that cannot open a non-following handle, only `ENOENT` counts as removed while any other lookup error leaves the target reported as present, directories are revalidated without following immediately before the scan descends, and each scan read is bounded by a 512 MiB limit and a growth check so an oversized or growing file fails the run as unscannable instead of hanging it. Sixteenth pass: configured credential values are redacted longest first and deduplicated so an overlapping shorter value can no longer leave a longer one's remainder in the clear (unit test), the harness records the in-memory report hit as a flag rather than the path `report` so a credential-bearing file of that name is quarantined like any other (verified on a synthetic tree), the scan has aggregate budgets (2 GiB read, 20,000 files) with every unscanned remainder failing the run and being quarantined, and a platform that cannot open a file without following links (no `O_NOFOLLOW`) treats every scan target as unscannable instead of opening it through a possible replacement link. Seventeenth pass: the harness's own report and console redaction orders configured values longest first and deduplicated, matching the runtime (probe with an overlapping pair confirms no fragment survives). Eighteenth pass: after a repair is claimed, the feedback reads and the writer both run inside the spawned worker task, so a client that disconnects mid-request can no longer strand a claimed attempt without a worker; the harness records a failing check and distrusts the leak scan when the runtime's exit is not observed after SIGTERM and SIGKILL; and the scan compares UTF-8 bytes instead of Latin-1-decoded text, so a credential with non-ASCII characters is found (probe confirms). Nineteenth pass: explicitly configured credential values are redacted (runtime) and scanned and redacted (harness) whatever their length, with length thresholds kept only for heuristic token detection (unit test with a four-byte value); and quarantine pins the output root by device, inode and real path at start and, before every destructive step, refuses to touch a target when the root was replaced or any component between it and the target is no longer a real directory (probe: a subdirectory swapped for a symlink to an outside directory after the scan is refused and the outside file survives). Twentieth pass: every string in the repair evidence envelope (reason, check records, quoted output, review findings, keys included) is redacted and the whole encoded envelope is bounded to 48 KiB by progressively tighter item and text caps, with an explicit omission note as the last resort (unit test: 500 secret-bearing findings and 300 checks); the harness walks the output tree with streamed listings, counts every visited entry against the 20,000-entry budget while walking and treats an incomplete walk as a leak that quarantines the fixture checkout; on Linux the scan and quarantine resolve every name through non-following directory handles held under `/proc/self/fd` and remove trees through those handles, so a renamed root or a component replaced by a link cannot redirect a read or a removal (probe: a root renamed after opening is still scanned and cleaned while a decoy at the old path survives; a parent swapped for a link is refused), and without held handles recursive removal is refused and recorded; and each run records the runtime binary's SHA-256 and fails unless the binary is newer than every tracked runtime source of the recorded revision and those sources are unmodified (verified: touching a source file fails the check). Twenty-first pass: the binary is bound by content instead of timestamps: `crates/luuna-runtime/build.rs` embeds a SHA-256 over every build input (crate manifests, build scripts, `src/` and `assets/`, workspace manifest and lockfile), `/health` reports it as `build_identity`, and the harness requires it to equal the digest of the checkout's build inputs with those inputs clean (verified: a binary built from modified sources, then touched after the sources were restored, fails); redaction in the runtime and the harness deletes any configured value still present after marker replacement (inside a marker such as `redacted`, across a marker boundary, or JSON-escaped) until none remains, and the final repair prompt is verified the same way (unit tests and a probe with colliding values); and an incomplete scan walk clears every entry under the output root through the held root handle, since unvisited entries can sit at any level up to the root (probe: 51 root entries removed after the budget stopped the walk at entry 11). ### Established and not established

Established on Linux with a genuine provider: an approved real writer in a Luuna-owned worktree; required host checks bound to the exact candidate and executed before any review; a fresh, separately identified Pi reviewer whose structured verdict the runtime enforces (`passed` → `reviewed`; `changes_required`/`blocked` → `paused`; invalid or self-inconsistent output → `failed`, never `reviewed`); manual repair reusing the immutable approval to create r2 with fresh evidence; bounded automatic repair stopping at `max_attempts`; cancellation and hard-kill recovery with reaped children and conservative spend reservation; developer checkout untouched; no credential value in any artifact.

Observed provider behaviour, recorded rather than hidden: `gpt-4.1` passed every check in runs 6 through 10, 12 through 14 and 16 through 23, 26, 27, 29 through 35 and 38 through 48, 50, 51, 55 through 58 and 60, and in runs 11, 15, 24, 25, 28, 36 and 37 its first writer attempt on the blocking ticket made no matching edit yet claimed one, which the runtime failed closed without a candidate (runs 52 and 53 again; in runs 54 and 59 the repair writer introduced a syntax error that the fresh checks caught; run 49 is excluded: a harness defect stopped it before any provider session); the smaller `gpt-4o-mini` and `gpt-4.1-mini` violated the reviewer JSON contract in 2 of 5 feature reviews; the runtime failed those candidates closed. Recovering from such a failure currently requires a new candidate revision through repair, because `validate` only resumes `pending` or `interrupted` candidates. That is safe but costs a writer attempt for a candidate whose checks passed; allowing a fresh validation generation for a candidate with passed checks and no recorded verdict was proposed for the MVP usability gate here and is implemented in the October 21 section below. `python -m unittest -v` output was not recognised by the test-count heuristic in these runs (`tests_detected: null`); the pass/fail decision still came from the exit code, and the empty-suite guard did not apply to that runner (recognised since October 21, below). Baseline runs leave `__pycache__` untracked in the developer checkout, as recorded for M2b. The reviewer's own transcript is not persisted; only `review.started`, the verdict, findings and evidence are.

Not established: native Mac/Windows client launch and service lifecycle (no capable host here); any provider other than OpenRouter; model behaviour beyond the three models above. M3's provider exit is closed on Linux; M3 as a whole closes only with the native-host evidence. Decision recorded during review: v1 ships no OS sandbox for native checks; bounded, redacted repair feedback stays on by default (ADR 0009).

Verification of this change set on Linux: `cargo test --locked --workspace` (174 passed), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `npm test` (20 schema checks, 5 scope-guard tests, 22 client tests, 9 desktop tests), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs`, `git diff --check`, fifty-nine `node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode fixture` runs (46/46 each, 47/47 once the runtime-exit check was added, 49/49 with the binary-revision and held-handle checks, 50/50 with the clean-checkout check, 51/51 with the pinned-compiler check, 53/53 with the restart-binary and hard-kill-exit checks, 55/55 with the running-image and Pi-provenance checks, 56/56 with the per-scenario Pi re-hash, 57/57 with the stray-process check, 58/58 with the post-run checkout check, 60/60 with the credential-free verification start, 61/61 with the post-reap developer-checkout check, where the harness itself was intact; run 25 exposed a scan-limit constant declared below its first use, fixed before the next push; a later run flagged a README edit under `crates/` as a source change, so the revision check was scoped to build inputs) and the sixty real runs above; run 60 ran on the final code of this change set from a clean committed tree. Deliberately stale binaries (a source touched after the build; a binary built from modified sources and touched after they were restored) failed the binary check as intended and are not counted.

## MVP usability gate: re-validation after an invalid review, October 21, 2026

The gap recorded under "Established and not established" above is closed on Linux. The sixty genuine runs showed that a small model can violate the reviewer JSON contract after every required check has passed; the runtime failed those candidates closed, and the only recovery was a repair revision, which spent a writer attempt on a candidate nothing was wrong with. The change set below adds the in-place recovery and leaves every other path as it was.

**Delivered (R09/R10; ADR 0009 point 7).** `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` with the exact hash now also accepts a `failed` candidate whose every required recipe has a passed result in its current validation generation and whose review is absent (invalid or self-inconsistent reviewer output, a refused reviewer session, a reviewer that returned nothing). `luuna-storage` admits the domain transition `Failed -> Validating` only under that condition and the existing headroom check, in the transaction that opens generation `n+1` (`candidate.validation_started` now always carries `revalidation: true|false`); the candidate revision, approval, plan hash, worktree and attempt count are unchanged, generation 1's records stay as audit rows, the checks run again under `c{revision}-g{generation}` artifact identities and a fresh reviewer session starts with the generation named in its prompt and nothing of the earlier reviewer's output. `Store::can_candidate_revalidate` applies the same approval, ticket and manifest binding as the gate in a read-only transaction; `GET …/candidate` reports it as `revalidate_allowed` next to `repair_allowed`, and the desktop shows "Re-validate and review" with the reason only when the runtime says so. Refused, as before: a failed, blocked, missing or interrupted check (repair or retry), any recorded verdict including `changes_required` (repair or re-plan), a cancelled candidate, an active worker, a stale hash, a revised ticket or manifest, and a reviewer lost mid-turn, whose reserved spend exhausts the cost headroom. No new budget exists anywhere in this path. Separately, `luuna-executor` recognises Python `unittest` summaries (`Ran N tests`, `NO TESTS RAN`), so `tests_detected` is populated for the harness's real `unittest` check and the empty-suite guard applies to that runner.

## MVP usability gate: client hardening, shutdown interruption and the desktop smoke, October 21, 2026

**Runtime (ADR 0004, R15).** An orderly shutdown (Ctrl+C or SIGTERM) used to reuse the cancellation signal and therefore recorded in-flight work as `cancelled`, a terminal state with no recovery, while a hard kill left the same work `interrupted` and resumable after restart. The baseline poll retries after a failed request instead of stalling. Every refused action is reported as "<Action> refused: <the runtime's reason>" plus the next allowed step (`apps/desktop/src/failures.ts`: budgets spent, state moved on, active work, baseline required, approval required, interrupted, invalid review, review did not pass, checks failed, host blocked, scope, cancelled, dirty checkout), and every recorded reason under a ticket or candidate carries the same guidance; transport failures and 5xx responses are described in plain sentences and no server body is ever shown. Implemented behavior:

It never treats prompts or host-native execution as an OS sandbox. ## Desktop design system, October 21, 2026

The desktop client now follows one token-based design system ([DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md), [ADR 0013](decisions/0013-desktop-design-system.md)). It is presentation only: the runtime still decides every state, permission, reason and next step, and no render or enable condition, handler, visible text, label, aria value, heading level or smoke-read DOM order changed.

**Delivered.** The pieces:

- **Tokens.** `apps/desktop/src/design/tokens.css` defines the dark default and a full light scheme under `prefers-color-scheme`. Layered base and component sheets plus one token-only sheet per screen are bundled from `'self'` (Tauri CSP unchanged).
- **Tones and the badge.** Six outcome tones are carried by colour, a shape mark and the unchanged runtime text. Exhaustive `Record` maps from the api-client unions live in `design/tone.ts`, so a new runtime state fails the type check until it has a tone. Only passed evidence and a live connection are green: a completed demo session used to be painted green and is now neutral. Interruption and outages use their own tone, never danger. `StatusBadge` is the one chip.
- **Shared components.** Panel and subpanel spacing, tray, meta line, form group, field row, headed records, the reason and next-step pair, section disclosures, bounded scroll regions and empty states.
- **Accessibility.** WCAG AA in both schemes. The narrow layout keeps visual order equal to DOM order, and forced colours keep marks and selection.
- **Process.** Three independent proposals were scored by two judges, and four screen agents each applied the system to one screen. Two review rounds followed: dark, light and 760 px screenshots, a behaviour-preservation audit and a design-system code review. They found and fixed a base specificity bug (disabled inputs looked enabled), fields inheriting the label's weight, textareas ignoring `rows`, an empty field-row column, light surfaces that did not separate, stacked tone rules and hashes breaking with orphaned tails at 760 px. They also caught a vacuous enforcement design: Vitest returns `""` for `?raw` CSS, so the test reads stylesheets with `node:fs` and fails on an empty sheet.

**Enforcement.** `design/design-system.test.ts`, part of `npm test`, checks:

- token-only stylesheets: no colour, length or duration literals, no `opacity` or `!important`, approved media queries only;
- every `var()` resolves, and both schemes define the same colour roles;
- WCAG ratios for every semantic text, mark, border and focus pair in both schemes;
- no selector named after a runtime state, and tone variables read only under `[data-tone]`;
- shallow screen selectors, registered component files, heading levels, no inline styles, badges through `StatusBadge`, and dismissible alerts;
- the tone taxonomy itself.

`scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` gains a presentation audit on the reviewed walkthrough page, the recovery page and the offline page. It checks WCAG AA contrast of every visible text run, placeholders included, against its composited background in the dark and the light scheme, after colour transitions settle. It also checks that the client follows the system scheme and that nothing scrolls horizontally at the 760 px window minimum. Against the old dark-only stylesheet these checks failed: two text runs were at 4.15:1 and there was no light scheme.

- `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs` passed 57/57: the 46 existing checks plus 11 presentation checks (synthetic). An earlier run measured colours mid-transition after a scheme switch; the audit now waits for transitions to settle.

The component submodule smoke was not run: this session can reach only the Luuna repository.

**Not established.** No native rendering of the new styles was checked: WebKitGTK, WebView2 or macOS WebKit, and Windows high-contrast mode. Main's Windows native smoke predates this change. Screenshots were reviewed from headless Chromium only. GitHub Actions refused every job of this branch and of `main` before a runner started (account billing), so CI gives no evidence here.

## MVP usability gate: backup and migration recovery drill on Windows, October 21, 2026

The last cloud-undoable item of the MVP gate other than the Mac smoke is closed on this Windows host. `node scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs` is the documented, repeatable drill for ADR 0016 (walkthrough step 7b): it builds or takes a built `luuna-runtime`, copies it privately, and against a disposable data directory with the synthetic Pi fixture it registers, discovers and confirms a fixture project, creates a ticket and completes one synthetic demo run; takes an online backup while the runtime runs and checks the printed digest against the file; shows `restore` refused while the runtime owns the directory and the runtime unaffected; stops the runtime through the authenticated shutdown; damages the database body and shows `check` and startup both refusing it before any write; restores the snapshot (the damaged file is moved into `backups/replaced-<timestamp>/`, not deleted), starts again and compares the whole authoritative view (projects, project events, tickets, runs and every run's event stream) with the pre-backup snapshot; completes new work on the restored database; marks the database as written by schema 10 and shows `check` and startup naming the newer version and the restore step, then restores and compares again; and finally runs the storage suite's upgrade drill across every earlier schema version with its automatic pre-migration snapshot. The report (`report.md`, `report.json`, maintenance transcripts, the two state snapshots) is written to `--out`.

**Result on this host (Windows 11 10.0.26300 x64, Rust 1.90.0, Node 26.10.0, Python 3.11.9, Git 2.55.0; runtime copy sha256 `a1d7de46…fc958b` built from the tree before this change set's runtime edits):** 31/31 checks passed on the first run; the sanitized report is [evidence/backup-recovery-drill-2026-10-21.json](evidence/backup-recovery-drill-2026-10-21.json). The migrations suite passed 7 tests. The drill never touched the developer's own `.luuna` directory and called no provider.

**Not established.** Hardware power loss (the restore roll-forward tests of PR 11 cover process death, not a lost disk cache), a Mac run of the same drill, and recovery of worktrees and private artifacts, which are files outside the snapshot by design.

## M5: verified stack profiles, host capability probing and approved scaffolding, October 21, 2026

Implemented per [ADR 0019](decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md) on this Windows host: `luuna-discovery::capabilities` probes every profile tool once per proposal (PATH/PATHEXT resolution as the executor, version argument only, bounded output and deadline, sanitized environment; Store app-execution aliases count as missing; `xcodebuild`/`swift` recorded missing off macOS without probing), discovery annotates every proposed check with `capability` and `missing_tools` and raises one `missing-tool` question per absent tool, and every advertised profile proposes real recipes (Node/React/Next.js/TypeScript with the detected runner, Go, Python with pytest only when configured, Rust, Flutter, native Android through the Gradle wrapper with `jdk`/`android-sdk`/`android-device` capabilities, native iOS through `xcodebuild test` with scheme/destination questions and the `xcode` capability). `luuna-discovery::scaffold` holds the embedded zero-network templates; `POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold/propose` and `POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold` propose, hash, confirm and execute them with the real baseline through `luuna-executor`, then register the project and record `project.scaffolded`. The domain gained only additive, defaulted fields (`CapabilityStatus`, `ToolProbe`, `HostCapabilities`, `ProposedCheck.capability`/`missing_tools`, `Discovery.host_capabilities`); stored discoveries still decode.

**Commands and results (Windows 11 x64, Rust 1.90.0, Node 26.10.0, Python 3.11.9, Git 2.55.0):** `cargo test --locked -p luuna-discovery` passed 15 library tests and the 8 profile fixture tests (Next.js/TypeScript, React with Node, Go, Python pytest and unittest, Flutter, Android, iOS, Rust, plus legacy decoding), each asserting that the annotation equals the real probe; `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --test scaffold` passed 6 end-to-end tests: Node (`npm test` running `node --test`), node-typescript (Node type stripping), Python (`python -m unittest -v`, `tests_detected: 1`) and Rust (`cargo test --locked`, `tests_detected: 1`) scaffolds with passing real baselines and registered projects whose discovery proposes the same recipe; Go and Flutter blocked consistently with the probe and refused with 422 at execution; Android and iOS always blocked; React refused without `confirm_network`; the refusals (unknown profile, invalid name, data-directory parent, relative parent, non-empty target at propose and execute, bad, unknown or tampered hash, `confirm: false`, key reused for another hash, name already registered) and the idempotent replay with one commit. The host probe found git, node, npm, bun, cargo, rustc, clippy, python and python3 and reported pnpm, yarn, go, pytest, ruff, mypy, flutter, dart, java, gradle, adb, the Android SDK, xcodebuild and swift missing.

**Not established.** Go, Flutter, Android and iOS profiles and scaffolds are proved only in their blocked and annotated form here; `go test ./...` on the Go template, `flutter create`, `flutter test`, Gradle and `xcodebuild` recipes have not run anywhere. The React scaffold's `npm install` step was not executed. Device and simulator presence is not probed. M5's capable-runner exit and the Mac-only checks remain open.

## M6: client parity (capability catalog and terminal client) and scoped-memory completion, October 21, 2026

Per [ADR 0020](decisions/0020-capability-catalog-and-tui.md), `schemas/capability-catalog.json` lists every product action (49 after the M5, M7 and memory routes joined it) with its route, typed-client method, desktop control marker and TUI command; `scripts/check-contracts.mjs` validates it against the runtime's served routes and the client; the failure explanations moved into `@luuna/api-client` and are shared by the desktop and the new `packages/tui` (`luuna-tui`: readline menus, outage display and self-reload, hidden token entry, full-hash approval acknowledgment, SSE following with `Last-Event-ID` resumption, scriptable non-interactive mode). Per [ADR 0021](decisions/0021-memory-promotion-and-project-export.md), memory promotion and the scope-safe project export exist in the runtime and both clients.

**Commands and results (Windows 11 x64, Node 26.10.0, npm 11.19.1):** `npm test` passed the contract suite (29 positive/negative schema checks; catalog of 49 actions validated against 43 served routes and the typed client; no runtime mutation without client parity), 10 scope-guard tests (9 passed, 1 pre-existing Windows skip), 8 component-pin tests, 7 harness tests, 251 desktop tests (including the new catalog-marker test), 39 API-client tests (3 new SSE tests) and 59 TUI tests (one per catalog action issuing its cataloged method and route against a mocked fetch, argument parsing, SSE following); `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` passed. `node scripts/tui-smoke.mjs` passed 53/53 checks against a built runtime and the synthetic fixture: wrong token and bad path refused with next steps, import, discovery, confirmation, baseline with log, ticket, plan, approval refused without the hash and with a wrong hash then approved with the exact hash, writer, worktrees and attempts equal to the API, diff bound to the hash, an invalid review failing the candidate and re-validation to generation 2, memory create/list/delete by hash and prompt save/render with the real component CLIs, a hard kill during a held check with the outage and the reconnection observed by a live follower that received all 51 events in order across the restart, interruption with reason and resumption to `reviewed`, and an orderly shutdown through the TUI (synthetic Pi; client and lifecycle evidence only). `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib export_tests` passed the export guard's unit test, and `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib components_real_promotion -- --ignored` passed (47 s, real Atlas, Missions and Beacon CLIs): a process memory promoted to project and then to user with provenance naming its origin, a skipped step and a stale hash refused, the same key replayed, project and user lists correct, an export carrying only project memory while a user memory exists, and an export refused when a ticket quotes a host path.

**Not established.** The interactive TUI mode has no pseudo-terminal harness and no keyboard audit; it has no terminal tone mapping. Import of a project export elsewhere is not implemented. Retention policy for memory remains documentation.

## M7: GitHub publication, reconciliation, CI observation and the doctor diagnostic, October 21, 2026

Per [ADR 0018](decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md): `luuna-git::remote` (GitHub remote parsing, read-only push URL, `ls-remote`, push by URL with the token only in scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*` headers and prompts disabled), storage migration 11 (`publications`, `publication_intents`), `luuna-runtime::publication` (gate, supervised publisher and reconciler, reqwest/rustls GitHub client with a configurable base URL, CI and merge observation) and the three routes `POST /runs/{id}/publish`, `GET /runs/{id}/publication`, `POST /runs/{id}/publication/reconcile`; `luuna-runtime doctor [--json]`. New dependencies: `reqwest` 0.13 (rustls, no system TLS) and `rustls` 0.23 with the `ring` provider; `--locked` builds pass.

**Commands and results (Windows 11 x64, Rust 1.90.0, Git 2.55.0):** `cargo test --locked -p luuna-git --lib remote` 3 passed; `cargo test --locked -p luuna-storage` all suites passed (the migrations suite's hypothetical newer table was renamed because migration 11 now creates the real `publications` table); `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib publication` 3 passed, `--bin luuna-runtime` 3 passed (doctor assembly and dispatch); `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --test publication` **6 passed, 0 failed** against a fake GitHub API on loopback and a local bare repository reached through the checkout's own `pushInsteadOf` rewrite under a GitHub-shaped registered identity: publish refused before a passed review and after a stale hash; a successful publication pushing the exact candidate commit and opening exactly one pull request; the same idempotency key replayed without side effects; a pull request created but answered after the client timeout, found by reconcile without a duplicate; a push that succeeded while PR creation failed, with reconcile retrying only the PR step; CI failure observed distinctly; a pull request reported merged making the record `integrated` with no merge request ever received by the fake server; and no route containing "merge". `cargo clippy --locked -p luuna-git -p luuna-storage -p luuna-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. A real `doctor` run on this host reported `ok` with Pi 1.3.0 resolved, the port answering `/health` and the components discovered, exit 0, and `missing data_dir` with exit 1 for an absent directory.

**Not established.** No real GitHub push, pull request, CI observation or human merge was performed: every scenario used the fake server and the bare remote, and real-token evidence is the M7 exit. Multi-repository linking has no end-to-end run. CI failure is reported but does not drive the repair workflow. Signed installation: see the packaging section below.

## M4: multi-repository coordination, October 21, 2026

Per [ADR 0017](decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md): plan task graphs are validated (self, unknown and duplicate dependencies, cycles named), `budgets.max_workers` is bounded to the task count and the runtime's four-run limit, discovery proposes `package` relationships from `package.json` names, Cargo path dependencies and `go.mod` replace directives with `confirmed: false` and evidence, manifest confirmation refuses unconfirmed relationships and confirmed cycles, migration 10 adds durable per-task state (`run_tasks`) with `task.*` events and `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/tasks`, the scheduler (`luuna-runtime::graph`) dispatches tasks in dependency order up to `max_workers` with one writer per repository, blocks dependents of a failed task with the reason, passes `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_<REPO>_PATH`/`_COMMIT` to consumer writers and checks, records one candidate set with every repository's exact commit and `<consumer>:<producer>` bindings, validation runs every repository's required recipes in its own worktree with the bindings and reviews one bounded combined diff, a failing consumer check fails the set with `integration blocked`, repair of a multi-repository set is re-planning, and resumption by `task_id` requeues incomplete tasks under the original approval within the approved budgets. Single-task plans hash exactly as before.

**Commands and results (Windows 11 x64, Rust 1.90.0, Python 3.11.9, Git 2.55.0):** `cargo test --locked -p luuna-domain` 33 passed; `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --test multirepo` **9 passed** in three runs with the three-repository Python fixture (api, shared, consumer, the consumer importing the shared package through `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_SHARED_PATH`): a compatible change producing three exact candidate commits and a reviewed set; an incompatible rename (`fixture:write_rename_function`) failing the consumer check and blocking the set with the integration reason while the producer's own check passed; two independent tasks overlapping under `max_workers: 2` (held writers) and refused beyond the limit; a hard kill and an orderly shutdown mid-graph leaving completed tasks' commits and worktrees intact with the interrupted task recorded, and resumption of a failed task by `task_id`; a cyclic plan and an unconfirmed relationship refused; relationship proposals from the three manifest kinds. The whole-workspace results on the final tree are recorded in the M8 section below. In the agents' concurrent run, three ten-second-budget writer tests failed once under machine load and passed on an isolated rerun (31 passed); the final serial run below is the evidence.

**Not established.** No genuine-provider multi-repository feature has run (synthetic writer only; real Python checks). An interrupted task is resumable only when the interruption left cost headroom: an attempt lost mid-prompt reserves the remaining budget (ADR 0009 point 5), so a hard kill of a mid-prompt writer leads to re-planning. P42 delegated roles, P44 dependency overrides and checking plan dependencies against confirmed relationships are open and listed in the ADR.

## M7: Windows development installer, October 21, 2026

`scripts/package-windows.ps1` builds the release runtime, installs the pinned Pi tree with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev` in `tools/pi`, stages the runtime, the Windows helper scripts, the launchers, licences and the Pi tree, and runs `tauri build` with a bundle overlay (NSIS target, WebView2 bootstrapper, resources mapped to a `luuna/` folder beside the executable; a certificate thumbprint enables signing). The native bootstrap (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime.rs`) and `scripts/ensure-windows-runtime.ps1` prefer that packaged layout when it is present and fall back to the development checkout otherwise, so one helper serves both. The script verifies the packaged layout after the build and writes a report with the installer, desktop and runtime digests.

**Result on this host (Windows 11 10.0.26300 x64, Rust 1.90.0, Node 26.10.0, Pi 1.3.0, NSIS 3.11 fetched by the Tauri CLI):** `Luuna_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe`, 19,596,016 bytes, sha256 `774bdba7284aa172f0ad7776194aecab31a34992010500f4b870c79392361d24` (desktop executable `63b4003c…225935`, packaged runtime `a04d6d12…565180`), unsigned; sanitized report in [evidence/package-windows-2026-10-21.json](evidence/package-windows-2026-10-21.json). Two earlier attempts were corrected first: a `-Debug` switch clashed with PowerShell's common parameter, and a glob resource mapping flattened the staged tree (Tauri copies a directory source with its structure, a `**/*` glob without it). Host prerequisites the installer does not carry: Node.js for the Pi engine, Git, Python for Python recipes, and a provider key saved with `Configure Luuna.cmd`; `luuna-runtime doctor` reports them.

**Not established.** No clean machine has run the installer; it was built and verified on the development host only. It is unsigned (SmartScreen warns). Mac packaging does not exist. An update policy is not decided.

## M8: release-evidence run on the final tree, October 21, 2026

`node scripts/release-evidence.mjs` runs the required checks and every lifecycle harness in sequence, records each command's actual exit status, duration and parsed counts, maps each step to the requirement IDs it supports, and never promotes a synthetic step to genuine evidence. [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) is the acceptance report it feeds: R01–R15 and A01–A34 each linked to the evidence that exists, the platform matrix, the limitations and the items that block the v1 label.

**Result on this host (Windows 11 x64, Rust 1.90.0, Node 26.10.0, npm 11.19.1, Python 3.11.9, Git 2.55.0, Edge 155 as the Playwright browser):** formatting, strict Clippy, `cargo test --locked --workspace` (388 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored across 43 suites), `npm test` (29 contract checks and the strict 50-action catalog, 10 scope-guard with 1 Windows skip, 8 component-pin, 7 harness, 251 desktop, 39 API-client, 59 TUI), type check, build, hygiene, whitespace and the native desktop crate check passed; the real component CLI smoke, the 6 explicit real-component and 3 real-Missions runtime tests passed; the M1 fixture harness passed; the backup drill passed 30/30 (its migration-suite step delegated to the workspace run); the browser walkthrough passed 64/64, the component workflows 23/23 and the TUI walkthrough 53/53. Sanitized report: [evidence/release-evidence-2026-10-21.json](evidence/release-evidence-2026-10-21.json). Corrections made during the run, each recorded there: the aggregator now locates the installed Edge or Chrome for the browser smokes, the component smoke hands the runtime an absolute Bun path (the runtime resolves bare names without `PATHEXT`), and the new scaffold form's label no longer duplicates the registration form's; one walkthrough attempt failed a single check on a run-state badge race and passed on the rerun.

**Strict M3 fixture harness on the committed revision `e39b2b5`:** `node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode fixture` passed **69/69** (synthetic; harness and protocol evidence only, never provider or M3 success): clean recorded revision and build inputs verified, the pinned Pi tree verified against a fresh integrity-checked install, exact approval, scoped writer, failing checks, independent review, repair budgets, cancellation, hard-kill recovery, shutdown, both checkouts preserved, Windows-owned descendants drained and zero credential leaks in the artifact scan. Sanitized report: [evidence/m3-fixture-e39b2b5-2026-10-21.json](evidence/m3-fixture-e39b2b5-2026-10-21.json).

**Not established.** The strict harness ran on the committed revision only after the commit, so the first release-evidence run below records it as not run. No genuine-provider step ran (no provider was named), so no provider claim is made for this tree. Everything in [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md)'s blocking list remains open: Mac, a clean-machine installation, real GitHub publication, capable runners for Go, Flutter, Android and iOS, a genuine run on the current tree and a real-project pilot. The v1 label is not granted.

# Imported tooling privacy and repository hygiene review

Date: October 16, 2026. Baseline: `532048d1839d003d724e55e8a47dbfdc44145004`.

## Result

The imported tool authoring records do not belong in Luuna's active project context. They have been preserved outside the checkout and removed from the working tree during the component migration. No likely live credential was identified by the local signature scan described below. This is a bounded scan result, not proof that the repository's entire published history is secret-free.

The original baseline remains in Git history. Removing files in this change does not remove earlier commits or invalidate any credential. No history rewriting, credential rotation, publishing, or remote deletion was performed.

## Inventory and disposition

The baseline had 642 tracked files. The following 103 files were imported authoring metadata, rather than required application source or published package contents:

| Original component | Paths removed after preservation | Files |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `seeds/` | `.pi/`, `.seeds/`, `.mulch/`, `.canopy/`, `.claude/`, `.factory/`, `.warren/`, `.gitconfig.burrow` | 47 |
| `mulch/` | `.seeds/`, `.mulch/`, `.canopy/`, `.claude/`, `.factory/`, `.warren/` | 32 |
| `canopy/` | `.seeds/`, `.mulch/`, `.canopy/`, `.claude/`, `.factory/` | 24 |

Seeds included 16 Pi session JSONL files totaling 1,511,947 bytes. Those files held 828 records, including 780 message records and 764 records containing tool-call or tool-result markers. All 16 sessions included working-directory metadata. Their conversation and tool output contents must not be automatically loaded as Luuna agent instructions or product fixtures.

The tracked `seeds/.pi/agent/auth.json` was an empty JSON object. Its sole reachable historical version was also empty. The file was removed with the session metadata because authentication storage should remain local even when initially empty.

The `.seeds/`, `.mulch/`, and `.canopy/` records were the imported tools' own issue stores, expertise stores, and prompts. `.claude/`, `.factory/`, and `.warren/` contained tool-specific automation and agent configuration. `.gitconfig.burrow` contained an upstream author identity and had no source references. These records are historical authoring context, not Luuna's current policies. All three package manifests published only `src/`; the tools' source and tests implement and exercise their storage formats separately. Source files, tests, fixtures, upstream notices, and useful reference documentation were retained through the component migration. Original agent instructions were preserved in the archive before being replaced with current Luuna instructions.

The original source and metadata archive is outside Git at:

`/workspace/luuna-preservation/imported-components-before-luuna-rebrand.tar.gz`

Its SHA-256 is `22aff086b01148dcb5d73031c41c7d96e6d6bf0c2a2e844d7eb2e51a0de8955c`. The archive contains 648 members and is 1,869,773 bytes; an adjacent `manifest.json` records the baseline. Its directory permissions are `0700`, and both archive and manifest permissions are `0600`. Treat this archive as potentially private historical material. It is not a dependency, agent input, or file to republish. This workspace copy is not a guarantee of long-term archival retention.

## Secret scan evidence

A local Python scanner read every unique blob reachable from the available Git refs with `git rev-list --objects --all` and `git cat-file --batch`. It scanned 612 blobs, totaling 14,320,314 bytes, across these four reachable commits:

- `532048d1839d003d724e55e8a47dbfdc44145004`
- `25107b20de1e5d422e80ea4bed9692a1561dc61d`
- `bcf08d732b908b83955203eb9a89355e28d2c1dc`
- `f3c2a17ff2d1ec3eff50921cbb7b41bb37c87715`

Twelve signature categories covered GitHub tokens, AWS access IDs, Slack tokens, Google API keys, Stripe live secrets, model API keys, private key headers, npm tokens, PyPI tokens, JWTs, URLs with credentials, and quoted generic secret assignments. Synthetic positive controls passed for all twelve categories. Matches and output were redacted by construction: only rule, file, line, blob ID, and coarse classification were recorded.

One match occurred in the original `mulch/test/log.test.ts:114`: an example-like credential URL in a test fixture, adjacent to assertions and containing an explicit example marker. No provider-key or private-key signature was found. No session excerpts or candidate credential values were printed or copied into this report.

The local scanner and its redacted machine-readable output were written to `/tmp/luuna-secret-audit.py` and `/tmp/luuna-privacy-scan.json` for this review. These temporary files are not repository dependencies.

## Coverage limits and future handling

- The scan covered currently available reachable refs. It cannot establish the contents of unavailable remote refs, dangling objects, deleted forks, external caches, or prior clones.
- Seven binary blobs were searched for plaintext signatures. Compressed archive contents and PDF streams were not decompressed.
- Signature matching can miss unknown token formats, unquoted secrets, obfuscated values, and encrypted data. No online credential validation was attempted.
- Neither Gitleaks nor TruffleHog was installed. The attempted official GitHub release lookup was blocked by the network proxy with HTTP 403, so this report does not claim a scan by either tool.
- A later dedicated scanner run should supplement this baseline when an approved scanner distribution is available. If a real credential is discovered, revoke or rotate it first; a separate, explicitly coordinated history cleanup may then be appropriate.

Local sessions, authentication files, actual environment files, runtime state, and generated build outputs should remain ignored. Preserve upstream license and copyright notices. Review component changes as source changes; do not automatically import historical prompts, hooks, or personal work records into Luuna's agents.
