# Luuna implementation handoff

## Latest: M4–M8 slices, the Windows recovery drill and client parity (October 21, 2026)

On top of the PR 11 audit branch, this change set lands bounded, tested slices of
every remaining milestone on the Windows host, each recorded with what it does
not establish: the MVP gate's backup/migration recovery drill
(`scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs`, 31/31), multi-repository coordination
([ADR 0017](docs/decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md), three-repository
fixture, 9 scenarios), GitHub publication with an intent ledger and `luuna-runtime
doctor` ([ADR 0018](docs/decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md), fake-GitHub
scenarios only), verified stack profiles, host capability probing and approved
scaffolding ([ADR 0019](docs/decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md)),
the capability catalog, shared failure explanations and the terminal client
([ADR 0020](docs/decisions/0020-capability-catalog-and-tui.md), `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs`),
memory promotion and the scope-safe project export
([ADR 0021](docs/decisions/0021-memory-promotion-and-project-export.md)), an unsigned
NSIS development installer (`scripts/package-windows.ps1`) and the M8 report
([RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](docs/RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md), `scripts/release-evidence.mjs`).
Read the per-milestone sections at the end of
[FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](docs/FOUNDATION-STATUS.md) for the exact commands and
counts on this host. Storage migrations 10 and 11 were added; `reqwest`/`rustls`
are new runtime dependencies. Nothing was committed, merged, installed or published.

**Next assignment:** evidence on hosts this one is not, never a shortcut around
them: (1) a Mac run of the native smoke, the drill and the packaging; (2) a
clean Windows machine installing the produced installer and completing the
fixture walkthrough with `luuna-runtime doctor`; (3) a real GitHub publication
with a token the owner supplies (push, linked PRs, CI observation, a human
merge); (4) capable runners for Go, Flutter, Android and iOS profiles and
scaffolds; (5) a genuine-provider `m3-smoke` run and a genuine multi-repository
feature on the current tree; (6) a real-project pilot with the measurements
`docs/11-acceptance.md` asks for. Keep merging human; keep the v1 label ungranted
until [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](docs/RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) has no blocking row.

## Earlier: PR 11 review follow-up (October 21, 2026)

The audit branch includes fixes for all 14 confirmed review issues and Windows
acceptance-harness corrections. Existing main history, component pins, installed
executables, credentials and live database contents were preserved. PR 11 was
merged into `main` (merge commit `bf538cc`, October 21, 2026); no installation of
this revision is recorded. Native/browser and fixture checks passed;
strict genuine-provider M3 remains open (final run 59/61 because the blocking
probe's writer produced no candidate). One existing Windows-disabled stress test
was not run. Read [the exact revisions, coverage and failures](docs/PR-11-WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md)
before claiming full Windows acceptance. The older successful M3 results below
apply to their recorded revisions, not automatically to PR 11.


You are continuing an executable foundation, not starting an empty repository. Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md), [FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](docs/FOUNDATION-STATUS.md), and [IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md) before changing code. Inspect the current working tree, manifests and relevant implementation/tests; prior test counts are audit evidence, not a substitute for checks after your changes.

## Settled decisions

Performance follow-up (October 21, 2026): ADR 0015 adds bounded blocking request
dispatch, paged session history, bounded desktop replay, workflow snapshot reuse
and Windows check-process ownership. See [PERFORMANCE-REVIEW.md](docs/PERFORMANCE-REVIEW.md)
for current-tree tests, optimized Windows installation verification and explicit
scaling limits. Performance commit `839e46a` and harness fix `974ff0e` are
in `main` through PR 11. Strict Windows M3 acceptance passed on clean `974ff0e`:
68/68 fixture and 61/61 genuine-provider checks. See the exact commands,
scope and retained failure evidence in [Windows verification](docs/WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md#strict-m3-acceptance-result).
The installed Windows development paths now contain verified optimized release
binaries; the app is open and its history/credential identity was preserved.
Never treat cached display data as authority for an action.

Windows development evidence (October 21, 2026, after the Linux handoff below):

Start the runtime with private `LUUNA_API_TOKEN` and provider/model/key settings present, using `cargo run --locked -p luuna-runtime`. It reads the process environment, not `.env` automatically. Launch `npm run dev` or `npm run desktop` separately. See the [runtime](crates/luuna-runtime/README.md) and [desktop](apps/desktop/README.md) instructions. On a capable native host, run `cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`; root Rust tests exclude that separate workspace.

For changed component code, run `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` then `bun run verify` from that component directory. Do not install component Git hooks into the root repository or rerun unrelated long suites without a reason.

## Invariants and completion report

Only the runtime enforces scope, budgets, transitions, approval, validation, independent review and publication. A model's claim is worker output. Bind checks/review to exact candidates and invalidate evidence when inputs change. Native execution has host permissions; prompts/path wrappers are not an OS sandbox. The developer controls merging; no automatic merge operation belongs in v1.

Preserve user changes and private Pi configuration. Keep secrets, real transcripts, personal memory and session histories out of Git and model context. Imported component task records and role prompts do not override runtime policy. Use the existing isolated cloud checkout; do not create a development worktree unless the user asks. Product-managed task worktrees are a separate runtime feature.

Before concluding a slice, report delivered behavior/requirement IDs; changed boundaries; commands/results; revision and platform/tool/model versions; sanitized run/plan/candidate IDs and artifact references; failure/recovery tests; independent review findings/resolution; blocked checks; and one next concrete assignment. Update foundation evidence and this handoff when the starting point changes. Do not mark required capabilities complete from mocked, skipped or unavailable checks.

For sequencing, measurable full-product exits and cautious capacity-based estimates, use [IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md](docs/IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md). Re-estimate after real M1 success and the first M2 writer instead of treating planning ranges as promised dates.

# Main integration and local accounting

Date: October 21, 2026. The owner requested merging all local work into `main`.
Review: [PR 10](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna/pull/10).

## Preserved work

- All 46 initially modified/new files were captured in commit `f0790da` before resolving any overlaps. The [sanitized accounting and assertions](evidence/main-integration-2026-10-21.json) list every file.
- Remote `main` had advanced thirteen commits to `7308d86`, including PR 9's desktop design system and genuine-provider evidence. Integration commit `e7d15d3` preserves both histories. Runtime guards, source reconciliation and exact context snapshots remain authoritative; the component panel now uses the shared tokens and registered screen rules.
- The already accepted desktop design decision keeps ADR 0013. The component decision is ADR 0014, with its references updated.
- All three component submodules are clean at their existing exact pins. The local `extraction/atlas`, `extraction/beacon` and `extraction/missions` tips are ancestors of their respective component repository HEADs. They remain intact as historical refs, rather than importing standalone repository roots into Luuna.
- There were no stashes or additional worktrees. Ignored `.tools/`, dependencies, desktop generated files, `dist/` and Rust `target/` outputs remain local. Pinned Node/npm validation tools were installed only under ignored `.tools/`. Credentials and personal runtime data were not staged or published.

## Merge verification

`npm test` passed under Node 24.19.0 and npm 11.9.0: 24 contract cases, 6 scope-guard tests, 8 component-pin tests, 220 desktop tests and 25 API-client tests. Typechecking, the production build, repository hygiene and diff checks passed. Final Rust 1.90.0 formatting and Clippy with warnings denied passed; `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets` passed **185 tests, zero failed, 10 explicitly ignored** on Windows after the scope-guard fix. The final running runtime hash is `c23b8e64b9d6dd0c1b145f0c1935afa2b3a09fb5fd651173a073d125e36f9c65`.

The combined UI passed 27 native component checks, 23 browser component checks, 55 native lifecycle/presentation checks and 57 browser lifecycle/presentation checks. These used real component CLIs and Git/unittest commands with synthetic Pi sessions. Native lifecycle checks include rendered contrast in both themes; the browser also checked the 760 px minimum width. The native desktop hash was `77f4387cc67febf0c8c6fb817f73a1ed0a56a2db601406e798cb55bbb01cb320`. No new genuine-provider component workflow is claimed.

The app workflow reports used runtime `3cee449015ac59fe6429c3339818490396bbafbd263f24fe3931be39b42e5a2a`. The subsequent pinned Node checks exposed a Windows verbatim-path/junction issue in the existing scope guard. Windows now uses the native realpath implementation before comparison, including missing-tail resolution. The existing canonical/ordinary-path guard regression and an added verbatim missing-tail case pass on Node 24. The final runtime was rebuilt and its Rust suite checked after this fix; the reports above are not relabelled as tests of that later executable.

Two earlier attempts were corrected before accepting evidence: a native build could not replace the open app until the owner closed it; and a browser component reload failed because Vite watched a Cargo-written Windows executable and exited with `EBUSY`. Both the app's Vite configuration and the isolated component harness now exclude `src-tauri` from watching. The browser rerun passed all 23 assertions. The browser lifecycle harness also required the installed Edge executable because its default Playwright browser was absent.

GitHub Actions run `39672767336` refused jobs before runner steps started. Check-run annotations explicitly identified the account payment/spending limit. This is unavailable hosted CI evidence; no successful hosted job or other-platform result is claimed, and no repository check or protection was disabled.

The personal runtime was stopped through its authenticated API only after confirming no active work, then restored with its existing state and credentials after build checks. Native packaging/signing, broader platform acceptance and full-v1 obligations remain separate from this source integration.

# MVP requirement and evidence report

Date: 2026-10-21. This names what the usable single-repository MVP demonstrates against the binding requirements in [02-requirements.md](02-requirements.md), where the evidence is, and what the MVP deliberately omits. It is the report the roadmap's MVP gate asks for; it does not call anything full v1. Evidence lines point at [FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md) sections and the committed harnesses; a fixture result is labelled synthetic wherever it appears.

Platform of the results recorded in the original report below: Linux cloud container (Rust 1.90.0, Node 24.19.0, Python 3.13, Git 2.43, Pi 1.3.0). **Update, October 21, 2026 (Windows 11 x64):** the Windows native lifecycle smoke passed in PR 11 (62/62 bundled WebView2), the backup/migration recovery drill is scripted and passed 31/31 (`scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs`, walkthrough step 7b), and the later milestone slices (M4–M8) are recorded in [FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md) and [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md); the omissions below describe the MVP as it was demonstrated and remain true of the single-repository MVP demo. No Mac result exists.

## Coverage by requirement

| ID | Requirement | MVP status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R01 | Local Mac/Windows operation | **Omitted from the MVP demonstration.** The runtime, client and Tauri shell build; no native launch, service supervision or installer has run on a Mac or Windows host. | Open gap recorded in every status section since M1 |
| R02 | Browser/TUI parity | Browser client only; no TUI exists. | Desktop smoke (`scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs`); M6 roadmap item |
| R03 | Pi with selected models | Met on Linux with OpenRouter (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini`); provider/model are runtime settings or per-action client fields; the credential never enters the client. | Status report M1 and M3 genuine-provider sections (sixty real runs, plus real run 61 on the MVP code, 61/61) |
| R04 | Import and creation | Import met (read-only inspection, discovery proposal, confirmed manifest revisions); scaffolding new projects is M5 and omitted. | M2a closure; walkthrough steps 2 and 3 |
| R05 | Multiple repositories | Omitted; the contract accepts relationships but one repository is scheduled. | M4 roadmap item |
| R06 | Coordination roles | Omitted beyond one writer and one independent reviewer per workflow. | M4 roadmap item |
| R07 | Approval before feature writes | Met: exact immutable plan hash, acknowledgment before approval, transactional revalidation at scheduling; missing or stale approval refused. | M2c closure; `luuna-storage` and `luuna-runtime` negative tests |
| R08 | Passing baseline before feature work | Met: baselines are supervised runs bound to manifest hash, commit, tree and host fingerprint; failed, blocked, empty, dirty and stale baselines block the writer. | M2b closure; `begin_implementation` gate |
| R09 | Real checks and fresh review | Met for tests and any command recipe: required recipes run in the owned worktree before a fresh read-only reviewer whose structured verdict the runtime enforces; static analysis and convention checks are whatever recipes the manifest confirms. | M3 implementation and genuine-provider sections; ADR 0009 |
| R10 | Bounded repair and useful pause | Met: manual and opt-in automatic repair under the immutable approval; attempt, time, cost and repair limits; infrastructure failures stop without edits; re-validation after an invalid review (October 21); reserved spend after interruption. | M3 sections; ADR 0009 points 4, 5 and 7 |
| R11 | Linked PRs | **Omitted.** No publication route exists; reviewed candidates are local commits in Luuna-owned worktrees. | M7 roadmap item |
| R12 | Human-controlled merge | Met by construction: no merge or push operation exists in the runtime. | Architecture, ADR 0009 |
| R13 | Stack profiles | Omitted beyond what the confirmed manifest's recipes run (Python and this repository's Rust/Node recipes have run). | M5 roadmap item |
| R14 | Scoped memory | Omitted; Atlas is not integrated. | M6 roadmap item |
| R15 | Runs independent of client lifetime | Met on Linux: closing or reloading the client cancels nothing; the client replays by cursor; hard kill and orderly shutdown record interruption and the work resumes after restart. | M1 closure; October 21 client-hardening section; desktop smoke recovery scenarios |

Engineering requirements E01 to E09 are met for the single-repository path (deterministic runtime gates, immutable revisions and hashes, bound evidence, fail-closed checks, idempotent creation and expected-revision guards, invalidation on change, untrusted repository content, preserved worktrees, loopback with bearer authentication). E10 is partial: migrations and pins are recorded; the OS matrix has not run.

## What a developer gets

Import a repository, confirm its checks, prove a baseline, write a ticket, approve an exact plan, let a scoped Pi writer change a Luuna-owned worktree, run the real checks and a fresh independent review on that exact candidate, inspect diffs, logs and findings, repair within approved budgets, and recover from cancellation, crash or shutdown with the evidence intact and the next step named. The result is a reviewed local commit the developer publishes and merges by hand.

## What the MVP omits, explicitly

- Native Mac operation (R01): no Mac host has run anything. Windows: the native smoke, the recovery drill and an unsigned development installer exist (see the update above); a clean-machine installation has not run.
- Publication: no push, no pull request, no CI observation (R11).
- Multi-repository projects, relationships and roles (R05, R06).
- Project scaffolding and the stack-profile matrix (R04 creation, R13).
- Missions, Atlas and Beacon integration and scoped memory (R14); tickets remain temporary local records (ADR 0003).
- A TUI and the shared capability catalog (R02).
- Any OS sandbox for native checks: checks run with host permissions under the developer-confirmed manifest (ADR 0009).
- A writer interrupted mid-session cannot be resumed under the same approval; the next plan revision is required (its worktree is preserved).
- Automatic runtime startup from the desktop shell; the service is started by hand.

## Evidence the MVP relies on, by kind

- Deterministic tests: `cargo test --locked --workspace` (Rust domain, storage, executor, Git, discovery, engine and runtime suites with the synthetic Pi fixture and real host commands), `npm test` (schema, scope guard, client, desktop).
- Lifecycle harnesses, synthetic: `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode fixture`, `node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode fixture`, `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs`.
- Client presentation: `apps/desktop/src/design/design-system.test.ts` under `npm test` (token-only stylesheets, contrast of every semantic pair in both schemes, tone taxonomy, screen structure) and the desktop smoke's presentation audit (rendered contrast in the dark and light schemes, no horizontal scroll at 760 px). See [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md).
- Genuine provider: `node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode real …` and `node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode real …` with a configured credential; results are tabulated in the status report and never inferred from fixtures.
- Native hosts: Windows only (PR 11 native lifecycle smoke; `scripts/backup-recovery-drill.mjs` 31/31; `scripts/package-windows.ps1`). Mac: none.

# Performance review — October 21, 2026

## Follow-up: bounded execution and optimized Windows upgrade

The October 21 follow-up implements ADR 0015. The first-pass findings and
measurements below remain historical evidence, not the current list of defects.

| First-pass finding | Follow-up disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Large session history / retained payloads | Indexed keyset run pages; event pages capped at 200 and about 1 MiB; one historical page loaded on demand; bounded live event window and incremental bounded assistant display. Legacy full-history routes remain compatible. |
| SQLite blocking Tokio I/O | Authenticated requests use at most 32 blocking tasks; existing four-run admission also bounds workers. SSE has 16 stream slots and bounded blocking reads. Health/shutdown remain reachable at request capacity. Transaction boundaries and FULL durability are unchanged. |
| Workflow refresh fan-out | Four-way concurrency; settled snapshots reused; explicit refresh, actions, reconnect and component changes invalidate snapshots. Source observations are display snapshots; runtime source/approval checks still run. |
| Noisy checks | 64-slot nonblocking display queue, at most 100 excerpts per stream, bounded version probes. Both artifact streams still drain and retain their capped, hashed evidence. |
| Windows check descendants | Suspended creation, Job Object assignment before execution, kill-on-close ownership. Real child/grandchild assertions now run on Windows; the stalled-consumer test drains 40 MiB of output without unbounded progress or blocked pipes. Executor tests finish in about four seconds. |
| Development-profile installation | Both runtime and desktop built in optimized release mode; the installed checkout-based paths are retained for existing launchers. Installation verification is recorded below. |

### Installed Windows result

The existing checkout-based Windows installation was upgraded after confirming
it had no active work. The previous executables, SQLite database and encrypted
connection/provider records were backed up under
`%USERPROFILE%/.luuna/verification/performance-upgrade-20261021-183141`.
Saved run records, connection token identity, data-directory identity and provider
record bytes were verified unchanged. No plaintext credential was logged.

- Installed runtime: `target/debug/luuna-runtime.exe`, now an optimized release
  binary despite the retained development-launcher path. SHA-256
  `74fb9ad1964675bf7b1bcab5c19c5d3939f32addb86878d68ae8e8c4292441a6`.
- Installed desktop: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/luuna-desktop.exe`,
  optimized release binary, SHA-256
  `596df0c08d54d9d1d6280b9b546a013efcf39caa82e90fd0b6c909dc3bef1662`.
- Final runtime content identity:
  `sha256:3924f254ad3d284fd4745b3c0da0a65379205a4642545eddd9d8c9e8ccbf0991`.
  The final rebuild includes additional test source in that digest; production
  behavior is unchanged from the earlier native/provider workflow smokes. The
  final binary separately passed genuine-provider M1 **20/20** and installed
  native startup **17/17**.
- Startup checks: automatic private IPC connection, warm reuse, cold retry,
  foreign-listener refusal, concurrent windows, reload, disconnect, preserved
  history/credentials and runtime survival after all windows close. Evidence:
  `%USERPROFILE%/.luuna/verification/native-startup-61225f0a/report.json`.
- One observed warm launch-to-connected: **3.792 s**. Cold retry plus concurrent
  launch-to-connected: **5.603 s**. These include PowerShell identity checks,
  WebView2 profile creation and test observation; neither is a controlled median
  nor a signed-installer benchmark.
- Finally launched the ordinary installed desktop again. Its actual process
  path/hash matched the upgraded executable; its visible window responded and
  the runtime health endpoint answered. `final-window.json` in the upgrade
  directory records this check. The app is left open, with its independent
  runtime running. A later ordinary debug build can replace these release
  binaries at the development paths; no distribution/update service is implied.

### Follow-up measurements

- 10,000 synthetic runs, nine warmed debug samples: original N+1 median
  361.965 ms, complete single-query history 81.362 ms, first indexed 200-run
  page **1.762 ms**. These are different workloads; the page returns 200 rows,
  while the complete-history measurement returns all 10,000.
- Browser stress: 10,000 events, about 10 MiB, at most 200 displayed rows.
  First-page rendering was 217 ms in one run and 956 ms during concurrent
  builds/tests. The instrumented repeat reconstructed all 10,000 records in
  3.20 s. No controlled median or universal speedup is claimed. Empty polls
  caused zero event-list DOM mutations; historical paging remained stable
  during append, payload expansion, both schemes at 760 px and disconnect.
- Initial assistant reconstruction still traverses history page by page;
  workflow ticket enumeration and legacy API consumers can still request whole
  lists. These are explicit scaling limits, not claims of constant-time loading
  or complete production-load profiling. A durable display projection and
  workflow pagination remain possible later slices.

### Follow-up verification

| Coverage / command | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets --target-dir target/performance-followup -- --test-threads=2` | **191 passed, 0 failed**, 11 explicitly opt-in tests measured separately. Includes bounded database admission/health responsiveness and terminal SSE draining across multiple pages. |
| Storage page tests | Stable ordering/ties, project filter, inserts between pages, forward reconstruction, reverse paging, byte cap and single-oversized-event progress passed. |
| `cargo test --locked -p luuna-components --test real --target-dir target/performance-followup -- --ignored --test-threads=1` | Actual pinned component CLI integration passed. |
| `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib --target-dir target/performance-followup -- --ignored --test-threads=1` | All eight real Missions/Atlas/Beacon tests passed, including drift, idempotency, uncertain side effects and restart. |
| `cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --test writer --target-dir target/performance-followup -- --ignored --test-threads=1` | Component-source changes during real CLI writer/reviewer boundaries were refused; passed with synthetic Pi. |
| Native component UI | **27/27**, actual pinned CLIs, optimized WebView2, synthetic Pi, activation/reconciliation, explicit resource selection, source drift and replay. |
| `npm test` | 24 contracts, 6 guard, 8 pin checks, 221 desktop and 28 API-client tests passed. |
| `npm run typecheck`; production frontend build; workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`; format and hygiene | Passed after correcting a newly added test fixture's missing envelope fields and adding a dismiss button required by the design-system test. |
| Native Tauri Rust unit test | Passed. Release Tauri build succeeded; toolchain emitted the existing deprecated STATIC_VCRUNTIME warning. |
| Browser MVP | **57/57**, including actual runtime/check commands, restart/shutdown, accessibility, dark/light schemes and minimum width. Synthetic Pi. |
| Optimized native WebView2 MVP | **55/55**, same lifecycle plus native independent-runtime lifetime. Synthetic Pi. |
| Genuine-provider M1 | **20/20**, OpenRouter with `openai/gpt-4.1-mini`, pinned Pi 1.3.0, optimized runtime. Completion, cancellation/reap, failure and restart covered. |
| Genuine writer/repair/reviewer diagnostic | First `gpt-4.1-mini` run 15/16: model repair hardcoded the greeting, tests passed, independent review correctly returned `changes_required`. Evidence retained. Fresh `openai/gpt-4.1` run **16/16**, including exact candidate identity, actual failing check, new repair revision, fresh review and untouched developer checkout. |
| Strict M3 acceptance | Initially refused the uncommitted checkout. After authorized commits and Windows harness fixes, clean `974ff0e` passed **68/68 fixture and 61/61 genuine-provider assertions**. See [strict acceptance evidence](WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md#strict-m3-acceptance-result); the earlier Windows diagnostic remains separate. |

Two initial test invocations hit Windows linker file locks when another test
process held the same executable; final checks were serialized appropriately.
No product assertion was relaxed for those failures. This is Windows evidence;
macOS/Linux native clients, production-scale p95/p99, and installer/signing
remain unverified here. The original documentation validation is separate.

Private evidence is outside the repository under the user's `.luuna/verification`
folder (provider tests and upgrade) and the Windows temporary directory (smokes
and test logs). No credentials or real session transcripts are committed.

---


This review covers the implemented React client, shared API client, Windows Tauri
bootstrap, Rust runtime/storage, Pi transport, check executor, Git/discovery and
the Luuna component adapters. It does not certify maximum possible performance,
full-v1 functionality, macOS/Linux rendering, or provider response latency.
Component internals remain independently maintained submodules.

## Changes made

1. **History queries:** `Store::runs` and `Store::projects` now fetch their rows in
   one SELECT instead of listing IDs and preparing/executing one SELECT per ID.
   Shared row decoding preserves ordering, every field, and JSON error handling.
   No schema, transaction, durability, approval or candidate policy changed.
2. **Session replay:** a per-subscription `EventReplay` validates only incoming
   records, retains identity indexes, rejects conflicting/gapped pages atomically,
   and returns the same snapshot for empty/overlapping pages. Existing records
   keep their object identity. New pages still copy the snapshot's array; this is
   not a constant-memory transcript store.
3. **Workflow replay:** each workflow retains just its event cursor and latest
   reason. Subsequent refreshes request only events after that cursor instead of
   the entire transcript. Cursors commit together after successful validation and
   reset on project/client changes. Ticket sources and candidate permissions are
   still refreshed from the runtime; no freshness or authorization cache was added.
4. **Rendering:** the session event view renders at most 200 rows, with earlier,
   later and latest controls. Browsing an earlier page holds its position while
   events arrive. All events remain accessible. Closed payloads are formatted
   only when opened; error disclosures retain their initial open state. Memoized
   rows, transcript extraction and the project panel avoid unrelated work during
   typing, empty event polls and history refreshes.

These are implementation optimizations within the accepted architecture, not a
new authority, API protocol, storage format or lifecycle decision.

## Measurements

Windows, Rust 1.90.0 debug profile; synthetic disposable data only. Timing values
are local observations, not CI thresholds or end-to-end provider speedups.

| Workload | Before | After | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Retrieve 10,000 saved runs, median of nine warmed samples | 1,180.364 ms | 164.052 ms | 7.20× faster; 10,001 SELECTs reduced to one. Compares the original lookup algorithm with the new implementation in the same benchmark. |
| Merge 10,000 events in 100 pages, then 100 empty polls; median of nine warmed samples | 172.345 ms | 2.160 ms | 79.79× faster for replay bookkeeping; does not include network, rendering or provider work. |
| Render a 10,000-event, roughly 10 MiB synthetic history in Edge 155 | 3,604 ms | 1,111 ms | Individual observations before/after adding paging, both already using lazy payloads. Concurrent host load varied; not a controlled median or comparison with untouched main. |
| Event DOM rows for that history | 10,000 | 200 | Remaining events are available through paging. |
| Event DOM mutations during idle polling, after load | Not measured | 0 | Verified over 3.1 seconds while polling continued. |

Workflow transcript bandwidth now scales with newly appended events per refresh,
instead of the total accumulated transcript on every refresh. No numeric network
speedup is claimed. The production JS bundle grew from 256.19 kB / 77.83 kB gzip
to 258.45 kB / 78.42 kB gzip; these changes optimize ongoing work, not bundle size.

Reproduce with:

```powershell
node scripts/performance-replay.mjs
cargo test --locked -p luuna-storage --test history --target-dir target/performance-review -- --include-ignored --nocapture
node scripts/performance-ui-smoke.mjs --browser 'C:/Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe'
```

The UI benchmark intercepts every request to its synthetic endpoint. It never
uses personal history or calls a provider. It checks cursor continuation, zero
idle event mutations, lazy payload open/close, history paging and disconnect.
The storage test checks all fields/order against individual reads, restart
preservation, and refusal of malformed persisted JSON.

## Findings from the first pass (follow-up disposition below)

| Priority | Finding and evidence | Next bounded improvement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High at large history sizes | `/runs`, event replay and several project lists still return all matching records. The browser retains the selected run's full event payloads, although its DOM is bounded. `App.tsx` refreshes all runs every two seconds, including when idle. | Add explicit cursor pagination/project filters to runtime/API contracts, fetch historical event pages on demand, and exercise reconnect without dropping events. Do not silently truncate history. |
| High under concurrent load | The service performs synchronous SQLite work behind one `std::sync::Mutex<Store>` inside async handlers and worker event paths. FULL synchronous commits preserve evidence but can occupy Tokio workers during disk stalls. | Measure request p95/p99 during high-rate worker output, then consider a bounded database worker or carefully scoped blocking jobs. Preserve atomic state/event transactions, admission draining and shutdown ordering. No weakened durability setting is justified. |
| Medium with many tickets/workflows | `Workflows::load` still loads plans and source state per ticket, and leases/candidate state per workflow. Missions source reads invoke pinned native CLIs; each call verifies source/toolchain identity. The selected workflow is also observed by the session panel. | Introduce a bounded project-summary read or shared client refresh coordinator; batch compatible source observations without caching away drift checks. Measure CLI startup separately from source verification. |
| Medium under noisy checks | The executor sends progress into an unbounded channel. The baseline relay limits persisted display events, but capture can keep allocating/sending updates after that limit. Artifact files themselves are capped at 16 MiB per stream and continue draining. | Bound/coalesce display progress, explicitly preserve start/final evidence, and stress cancellation against a fast producer and slow consumer. Blocking pipe drainage on a saturated UI queue would be a regression. |
| Medium for native teardown | Windows executor descendant cleanup remains weaker than the component runner's Job Object ownership, as already recorded in ADR 0007. The native executor test process took about 61 seconds despite passing individual deadlines, consistent with descendant-held pipe cleanup costs. | Add verified Windows descendant ownership/cleanup as its own lifecycle slice; prove child/grandchild exit and prompt shutdown. Do not confuse direct-child cancellation with tree ownership. |
| Lower priority without measurements | Windows cold startup invokes a fixed PowerShell bootstrap and performs identity/authentication checks. Tauri already runs that blocking work off the async worker. The developer build is not a release-profile performance measurement. | Measure cold/warm packaged startup and process memory before considering bootstrap or release-profile tuning. Keep duplicate-start reconciliation and token boundaries. |

Pi framing (1 MiB), Git output (8 MiB), manifest inspection (1 MiB), component
I/O/deadlines and check artifact bounds were reviewed. Those existing bounds are
valuable; removing validation, source identity checks, hashes or durable writes
to make benchmarks faster would weaken the application. No such change was made.

## Verification and limits

Product evidence here is separate from the original documentation validation
report. The following checks ran on this Windows host:

| Command / coverage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | Passed: 24 contract cases, 6 scope-guard tests, 8 component-pin tests, 221 desktop tests, 27 API-client tests. |
| `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build` | Passed. Final production JS: 258.45 kB, 78.42 kB gzip. |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | Passed. |
| `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets --target-dir target/performance-review -- --test-threads=2` | Final run passed, exit 0, zero failures. Explicitly ignored provider/component/platform prerequisites and the manual benchmark remain separate from normal workspace coverage. The real-component native smoke and manual benchmark are recorded below. |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --target-dir target/performance-review -- -D warnings` | Passed; storage Clippy rerun after its test correction also passed. |
| `cargo test --locked -p luuna-storage --all-targets --target-dir target/performance-review -- --test-threads=2` | Passed: 34 tests; manual benchmark intentionally ignored in the normal run and passed separately. |
| `node scripts/performance-replay.mjs` | Original/incremental output equality verified; timing above. |
| `node scripts/performance-ui-smoke.mjs --browser <Edge>` | Passed: 10,000 events, 200 rendered rows, payload open/close, earlier/later/latest paging, cursor continuation, fixed historical position during an appended event, 760 px width in both schemes, idle DOM and disconnect. Final repeat rendered in 1,077 ms. |
| `$env:LUUNA_CHROMIUM = <Edge>`; `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime target/performance-review/debug/luuna-runtime.exe` | 57/57 passed: browser workflows, real checks, synthetic Pi, restart/shutdown, accessibility, contrast in both schemes and 760 px width. |
| Set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to absolute `target/performance-review-native`; `npm run tauri --workspace @luuna/desktop -- build --debug --no-bundle` | Passed. Separate executable; existing personal app not replaced. Existing STATIC_VCRUNTIME deprecation warning remains. |
| `node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs --native target/performance-review-native/debug/luuna-desktop.exe --runtime target/performance-review/debug/luuna-runtime.exe` | 55/55 passed in actual bundled WebView2, including independent runtime lifetime. Native harness skips the browser-only 760 px resize check. Reviewed the resulting workflow screenshot. |
| `node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --native target/performance-review-native/debug/luuna-desktop.exe --runtime target/performance-review/debug/luuna-runtime.exe --runtime-label performance-review` | 27/27 passed: actual pinned Missions/Atlas/Beacon, private-memory selection, lost-response retries, source drift/reconciliation, approval/implementation refusals, real candidate checks, synthetic writer/reviewer, reload and normal window closure. |
| `node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs`; `git diff --check`; `node --check` on both added benchmark scripts | Passed. |

Native client tested: SHA-256
`e0a6d945bee49d0f59ce0a1b46aa2bf258a4f7869b0f33e30785f46ee298ef8e`.
Runtime used by the smokes: SHA-256
`1bc6bba46c7963c295b54dd9bad0b491404192a59ba6209c95a7aad72dca3f1c`.

The native smoke verifies the bundled application, not only a Vite build. It
does not establish macOS/Linux GUI performance, a signed installation or a
release-profile memory/CPU baseline. Automatic connection was observed in the
component smoke; the separate full cold-start/foreign-listener suite was not
rerun because bootstrap code did not change.

The initial default-target Rust command could not replace the running personal
`target/debug/luuna-runtime.exe` (Windows error 5). Verification uses a separate
target directory; the personal executable and state were not upgraded. The first
full parallel test attempt later missed the five-second wait for the second
`pi.agent_start` in the repair-cancellation fixture while builds ran concurrently.
The same test passed alone and in the next full run. That run exposed a separate
storage-test assumption: two fast stages were assumed to always cost exactly one
rounded second each. A stage finishing within the same persisted millisecond
legitimately costs zero, yielding 31 rather than the hardcoded 32 seconds. The
regression test now checks exact added charges and cross-revision accumulation
relative to the recorded stage time. Production budget accounting is unchanged.
Final results are recorded separately rather than hiding either initial failure.

The first browser smoke attempted Playwright's absent default Chromium because
that harness uses `LUUNA_CHROMIUM`, not a `--browser` option. Using the existing
Edge executable through the supported environment variable resolved this.
An attempted workspace rebuild while the disposable native component smoke held
its runtime executable also hit Windows error 5; this was a test-artifact lock,
not a service failure. It did not interrupt the smoke or the personal service.

No commit, push, installer publication, personal service upgrade, or real-provider
execution is part of this review. Native smokes use disposable runtime state and
synthetic Pi; real check commands still run. Provider latency/cost, sustained
production load, native memory profiling and other operating systems need their
own evidence before any broader performance guarantee.

text:
# PR 11 Windows review fixes and preservation evidence

Date: October 21, 2026 (America/Chicago). PR: [#11](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna/pull/11).
The PR was merged into `main` afterwards as `bf538cc` (October 21, 2026); the verification below ran before the merge. **The confirmed review fixes are complete, but strict genuine-provider M3 acceptance remains open: the final run passed 59/61 checks.** The local Rust/frontend, native/browser lifecycle, component and fixture suites passed, with one existing Windows-disabled stress fixture.

This record is Windows product evidence,
separate from the original documentation validation report and historical Linux results.

## Revisions and preservation

Product fixes are in `f9def0900b68404c3b03dd158bc093cde911ae80`.
Acceptance-harness corrections are in `a5ff089` and `631ed21` (the final clean strict-M3 test revision).
The subsequent evidence commit changes documentation only. These commits descend
from the existing audit branch and retain all of main at `24a7e4a`.

- Installed runtime and desktop executable SHA-256 hashes are unchanged. Builds
  and test services used separate output directories, disposable stores and fixtures.
- The live database still matches the pre-test snapshot row-for-row across all
  23 tables, including migration metadata. Its service remains authenticated.
- A SQLite online backup was upgraded in a disposable directory. All 924 existing
  rows across 22 historical tables survived unchanged; schema 9 and the automatic
  pre-migration snapshot were verified. No migration ran against the live store.
- The encrypted provider file is byte-for-byte unchanged. Native warm startup
  refreshed connection metadata through the existing bootstrap; the existing
  runtime and token still authenticate. Connection-file ciphertext is therefore
  not claimed byte-identical.
- Missions, Atlas and Beacon gitlinks and manifest pins are unchanged. Historical
  logs, plans, approval/evidence records, worktrees, requirements and ADRs remain.
  The verification made no installation, merge, automatic publication or
  component-internal change; the PR was merged into `main` afterwards.

## Review issues fixed

| Issue | Result and regression evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Deleted Python application module reported as infrastructure | An absent module alone stays an ordinary failure; external classification requires a bounded explicit requirements declaration. Executor tests cover deletion and a declared missing dependency. |
| Relative and absolute SSH paths conflated | Repository keys preserve path scope; domain tests distinguish SCP relative/absolute/URI paths. |
| Concurrent backup overwrites a snapshot | Verified snapshots publish with atomic no-replace hard links; a competing destination wins without being overwritten. Unsupported filesystems fail closed. |
| Historical uppercase artifact names lost | Safe legacy filename fallback preserves API access and digest-checked repair feedback without renaming evidence. |
| Bad metadata/event aborts orphan recovery | Startup reads state columns and decodes individual ownership events independently; malformed ownership grants no termination authority. |
| Baseline ends before its record and leaves polling stuck | Poll state updates after failure-reason loading; native and browser smokes exercise early identity rejection and an enabled retry control. |
| Server permits a new plan during live work | Transactional ticket-wide guard covers all plan IDs, active attempts, leases and candidate checks/review; waiting candidates may still be superseded. |
| Rebind leaves old authorization usable | Identity-changing rebind withdraws current manifest confirmation; approval/execution require reconfirmation. Append-only manifest history remains accessible. |
| Truncated diff says no changes | Client displays truncation, omitted-file information and drift. |
| Approver cannot see cumulative ticket usage | Ticket details display prior workflows, attempts, repairs, time and recorded/reserved cost before plan approval, including unpriced-usage caveats. |
| Identity recovery errors contain placeholders | Errors include concrete project/repository rebind routes; UI smoke verifies the actual route. |
| Restore can leave a partial database swap after process death | Durable restore intent rolls forward before SQLite opens; original database/sidecars remain preserved. Windows tests cover every move boundary and installation-before-finalization. This is process-interruption recovery, not hardware power-loss certification. |
| History paging loses selection and controls | Selection is reconciled with each page; browser test pages between completed and running sessions and checks cancellation controls. |
| Workflow replay accumulates full histories | Each bounded page is reduced and discarded before the next fetch; tests require reduction before subsequent reads and reject replay gaps. |

## Windows verification

Pinned Rust 1.90.0, Node 24.19.0, npm 11.9.0, Bun 1.4.3, Python 3.11,
and the installed Edge/WebView2 were used for project checks. The strict Pi-provenance installer intentionally uses npm bundled beside the pinned Node executable (11.17.0 in this distribution), with empty npm configuration, as required by the repository harness. Native testing ran the explicitly
hashed bundled Tauri executable built with `tauri build --debug --no-bundle`.
A plain debug Cargo build is not treated as bundled-client evidence.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rust workspace, all targets, serial test execution | 338 passed, 12 explicit ignores in the normal invocation |
| Explicit real component integration tests | 8 runtime tests, 1 component CLI test and 1 writer/reviewer source-drift test passed |
| Explicit storage history benchmark | 1 passed; 10,000 runs, indexed first 200 median 2.629 ms in this run |
| Remaining ignored test | 1 existing Windows-disabled large-index fixture requiring paths beyond MAX_PATH or about 90,000 files; not executed |
| Rust formatting and Clippy with warnings denied | Passed |
| Frontend/contracts/harness tests | 248 desktop, 36 API-client, 29 contracts, 10 guard, 8 pin and 7 harness checks passed |
| Type checking, frontend/native build and repository hygiene | Passed |
| M1 fixture / genuine provider | 19/19 synthetic; 20/20 genuine OpenRouter `openai/gpt-4.1` |
| Strict M3 fixture / genuine provider | 69/69 synthetic; final genuine run 59/61 (failed blocking-probe candidate creation; acceptance remains open) |
| MVP lifecycle and presentation | 64/64 browser; 62/62 bundled native WebView2 |
| Actual Missions/Atlas/Beacon UI workflows | 23/23 browser; 27/27 bundled native; real CLIs and checks, synthetic Pi |
| Large-history browser | 10,000 events, 200 visible rows, no idle event-DOM mutations; payload expansion, append/paging, selected-run controls, both themes at minimum width and disconnect passed |
| Copied-data upgrade and live-data preservation | Passed as described above |

Strict M3 checks bind the runtime to clean build inputs and the pinned compiler;
verify the installed Pi tree against a fresh integrity-checked lockfile install;
exercise exact approval, scoped changes, failing checks, independent review,
repair budgets, cancellation, hard-kill recovery and shutdown; preserve both
checkouts; drain the Windows-owned descendants; and scan artifacts for credentials.
The strict fixture run passed all 69 checks with zero leaks or unreadable files.
The final genuine run at `631ed21f12a7a05ff60c8623624c04605e218e20` passed feature, manual repair with fresh checks/review, cancellation, restart, preservation, cleanup and leak-scan checks. Its blocking-review scenario produced no writer change, so Luuna correctly failed that attempt without a candidate; the independent-review/automatic-repair probe was not reached in that invocation. Both the scenario assertion and its prerequisite failed, yielding 59/61. The leak scan found zero credential leaks, unreadable files or incomplete traversal. This is **not** a passing complete genuine-provider M3 run.

## Reproduction and evidence locations

Use pinned Node/npm first on PATH, and an isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; do not
replace the installed executable while it is running. Commands actually used:

```powershell
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked -- --test-threads=1
cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --locked -p luuna-components --test real -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --test writer -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo test --locked -p luuna-storage --test history -- --ignored --nocapture
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run tauri --workspace @luuna/desktop -- build --debug --no-bundle --ci -- --locked
node scripts/check-hygiene.mjs
node scripts/performance-ui-smoke.mjs --browser '<installed Edge executable>'
node scripts/m1-smoke.mjs --mode fixture --runtime '<isolated runtime>' --out '<new directory>'
.\scripts\with-windows-provider.ps1 -Smoke m1 -Model 'openai/gpt-4.1' -Runtime '<isolated runtime>' -Out '<new directory>'
node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode fixture --out '<new directory>'
.\scripts\with-windows-provider.ps1 -Smoke m3 -Model 'openai/gpt-4.1' -Out '<new directory>'
node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime '<isolated runtime>' --out '<new directory>'
node scripts/mvp-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime '<isolated runtime>' --native '<bundled desktop>' --out '<new directory>'
node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime '<isolated runtime>' --out '<new directory>'
node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime '<isolated runtime>' --native '<bundled desktop>' --out '<new directory>'
```

Private logs are under `.luuna/verification/pr11-windows` in the developer's home.
JSON/Markdown reports and UI images are in sibling `pr11-*` acceptance directories:
`pr11-m1-fixture`, `pr11-m1-real`, `pr11-m3-fixture-631ed21`,
`pr11-m3-real-631ed21`, `pr11-browser-ui-final`, `pr11-native-ui-final`,
`pr11-browser-components-final2` and `pr11-native-components-final2`.
Real transcripts, credentials, copied personal databases and private reports are
not committed. Only this sanitized evidence summary is tracked.

Earlier failures remain in those private logs. They exposed Windows path spelling,
hidden-file fixture writes and stale harness assumptions: a fixed idle-poll
sleep shorter than the new poll interval; a restart waiting for pipe closure
before reviewer reconciliation; replanning without the supersede checkbox; and matching only the older no-candidate wording rather than checking the failed second attempt.
The final tests exercise the corrected paths. The M3 rerun observed SIGKILL process
exit while stderr was still open, then required the log to drain after the reviewer
exited. Final cleanup/leak gates were retained. The normal parallel Rust attempt
hit timing-sensitive writer waits under concurrent Windows load; the complete
serial suite passed. A rebuild attempted while a disposable test runtime was
running hit Windows' executable lock and was rerun after that service stopped.

Two earlier genuine M3 attempts also recorded model-generated Python syntax errors during manual repair. The first passed 61/62 checks; the second passed 60/62, including the outdated no-change assertion as its other failure. Luuna failed those candidates before review. The reports remain available; No complete genuine-provider M3 invocation passed every check in this session, and the final successful manual repair does not establish that model repairs always succeed.

This establishes the listed Windows scenarios, not universal failure-freedom,
signed installation, newly tested cold bootstrap, Mac/Linux acceptance on these
commits, or full-v1 completion. The native bootstrap code was unchanged and its
prior platform evidence remains historical. No merge was performed during the
verification. PR 11 was merged into `main` afterwards (`bf538cc`), and this
report records no testing after the merge.
