# Windows development setup and verification

## PR 11 follow-up: current acceptance status

See [PR 11 Windows verification](PR-11-WINDOWS-VERIFICATION.md) for the review
fixes, 349 passing Rust checks including explicit integration/benchmark runs,
passing native/browser and fixture suites, and preservation evidence. Strict
genuine-provider M3 is still open: the final clean-revision run passed 59/61,
with no candidate produced for its blocking-review probe. One existing Windows
large-index stress fixture remains skipped. The installed build was preserved;
PR 11 was not merged or deployed. The successful earlier results below remain
historical evidence for their stated revisions.


Date: October 21, 2026. This is Windows evidence, separate from the historical
Linux reports and the original documentation validation report.

## Strict M3 harness portability follow-up

The clean-revision fixture attempt on performance commit `839e46a` passed all
workflow scenarios but only 65/68 total assertions. Windows had no harness-wide
descendant owner, making the final leak scan untrusted. The ignored-file audit
also exceeded its byte bound because Git collapsed `.tools/` into one ignored
parent and the documented dependency exclusions were not applied recursively.

The harness now starts under `scripts/windows-m3-job.py`: a fresh kill-on-close
Job Object owns Node before it resumes, including detached descendants and
descendants of a hard-killed runtime. Before scanning artifacts, the helper
verifies membership on opened handles, stops owned survivors and waits for the
job to contain only the harness and its short-lived inspection helper. Missing
ownership or failure to drain remains a failed acceptance check. Tests cover
detached grandchildren, breakaway requests, supervisor death, an unrelated
live process and missing ownership. This is test-process ownership, not a
sandbox or a change to approval/runtime policy.

Ignored-file hashing now applies the existing target/node_modules/dist
exclusion at every depth, while retaining other ignored configuration and the
original entry/byte/depth bounds. Git metadata and fixture snapshots retain
every file by default. `npm run test:smoke-harness` covers both fixes; results
from fresh committed acceptance runs are recorded separately below.

### Strict M3 acceptance result

Both strict suites passed on clean commit
`974ff0e464919055c9566a1b3daf25565a98d55c` after the performance changes were
committed as `839e46a`. Fixture mode passed **68/68** assertions; genuine
OpenRouter / `openai/gpt-4.1` mode passed **61/61**. Each invocation built its
own runtime from the recorded revision with pinned Rust 1.90.0 and ran with
Node 24.19.0. Real mode verified all 16,480 installed Pi tree entries against
a fresh integrity-checked install of the tracked lockfile (Pi 1.3.0).

Coverage includes exact approval, a scoped feature, failing checks followed by
manual repair and fresh independent review, blocking findings with bounded
automatic repair, in-flight review cancellation, hard-kill/restart recovery,
conservative spend reservation and orderly authenticated shutdown. The real
blocking probe produced no fresh repair candidate and correctly paused with
repair closed; it was not counted as a successfully implemented requirement.
Fixture mode additionally exercises malformed review output and re-validation.
Both runs preserved the developer and Luuna checkout audits, drained owned
Windows descendants, and completed their artifact scans with zero credential
leaks or unreadable files. Windows uses checked paths rather than Linux's held
directory handles; this recorded platform distinction remains unchanged.

Reproduction from a clean checkout, with pinned Node first on PATH and an
existing DPAPI-saved provider configuration:

```powershell
node scripts/m3-smoke.mjs --mode fixture --out "$env:USERPROFILE/.luuna/verification/strict-m3-fixture-974ff0e"
.\scripts\with-windows-provider.ps1 -Smoke m3 -Model 'openai/gpt-4.1' -Out "$env:USERPROFILE/.luuna/verification/strict-m3-real-974ff0e"
```

Use new, empty output directories when repeating these commands. Private
`report.json` and `report.md` files are retained in those directories; no real
transcripts or credentials are committed. `npm test` also passed: 24 contract,
6 scope-guard, 8 component-pin, 5 smoke-harness, 221 desktop and 28 API-client
checks. JavaScript syntax, repository hygiene and diff checks passed. The
acceptance results identify the code revision above; the subsequent evidence
documentation commit does not change executable code or harness behavior.

This closes strict Windows M3 acceptance for these scenarios. It does not
establish signed installation, packaged service supervision, other operating
systems or full-v1 completion. The installed optimized app/runtime were not
replaced by the disposable acceptance builds.

## Latest result: merged design system and component workflows

The component work was combined with current `main` and its desktop design
system in [PR 10](https://github.com/brodynelly/luuna/pull/10). The rebuilt
native frontend passed 27 component and 55 lifecycle/presentation checks,
including both colour schemes. Browser checks passed 23 component and 57
lifecycle/presentation assertions, including 760 px layout. Pinned Node 24.19.0
checks exposed and verified a Windows verbatim-path/junction scope-guard fix.
The final runtime passed 185 Rust tests with 10 explicit ignores, formatting
and Clippy, and was restored with existing state and credentials. See
[the complete accounting and artifact identities](MAIN-INTEGRATION-2026-10-21.md).

## Earlier result: component integration and final development upgrade

The final component-enabled runtime was installed and started on October 21,
2026 after the user chose unsigned development and switched Smart App Control
Off in Windows Security. Existing saved history, token, data directory and
encrypted provider bytes were preserved. The normal desktop is connected.

The final runtime SHA-256 is
`99d9521784bc373237ef4d65b3bdd6189f3290faf557fad2946705f39d890256`;
the bundled desktop SHA-256 is
`21ddca8c75b1bb709bcd2886b6362e809b6d8aa6cc048447f94df74ce2591f4f`.
Actual native WebView2 checks passed **27/27 component workflows**, **46/46
lifecycle/recovery checks** and **17/17 automatic startup checks**. Component
CLIs and Git/unittest checks were real; Pi writer/reviewer fixture sessions were
synthetic. See the [final evidence](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md#final-windows-native-verification-and-completed-development-upgrade)
and [component workflow guide](COMPONENT-WORKFLOWS.md). No new genuine-provider
component workflow or signed installer is claimed.

## Earlier result: automatic native startup and connection

Before remote publication, the final Windows tree passed `cargo test --locked
--workspace` (**174 tests**), root Rust formatting and Clippy with warnings denied,
native formatting/Clippy and its one contract test, `npm test`, frontend
typechecking/build, PowerShell/JavaScript syntax and repository hygiene checks.
The first root test invocation hit the running executable's Windows file lock;
the idle service was stopped through the authenticated API, the full suite
passed, and the service was restored with its existing state and credentials.
No new provider requests were made for these publication checks.

The native app now starts or authenticates/reuses the independent Windows
runtime and connects on launch or reload without copying a token (ADR 0011).
`node scripts/windows-native-startup-smoke.mjs` passed **17/17 checks** in the
actual bundled WebView2 app. It proved warm PID reuse, normal WM_CLOSE, cold
startup after explicit shutdown, refusal of a foreign listener before any HTTP
request, automatic retry, reload, concurrent windows using one runtime,
disconnect/reconnect, preserved data/history and unchanged encrypted provider
bytes. Browser local/session storage stayed empty. The test launched from a
different working directory. All test windows closed normally and the runtime
remained healthy.

The final normal executable was then opened without debugging flags and its
actual window reported `Local runtime connected`, with the existing reviewed
workflow history. It was left open. Native binary SHA-256:
`36e00f6e0d12c73163f316efce6f23a9d9e1afc2ea3adfe66a2b3ed67403c843`.
The private report and screenshot are in
`%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\verification\native-startup-846e1ffd`.

The browser fixture regression passed **46/46**, including approval, writer,
candidate/review, shutdown interruption and recovery. Evidence is in
`%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\checks\auto-browser-1c6b3ca0`. The first attempt lacked
Playwright's bundled Chromium; the passing retry used the installed Edge through
`LUUNA_CHROMIUM`. No browser installation was needed. Earlier native startup
attempts are preserved: the first exposed string-error display, the next two
exposed Windows descendants retaining a pipe handle. Native startup now consumes
a bounded JSON line with a reply timeout instead of waiting for runtime-lifetime
EOF. Neither failure was counted as successful startup evidence.

The complete native fixture workflow also passed **46/46** on the same binary,
including wrong-token refusal, baseline, exact approval, writer, candidate
diff/checks, independent review/re-validation, crash recovery, explicit shutdown
and conservative interrupted-review spend. Its report is in
`%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\checks\auto-native-0357fa93`. The harness now waits for
automatic startup to settle and explicitly disconnects its test view before
switching to the isolated fixture runtime. The preceding attempt,
`auto-native-10dc1b93`, passed 44/48: its four failures were unreliable WebView2
CDP Tab/Enter delivery after that switch. Native coverage now exercises the
actual skip-link click/focus target and native form controls; browser coverage
retains the four keyboard assertions. No native keyboard-only claim is made.

Affected-code checks passed: `cargo test --manifest-path
apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --locked` (one native contract test), native
`cargo clippy ... --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, native `cargo fmt`,
the locked bundled Tauri build, `npm test` (20 schema, 6 guard, 16 desktop and
22 API-client checks), `npm run typecheck`, PowerShell parsing, JS syntax and
`git diff --check`. Root runtime Rust tests were not repeated for this client
change; their preceding shutdown evidence remains below. No new provider request
was needed for this startup change. Signed installation and Windows service
supervision remain separate work.

## Previous result: shutdown and native desktop

The three prior Windows shutdown failures are resolved by the authenticated
service-stop path in ADR 0010. `windows-shutdown-ui-1` passed 46/46 browser
checks; `windows-native-ui-2` passed 48/48 inside the actual bundled Tauri
WebView2 window. Both exercised shutdown during checks, exit code zero,
interruption with the shutdown reason, restart and fresh validation. The native
test also verified runtime independence after terminating its test client.
Keyboard-only form entry remains browser evidence: native WebView2 CDP input
needed DOM filling for the fixture URL/token. The first native run's input
delivery failure is retained in `windows-native-ui-1`.

`windows-shutdown-m1-real-1` passed all 20 genuine OpenRouter/Pi connectivity
checks, including authenticated clean shutdown. The full final Windows Rust
suite passed 173 tests; a subsequent idle-SSE shutdown regression also passed
with all 12 runtime API tests. The stream now closes on service stop even when
its workflow is idle, preventing it from holding HTTP shutdown open. Formatting,
Clippy with warnings denied, npm tests and TypeScript checks passed. One
pre-existing test needed to reopen the service
after shutdown: rescheduling in the stopped instance now correctly returns 503.

The native build succeeded on a normal retry and the supported Tauri build
command below. No Application Control policy or security setting was changed.
The packaged frontend no longer contains Chromium's rejected IPv6 CSP source.
Normal launch uses no WebView2 remote-debugging flag; the temporary debugging
endpoint is restricted to test-owned WebView2 profiles and ends with the test.

Previous native executable: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/luuna-desktop.exe`,
SHA-256 `7e959837b19fdfce7a1f5fd96c3f2cf0812567f4107dfa98a88e544f30e801bd`.
Final runtime SHA-256: `066ffb05758ef2ed263137cfaf4a219bf82167d7562cede3d7ba43ff07b403b5`.
A normal native app and the independent updated runtime were left running on
the prior diagnostic data, with its two reviewed real-provider candidates.

The explicit Windows stop script was exercised: the runtime exited cleanly and
the native window remained alive. Repeated native launches reused the same
client and verified runtime rather than duplicating processes. The launcher
refuses a different data directory while a runtime is live. A separate attempt
to test normal Alt+F4 closure was blocked by detected human input; no normal
window-close result is claimed from that attempt. Credential files and earlier
evidence were preserved. Signed installers, installed Windows service
supervision, arbitrary descendant containment/job objects, the backup/migration
drill and strict clean-revision M3 acceptance remain separate open work.

## Run locally

From this checkout in PowerShell:

```powershell
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix tools/pi
cargo build --locked -p luuna-runtime
npm run tauri --workspace @luuna/desktop -- build --debug --no-bundle --ci -- --locked
powershell.exe -NoProfile -STA -File scripts/set-windows-provider.ps1
powershell.exe -NoProfile -STA -File scripts/start-windows.ps1 -Native
```

After setup, double-click `Configure Luuna.cmd` to replace the key, or
`Start Luuna.cmd` to open the native development app; `Stop Luuna.cmd` requests
authenticated orderly runtime shutdown without closing the client. A second
native launch reuses the verified service/window; unrecognized occupied ports
are refused. Omitting `-Native` launches the Vite/browser client. During this verification
the launcher was given the successful diagnostic's existing data directory, so
the running client can inspect the two genuinely reviewed fixture workflows.

The first window accepts a masked OpenRouter, OpenAI, or Anthropic API key.
It encrypts the value with Windows DPAPI for the current account in
`%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\credentials\provider.json`. Existing encrypted
LocalAppData records are copied once when the new files are absent; originals
are retained. No plaintext key is saved in
the repository. Saving a key does not call a provider. Same-account processes
can decrypt DPAPI data; this is storage protection, not a sandbox.

The native app starts the runtime independently and connects automatically; no
connection dialog or token entry is needed. You can also open the built
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/luuna-desktop.exe` directly from Explorer.
The app depends on this checkout and its built runtime, Node and pinned Pi
dependencies. Explicit Disconnect stays disconnected until you choose Connect
automatically or reopen/reload the app. Browser mode at
`http://127.0.0.1:1420` retains the masked token/Copy dialog and manual form.
The runtime address is `http://127.0.0.1:4242`. Closing either client leaves the
runtime running. Private metadata and encrypted token are in
`%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\credentials\connection.json`; logs are in `.luuna/logs`.
After replacing a provider key, explicitly stop and restart the runtime to load
the new key. A warm app launch preserves the current service configuration.

Runtime data uses `%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\windows`. A Store-packaged host can
redirect LocalAppData into a substantially longer package path. With this
machine's Python 3.11, long candidate paths caused unittest discovery to report
zero tests, or explicit module import to fail. The runtime blocked these
results correctly. Keep runtime worktree paths short; long-path compatibility
across arbitrary tools is not established.

The defaults are OpenRouter `openai/gpt-4.1-mini`, OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini`, and
Anthropic `claude-sonnet-4-5`. Only the OpenRouter profile was exercised here.
The API accepts per-action provider/model overrides; the others are setup
choices, not verified provider claims.

## Earlier Windows pass, before the shutdown/native fixes

- A genuine Pi 1.3.0/OpenRouter response streamed through the Windows runtime.
  Authentication refusal, replay, cancellation with Pi reaping, invalid-model
  failure, restart interruption, history retention and exclusive data ownership
  passed the M1 smoke. Its orderly-shutdown signal check failed.
- The current-tree real-provider diagnostic passed 16/16 checks on its seventh
  run: actual Python baseline; missing-approval refusal; exact-plan approval;
  a real scoped writer; stale-candidate refusal; required commands; a fresh
  independent reviewer; deliberate failing check; manual repair revision;
  fresh checks/review; and unchanged fixture developer checkout.
- Browser fixture testing exercised import/discovery, baseline, acknowledgment
  before approval, candidate diff/logs, invalid review and re-validation,
  crash/reconnect recovery, reserved spend after interrupted review,
  keyboard controls and accessibility checks. It is synthetic model evidence.
- Root npm tests, frontend type checking and production web build passed.
  Component CLI suites were not rerun and those tools remain unintegrated.

Final checks on the changed working tree: `cargo test --locked --workspace`
passed 172 Windows tests (Unix-only tests are excluded); `cargo clippy --locked
--workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
passed. `npm test` passed 20 schema checks, 6 scope-guard tests, 13 desktop tests
and 22 API-client tests; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` passed. Hygiene,
JavaScript syntax, PowerShell parsing and `git diff --check` passed. Host tools
were Rust 1.90.0, Node 26.10.0, npm 11.19.1, Python 3.11.9 and Git 2.55.0.windows.5;
Node/npm were the existing newer supported tools, not the recorded Linux pins.

The final browser fixture smoke (`windows-ui-20261021-3`) passed 43/46 checks.
Its only failures were the three orderly-shutdown assertions. Registration,
baseline, exact approval, writer/diff, check logs, fresh review/re-validation,
crash recovery, reserved-spend refusal and keyboard/accessibility checks passed.
The service and client were then launched separately: authenticated history
showed two `reviewed` workflows and the `completed` baseline, the web client
returned HTTP 200, and a visible `Luuna` browser window and connection dialog
were observed. The running service executable was this checkout's
`target\debug\luuna-runtime.exe`, SHA-256
`23b1b136983f01e0f71afd5bb62c796828071b4fc5eaffb71ab17d6cd446d11d`.

Private diagnostic artifacts are under `LocalAppData\Luuna\verification`.
The successful real diagnostic is `windows-workflow-real-20261021-7/report.json`.
It records binary/source identity and the separate short runtime-data directory.
Earlier failed runs are retained. This diagnostic allows the explicitly dirty
working tree and is not a substitute for strict M3 acceptance.

Reproduce a current-tree real-provider diagnostic after saving a key:

```powershell
.\scripts\with-windows-provider.ps1 -Smoke windows-workflow -Out C:\path\to\new-report-directory
```

The diagnostic uses disposable fixture repositories and a bounded approved
budget for each scenario. It makes provider requests and can incur charges.
Secrets are decrypted only into the child process environment and restored
afterward. Do not commit its output or real session artifacts.

## Fixes and open issues

1. Fixed the scope guard's comparison of Rust verbatim Windows paths and Pi's
   ordinary paths. Genuine reviewers previously rejected their own worktree.
   The new Windows test retains junction-escape and read-only enforcement.
2. Scope tests use Windows directory junctions instead of privileged symlink
   creation. No system privilege or security setting was changed.
3. Browser smoke starts Vite through Node, avoiding direct `.cmd` spawning,
   and matches registered Git identity across Windows path virtualization.
4. M3 harness Git configuration uses `NUL` on Windows, rather than Node's
   `\\.\nul`, which Git rejected. The strict harness has not passed on Windows;
   Linux-only descendant containment and clean-revision evidence remain gaps.
5. Shutdown probes now require exit code zero before claiming orderly shutdown.
   Node SIGTERM/SIGINT kills on Windows did not exercise the runtime Ctrl+C
   handler. Native console-control/service supervision remains to be proved.
6. The initial native Tauri build was blocked by Windows Application Control when executing
   a generated `generic-array` build script (OS error 4551). The later normal
   retry and native GUI proof are recorded above. Installer success remains
   unproved; no policy setting was bypassed or changed.
7. The Rust reviewer-timeout test had a host-timing assumption: candidate-stage
   time need not consume eight seconds when writer/startup spent more of the
   aggregate budget. It now checks the actual exhausted-budget repair refusal.
8. Windows executor descendant ownership/job objects, backup/migration drill,
   native service packaging, component integration, TUI, multi-repository work
   and publication remain unverified or unimplemented as previously documented.

The native process checks retain host permissions. A green fixture run does
not establish provider behavior or operating-system containment.

title: Component workflows in Luuna
description: The application uses the pinned public luuna-missions, luuna-atlas and luuna-beacon sources through runtime adapters. See [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-work
text:
# Component workflows in Luuna

The application uses the pinned public luuna-missions, luuna-atlas and luuna-beacon sources through runtime adapters. See [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md) for authority and recovery rules.

## Use the application

1. After a fresh checkout, run `npm ci` and `npm run components:setup`. Build the runtime with `cargo build --locked -p luuna-runtime`, then start or restart that build. The application reports unavailable tools rather than substituting another ticket or memory authority.
2. Open a registered project and select **Enable components**. This explicitly creates private managed component stores and migrates existing tickets while preserving their IDs. Retry the same activation after an interrupted migration. The runtime blocks project mutations while activation is incomplete.
3. Create a ticket in the existing workflow panel. Its source is Missions. After an external CLI edit, refresh its source status and reconcile the displayed expected revision before making a new plan. Old approvals do not transfer to a changed ticket revision.
4. In the component panel, create project/process memory with explicit provenance, search it, and select only the records needed by this task. User memory remains excluded until the user-memory option is enabled and a record is explicitly selected. Delete requires the displayed source hash.
5. Create or preview a Beacon prompt. Updating its name uses the current expected version. Preview and select the current rendered version for the plan.
6. Create a plan. Review the full immutable plan, including selected memory content/provenance and prompt body. Approve its exact hash before implementation. The runtime checks the source again at approval, implementation, repair and validation/review boundaries. A changed or deleted selected resource requires a new plan and approval.

Deleting memory removes its Atlas source from active retrieval and invalidates selected references. Existing immutable plans and private operation history retain their audit snapshots; complete retention/erasure policy remains a full-v1 obligation.

Existing projects stay on the clearly labelled temporary ticket source until activated. No personal component store, imported task history, Pi configuration or unrelated memory is automatically loaded into a worker. The private source workspace is shown in component status; direct CLI work must use that workspace explicitly.

## Current API

All routes are authenticated under `/api/v1`.

| Method and route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET/POST /projects/{id}/components` | Inspect or explicitly activate/migrate the managed stores. |
| `GET /projects/{id}/memory?include_user=true&q=...` | Search bound records; `include_user` defaults to false. |
| `POST /projects/{id}/memory` | `{idempotency_key, scope, content, provenance}`; scope is project/process/user. |
| `DELETE /projects/{id}/memory/{id}?expected_hash=...` | Optimistic, idempotent deletion; source changes refuse deletion. |
| `GET/POST /projects/{id}/prompts` | List or create/update `{idempotency_key, name, body, expected_version?}`. Missing/zero expected version creates; positive version updates. |
| `GET /projects/{id}/prompts/{name}/render?version=N` | Current-version preview with rendered body and canonical resource hash. Stale versions are refused. |
| `GET /tickets/{id}/source` | Observe source identity/revision and reconciliation need. Ticket GET/list retains the last reconciled projection. |
| `POST /tickets/{id}/reconcile` | `{expected_revision}`; source changes advance the projection and stale old plans. |

Plan creation accepts optional `component_context: {memory_ids: string[], prompt?: {name,version,hash}}`. The resulting plan stores exact approved snapshots as `component_context: {memory: [{id,scope,hash,content,provenance}], prompt: {name,version,hash,body} | null}`. At most sixteen memories and 16,000 encoded bytes of combined resources are accepted. Omitting the optional field preserves older canonical plan hashes.

Operation keys persist across uncertain responses; retries with a different payload are refused. Missing source identity after an attempted create is reported for reconciliation rather than blindly repeated. Prompt source records, inherited sources and configured schemas contribute to the hash; schemas must validate without warnings. External CLI writes cannot be made atomic with a SQLite transaction, so later boundaries recheck source freshness.

## Reproduce focused verification

```
cargo test --locked -p luuna-components --test real -- --ignored --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib missions_real_ -- --ignored --nocapture
cargo test --locked -p luuna-runtime --lib components_real_ -- --ignored --nocapture
node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --runtime <fresh-runtime-binary> --browser <chromium-or-edge> --out <new-test-directory>
node scripts/m6-ui-smoke.mjs --native <bundled-desktop-executable> --runtime <fresh-runtime-binary> --runtime-label <build-identity> --out <new-test-directory>
```

The smoke uses disposable Git repositories, private component stores, free loopback ports and its own token. Browser mode uses a test-owned proxy. Windows native mode loads the bundled Tauri frontend in WebView2 and exercises production CORS directly. Native mode first verifies automatic connection to the existing local service, then disconnects and selects the isolated fixture service; it repeats this after reload. It requires a configured local development service but makes no provider calls. It closes only its own test window and verifies that the independent fixture runtime survives before authenticated shutdown. Both modes exercise actual component CLIs and real Git/check commands while using explicitly synthetic Pi writer/reviewer sessions. Fixture screenshots contain synthetic data. See [FOUNDATION-STATUS.md](FOUNDATION-STATUS.md#runtime-component-workflows-october-21-2026) for observed results and remaining platform/provider coverage.

## Current verification and Windows development startup

The [recorded Windows browser run](evidence/component-workflows-2026-10-21.json) passed all 23 assertions with actual pinned component CLIs and synthetic Pi writer/reviewer sessions. The final Rust workspace passed 196 tests, plus separate real-component suites. The final runtime subsequently passed [27 native component workflow checks](evidence/native-component-workflows-2026-10-21.json), [46 bundled native lifecycle/recovery checks](evidence/native-lifecycle-2026-10-21.json) and [17 automatic native startup checks](evidence/native-startup-2026-10-21.json). These exercise the actual Tauri WebView2 frontend; synthetic Pi sessions remain explicitly synthetic.

The earlier Application Control block and rollback are retained in the historical evidence. The user explicitly chose unsigned development and turned Smart App Control Off in Windows Security; the observed policy state changed from 1 to 0. The exact previously blocked final runtime was then installed and started successfully. Its SHA-256 is `99d9521784bc373237ef4d65b3bdd6189f3290faf557fad2946705f39d890256`. All three existing saved runs, the token, data directory and encrypted provider bytes were preserved. Project activation has not been forced in personal data. Signed distribution and broader platform/provider acceptance remain separate requirements.

title: Current Luuna architecture
description: Windows native development startup invokes a fixed local bootstrap command, starts or authenticates/reuses the independent runtime and connects without manual token entry
text:
# Current Luuna architecture

Windows native development startup invokes a fixed local bootstrap command,
starts or authenticates/reuses the independent runtime and connects without
manual token entry. DPAPI records live in `%USERPROFILE%\.luuna\credentials`;
existing encrypted LocalAppData records migrate once without deleting them.
Tokens reach the view through local IPC and stay in memory. Closing the window
leaves the service running. See [ADR 0011](decisions/0011-windows-native-bootstrap.md)
for the command boundary, reconciliation and checkout-based distribution limits.

Date: 2026-10-16, updated 2026-10-17 for M2a, M2b, M2c and the M3 implementation, and 2026-10-21 for re-validation after a review that left no verdict, shutdown interruption, client hardening the desktop design system and explicit component runtime workflows. Status: authoritative foundation baseline; implementation evidence is required for each milestone.

## Purpose and precedence

Luuna is a local-first development workbench for one developer working across related repositories. Its runtime coordinates scoped Pi sessions, exact-plan approval, actual checks, independent review, durable evidence, and eventually linked pull requests. The developer decides when to merge.

For new work, apply the following order:

1. Explicit current user requirements and repository-wide safety/security rules.
2. This document and accepted records in `docs/decisions/`; a later accepted decision must update this summary.
3. `docs/02-requirements.md` for full-v1 functional requirements not explicitly revised here.
4. The desktop/Pi RPC proposal for detailed design rationale.
5. The numbered design chapters, complete reference reading copies, diagrams, and examples as historical material.

README and AI-START-HERE are entry points, not alternative specifications. Existing source and tests show implemented behavior; they do not silently override a requirement. When an implementation differs, record the gap or an explicit decision.

## Delivery and boundaries

Runtime I/O isolation and bounded session history follow
[ADR 0015](decisions/0015-bounded-runtime-and-history.md): synchronous transactions
run under bounded blocking admission, SSE reads in pages, and the desktop keeps
a bounded live event window with on-demand historical navigation. Check progress
is lossy display data; private artifacts and durable runtime events remain the
evidence. Windows check processes join owned Job Objects before execution.

The initial client is Tauri 2 with React and TypeScript. An independent Rust service uses Tokio, an authenticated Axum API, and local SQLite persistence. Pi RPC subprocesses execute agent assignments. A client cannot directly authorize tools or decide that validation succeeded.

```text
Tauri/React client ── authenticated HTTP + resumable SSE ── Rust runtime
                                                          ├── SQLite + private artifacts
                                                          ├── supervised Pi RPC workers
                                                          ├── Git/worktree ownership
                                                          ├── deterministic check executor
                                                          └── versioned external adapters
```

Desktop-first is a sequencing decision. Browser/TUI capability parity, multiple related repositories, scoped memory, and Mac/Windows support remain full-v1 obligations. They are not exit criteria for the first single-repository foundation demo. No hosted service, mandatory NAS, GPU, automatic merge, custom agent loop, or full IDE replacement is required.

The desktop client's presentation follows one token-based design system ([ADR 0013](decisions/0013-desktop-design-system.md), [DESIGN-SYSTEM.md](DESIGN-SYSTEM.md)): six outcome tones mapped from the API unions, where only passed evidence is green and interruption is never failure, both colour schemes and WCAG AA enforced by tests. It changes how runtime state is shown, never what the runtime decides.

Client parity (R02, A33) follows one capability catalog ([ADR 0020](decisions/0020-capability-catalog-and-tui.md)): `schemas/capability-catalog.json` lists every product action with its runtime route, `@luuna/api-client` method, desktop control marker and TUI command; `scripts/check-contracts.mjs` validates it against the runtime's served routes and the typed client. The failure explanations (`packages/api-client/src/failures.ts`) are shared by the desktop and the terminal client `packages/tui` (`luuna-tui`, interactive menus and a scriptable non-interactive mode, SSE event following with resumption, hidden token entry, full-hash approval acknowledgment). Parity evidence: the TUI command test, the desktop marker test and `scripts/tui-smoke.mjs`. Actions still arriving from M4/M5/M7 join the catalog as they land.

The workspace should add crates when they contain a real contract or implementation: domain, storage, runtime/API, engine/Pi, Git, executor, validation, and external adapters. Shared frontend packages are created when an actual shared consumer needs them. Empty placeholders do not establish implementation progress.

## Runtime ownership

Only the Rust runtime may enforce state transitions, immutable plan hashes, approval scope, execution permissions, task dependencies, limits, retries, candidate identity, check evidence, review acceptance, and publication gates. Agents provide proposals and worker output. Deterministic runtime code produces authoritative domain events.

An approval binds to the complete canonical executable plan, its revision and hash, repository scope, base commits, check recipes, resource profiles, and budgets. Feature implementation requires a valid approval and a passing baseline. New code, rebases, dependency changes, and manual edits invalidate affected evidence. Review and publication refer to exact candidates; model text saying “passed” is never command evidence. The desktop displays the entire immutable plan and full hash and requires acknowledgment before enabling approval. Managed Git checkout, status, staging and commit disable configured clean, smudge and process filters with per-command overrides; these operations do not authorize repository-configured commands.

Native execution uses host permissions. Stronger isolation requires an explicitly configured execution profile with actual operating-system or container boundaries. Preserve developer changes and only clean up resources whose Luuna ownership is verified.

## Persistence and ticket authority

SQLite owns Luuna projects, immutable plan revisions, approvals, run/attempt lifecycle, sequenced events, check/review evidence, artifact references, and publication reconciliation. State mutation and emitted durable domain events must be committed consistently. Sensitive transcripts and provider data remain private artifacts with controlled access and retention.

The schema is versioned and append-only. At startup the runtime refuses a database that fails SQLite's quick check or was written by a newer schema, before writing anything to it. It applies only missing migrations, after an automatic pre-migration snapshot under `<data>/backups/`. `luuna-runtime backup` takes a consistent online snapshot. `luuna-runtime restore` needs the runtime stopped, verifies the snapshot, and moves the current database and its `-wal`/`-shm` aside before installing it. `luuna-runtime check` reports integrity and schema version. A snapshot covers the database only; artifacts and worktrees are files, so a complete backup is the data directory copied after an orderly stop. Startup recovery skips records it cannot decode, logs them by table and ID, and still settles their state where it can. See [ADR 0016](decisions/0016-storage-backup-and-schema-compatibility.md).

Baselines are runs: `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/baselines` executes a repository's confirmed required recipes through the supervised executor and records `CheckResult` evidence bound to the manifest hash, exact commit and tree, and an environment fingerprint, with private hashed artifacts. `Implementing` is entered only through the transactional gate that re-checks the approval, the current manifest and a passed matching baseline per repository; see [ADR 0007](decisions/0007-baseline-executor.md). One baseline per repository runs at a time. Every check's process group is recorded; whatever a check leaves running is terminated before its result is recorded, and startup recovery terminates verified survivors of checks a hard-killed runtime left behind (Windows checks run in kill-on-close job objects). Missing tools or dependencies and checks cut short by the workflow budget are blocked infrastructure, never failures a repair is asked to fix (ADR 0007 amendment, 2026-10-21).

Projects are registered from existing repositories. The confirmed **project manifest** (`schemas/project.schema.json`, hashed with `luuna-json-v1`) is machine-independent and append-only by revision; the **machine registry** maps each repository ID to its local path and the identity observed at registration (the redacted configured remote plus the root commits reachable from HEAD). A later observation must show an equivalent remote and contain those roots; only an explicit, evented rebind changes a binding. A checkout is registered once and never overlaps the runtime data directory. Discovery proposals and project-scoped events (`project.registered`, `repository.registered`, `repository.rebound`, `discovery.proposed`, `manifest.confirmed`) are durable, and replaying the project stream reconstructs the confirmed map. Inspection never writes to a repository or executes its text, including filters configured in submodules; see [ADR 0006](decisions/0006-repository-import.md).

Discovery also probes the host once per proposal (`Discovery.host_capabilities`: each profile tool resolved on `PATH` and asked only for its version) and annotates every proposed check with `capability: available | missing` and its missing tools, raising a `missing-tool` question rather than dropping the recipe; a confirmed check whose tool is absent is recorded `blocked`, never `failed`. Every advertised profile (Node, React, Next.js, TypeScript, Go, Python, Rust, Flutter, native Android, native iOS) proposes real recipes; iOS and Android device recipes carry capabilities (`xcode`, `android-device`) this host cannot satisfy and say so. New projects are created only through a hashed `ScaffoldProposal` (`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold/propose`: files, baseline recipes, generator and network steps, tool probes, `ready | blocked`) that the developer confirms by exact hash (`POST /api/v1/projects/scaffold`): the runtime writes the files, commits, runs the baseline recipe through the supervised executor as a real check, registers the project and records `project.scaffolded`; a failing baseline is returned as such and never reported passing. Android and iOS scaffolds are blocked proposals naming their platform generators. See [ADR 0019](decisions/0019-stack-profiles-and-scaffolding.md); capable-runner evidence for Go, Flutter, Android and iOS remains open.

Legacy projects retain the explicitly temporary SQLite ticket source until component activation. `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/components` durably initializes the private component workspace and migrates tickets while preserving IDs and numeric revisions. Enabled projects use Missions (Seeds-derived) as authority for ticket intent, acceptance criteria, status, dependencies and source fingerprints; SQLite stores its revision-aware projection and Luuna execution state. GET/list return the last reconciled projection; `GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}/source` reports actual source freshness and `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/reconcile` requires the expected projection revision. External edits advance the reconciled revision and invalidate stale plans; freshness, ticket readiness and dependencies are rechecked at runtime work/evidence boundaries. Missing components fail closed. There are never two independently writable authorities for these fields. See [ADR 0003](decisions/0003-ticket-authority.md) and [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md).

## Pi and maintained components

Pi is the agent engine, not the scheduler or validation authority. The engine contract supervises process creation, assignments, followups, events, stop requests, inspection, and disposal. Use a tested pinned release, strict JSONL framing, command correlation, bounded buffers, timeouts, and owned child-process cleanup. Stderr is diagnostic data. Prompt acceptance and agent settlement are separate events. Persist attempts so interrupted processes cannot become successful runs after restart.

Luuna maintains three branded CLI distributions: **Missions** (`@luuna/missions-cli`, Seeds-derived), **Atlas** (`@luuna/atlas-cli`, Mulch-derived), and **Beacon** (`@luuna/beacon-cli`, Canopy-derived). They live under `components/missions`, `components/atlas`, and `components/beacon` as separate package and integration boundaries. Preserve compatible underlying APIs/data formats, upstream copyright and MIT notices. Prefer adapters over rewrites or direct SQLite access to their records.

The owner resumed extraction on October 21, 2026 and explicitly authorized public component repositories. Missions, Atlas and Beacon now live in `brodynelly/luuna-missions`, `brodynelly/luuna-atlas` and `brodynelly/luuna-beacon`; Luuna stays private and consumes exact-commit Git submodules at the existing components paths. The manifest and gitlinks bind dependency identity; setup uses frozen Bun locks without lifecycle scripts, and consumer smoke checks exercise real CLI/JSON operations. Each destination owns its CI and source; registry packages remain private and unpublished. See [ADR 0012](decisions/0012-independent-component-repositories.md), superseding ADR 0002's hosted-extraction deferral.

The runtime now invokes these pinned CLIs through `luuna-components` with bounded input/output, a fixed stdin bridge, isolated HOME/config, sanitized environment, source/toolchain verification and owned process cleanup. Explicit per-project activation uses `<data_dir>/components/projects/<id>`; explicit user memory uses `<data_dir>/components/user`. It never adopts developer or imported stores. Atlas memory exposes explicit scope and provenance; Beacon exposes versioned prompt preview/update. A user selects resources for a plan, whose canonical optional `component_context` contains their exact snapshots, identities and hashes. The runtime rejects changed selected sources at approval and execution/evidence boundaries and gives workers only approved bounded content. Durable intent ledgers reconcile uncertain component writes before retry. Imported development metadata is not runtime data or permission to load instructions into agents. See [ADR 0014](decisions/0014-runtime-component-workflows.md) for activation, ticket reconciliation, resource selection and native-process limits. Memory promotion widens scope one step at a time (`process -> project -> user`) through `POST …/memory/{id}/promote` with the displayed hash, creating the wider record with provenance naming its origin and deleting the narrower one under the same intent ledger; `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/export` returns the manifest, ticket projections, project and process memory and current prompts, and is refused outright when it would carry user memory, a credential value or a path of this host ([ADR 0021](decisions/0021-memory-promotion-and-project-export.md)). Import of an export, retention policy and supported-platform evidence remain obligations.

## Candidate validation and review

Migration 5 stores exact candidate commit/tree identities, append-only validation generations and structured independent reviews. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/validate` names the expected hash and optionally `auto_repair`; it executes the approved required recipes inside the owned candidate worktree and starts a fresh read-only Pi reviewer only after the checks pass. Checks and reviews cannot be reused across candidate revisions or interrupted generations. A `failed` candidate whose required checks all passed in its current generation and whose reviewer left no verdict (invalid or self-inconsistent output, a refused session) may re-enter validation in place as generation `n+1`: same revision, approval and budgets, fresh checks and a fresh reviewer, no writer attempt; `GET …/candidate` reports that decision as `revalidate_allowed`. `GET …/candidate` and `GET …/diff` expose authoritative evidence and exact diffs; `POST …/repair` rechecks current approval, baseline/host and remaining aggregate budgets before creating the next scoped candidate. Model output never supplies command evidence. Repair writers receive the previous candidate's reason, check records, review and a bounded tail of each failed check log, never the private artifact paths. See [ADR 0009](decisions/0009-candidate-validation-review.md).

Since the second 2026-10-21 amendment to ADR 0009, every validation generation starts from the candidate tree alone: the owned worktree is verified and its untracked and ignored paths are removed and recorded. Content drift fails the candidate with a reason naming the change and the next step and is never re-validated in place. Review diffs ignore attributes that hide changes and are bounded with every changed path listed; a non-passing review must name a finding; reviewer tool calls are recorded by tool and path. `GET …/candidate` reports `validate_allowed` and `decision_reasons` from the gates the routes apply.

Automatic repair is opt-in and bounded by both the immutable plan and project repair policy. Infrastructure errors stop without repeated edits. Interrupted check and review stages retain elapsed usage up to their last durable heartbeat; a reviewer interrupted after its durable prompt marker, and every interrupted writer, reserve unknown spend and require re-planning when headroom is exhausted. Clients see aggregate workflow usage against the plan budgets and cumulative per-ticket usage, including spend the provider reported without a price. Review success is evidence for an exact candidate only; publication and human-controlled merge remain separate gates.

## Multi-repository coordination

A plan may carry several tasks, each on a distinct registered repository, with `depends_on` naming the tasks that must complete first; the contract refuses self, unknown, duplicate and cyclic dependencies by name, and bounds `budgets.max_workers` to the task count and the runtime's four-run limit. Discovery proposes `package` relationships between registered repositories from `package.json` dependencies, `Cargo.toml` path dependencies and `go.mod` replace directives with evidence and `confirmed: false`; confirming a manifest that still lists an unconfirmed relationship is refused, and confirmed relationships must be acyclic. `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` on such a plan runs the task graph: after the same gates as one writer (with one environment fingerprint per repository), tasks whose dependencies completed run concurrently up to `max_workers`, never two writers in one repository, each as a writer attempt in its own owned worktree, with every completed producer bound into the consumer's writer environment and prompt as `LUUNA_DEPENDENCY_<REPOSITORY>_PATH`/`…_COMMIT`. Per-task state is durable (migration 10, `GET …/tasks`, `task.*` events); a dependency's failure blocks its dependents with the reason, cancellation records every task, a restart marks running tasks interrupted and keeps completed commits and worktrees, and `implement` with `task_id` resumes a failed, blocked or interrupted task under the original approval within the approved budgets (an attempt lost mid-prompt still reserves the remaining cost budget, so re-planning follows as for one writer). When every task completed, one candidate set freezes every repository's exact commit and the `<consumer>:<producer>` bindings; validation runs every repository's required recipes in its own candidate worktree with the same bindings, binds results to exact commits, fails the set naming the repository and recipe (`integration blocked`) when a consumer check fails, and gives the fresh reviewer one bounded combined diff. Repair of a multi-repository set is re-planning. See [ADR 0017](decisions/0017-multi-repository-coordination.md); delegated roles (P42) and dependency overrides (P44) remain open.

## Publication and host diagnostics

A `reviewed` candidate with a `passed` review may be published (`POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/publish` with the exact hash and an idempotency key) to GitHub only, by the repository's registered identity: the runtime pushes each repository's exact candidate commit to `luuna/<ticket>/<hash prefix>` and opens one pull request per repository against the manifest's default branch, linking them when there are several. Every external write is preceded by a durable intent (migration 11: `publications`, `publication_intents`) and looked up by its stable identity first (`git ls-remote` for the branch, the pull-request head for the PR), so a timeout after remote success, a partial publication and a replayed key never duplicate anything; `POST …/publication/reconcile` retries only steps the ledger does not show succeeded. `GET …/publication` refreshes CI (check runs and commit status) and merge observation under bounded timeouts; a failing CI is reported distinctly and changes no evidence, and `integrated` is set only when every pull request is observed merged by a person. There is no merge route or call; a test asserts it. The GitHub token (`LUUNA_GITHUB_TOKEN`) reaches Git only through scoped `GIT_CONFIG_*` headers and the REST client as a bearer header; only its presence is ever reported. Events: `publication.requested`, `publication.pushed`, `publication.pr_opened`, `publication.failed`, `publication.reconciled`, `publication.integrated`. `luuna-runtime doctor [--json]` reports Git, Python, Node, the pinned Pi probe, the data directory and database, token and credential presence by name, the service port and the component toolchain, exiting 1 when a required item is missing. See [ADR 0018](decisions/0018-publication-and-doctor.md); every publication test runs against a fake GitHub API and a local bare remote, so real GitHub evidence remains M7 exit work. `scripts/package-windows.ps1` builds an unsigned NSIS development installer carrying the desktop, the release runtime, the Windows helper scripts and the pinned Pi tree; the native bootstrap of ADR 0011 prefers that packaged layout when it is present beside the executable.

## API and service lifetime

All application routes use `/api/v1`. Implemented project routes are `POST /api/v1/projects` (register existing repositories by absolute root path), `GET /api/v1/projects[/{id}]`, `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/discover` (read-only proposal), `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/manifest` (confirm with `expected_revision`), `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/repositories/{repository_id}/rebind` (explicitly re-point a moved or re-identified checkout) and `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/events`. The canonical create-ticket route is **`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/tickets`** (implemented in M2c with an idempotency key; enabled projects use the Missions authority of ADRs 0003/0014). Do not add a parallel `POST /api/v1/tickets` alias. Other operations address ticket, plan, and run identities: `POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/plans` records the next immutable plan revision and opens its workflow run, `POST /api/v1/plans/{id}/approvals` approves one exact hash, `POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/implement` schedules the writer after transactional revalidation, and `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/worktrees` and `/attempts` expose the Luuna-owned worktree leases and attempts (ADR 0008). Commands that can create work require idempotency; operations sensitive to stale state require expected revisions. SSE streams use durable event IDs/cursors for replay and deduplication. Artifacts use authorized IDs, never arbitrary request-supplied filesystem paths.

Bind the development service to loopback and authenticate protected API actions. A development launch may use an explicitly managed foreground process. The desktop reconnects to that service; closing a window or losing SSE does not decide run lifetime. Explicit shutdown stops or reconciles owned workers and persists interruption: since 2026-10-21 work stopped by Ctrl+C or SIGTERM is recorded `interrupted` (resumable after restart), never `cancelled`, and the client shows a lost runtime as an outage, reconnects by itself and reloads authoritative state when the runtime answers again. A Tauri child/sidecar alone does not prove independent lifetime. Platform-specific startup, supervision, token storage, and shutdown must be tested before distribution. See [ADR 0004](decisions/0004-service-lifecycle.md).

## Milestone evidence

Windows orderly service stop is `POST /api/v1/shutdown`, authenticated with the
existing bearer token. The runtime closes scheduling admission, drains admitted
mutation handlers, interrupts owned work and exits cleanly; window closure is
still only a client disconnect. Windows scripts reuse the DPAPI-encrypted token
and data directory across restart. See [ADR 0010](decisions/0010-authenticated-service-shutdown.md).

The initial tool-free connectivity slice exposes authenticated run creation/history, cursor event replay and SSE, and cancellation. M2a adds read-only repository import, discovery proposals and confirmed manifest revisions; M2b adds supervised baselines with bound evidence; M2c adds temporary local tickets, immutable plan revisions, exact-hash approvals, Luuna-owned worktree leases and one scoped writer whose candidate waits in `validating`. M3 adds candidate-bound required checks, a fresh read-only reviewer, structured findings, optional bounded automatic repairs and conservative restart recovery; its genuine-provider exit is closed on Linux (see the status report) while native Mac/Windows lifecycle evidence remains open. The bounded M6 component slice adds explicit Missions migration/reconciliation and selected Atlas/Beacon plan resources. Publication, broader M6 parity and supported-platform exits remain separate capabilities.

| Milestone | Required proof | Does not establish completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0 | Locked build, schema fixtures, deterministic approval/transition rejection, durable state checks | Folder creation or documentation checks alone |
| M1 | Real pinned Pi/provider session, streamed API events, persistence, cancellation, error handling and restart evidence | Scripted worker or fixture-only protocol tests |
| M2a | Real and synthetic imports with byte-identical checkouts, rejected invalid/mismatched repositories, proposed (not executed) recipes, confirmed manifest replay after restart | A proposed manifest, a stored recipe, or any claim that a baseline ran |
| M2b | Genuine passing and failing baselines with commit/tree/environment-bound results and hashed artifacts; missing executable, empty suite, dirty checkout, deadline, cancellation and restart recorded as blocked/failed/cancelled/interrupted; stale baseline cannot enter implementation | A writer, a worktree, or any run that modifies a repository |
| M2c | One approved fixture feature changed only its Luuna-owned worktree with the developer checkout byte-identical; missing or stale approval, changed base, changed recipe, unrelated repository or path, stale baseline, second writer and exceeded budget refused; cancellation and restart preserve the worktree and void the attempt; a genuine pinned-Pi writer run through a real provider | Validation of the candidate, independent review, repair or any publication (M3+); any claim that prompt or guard scoping is an OS boundary |
| M3 | Candidate commit/tree/hash frozen; required checks executed in the owned worktree before any review; a fresh, separately identified read-only reviewer whose structured verdict the runtime enforces; a seeded failing check needing a new repair revision with fresh evidence; bounded automatic repair pausing at the attempt budget; cancellation and hard-kill recovery with reaped children and reserved spend; a genuine provider-backed run of all of the above (closed on Linux, October 17, 2026) | Fixture reviewer verdicts as provider evidence; a model's self-assessment as check evidence; native Mac/Windows lifecycle, which stays open; any publication or merge |
| Desktop integration | Real service connection, run actions, streamed state and reconnection | Frontend build or decorative simulation alone |
| Full v1 | Original requirements/acceptance matrix including browser/TUI parity and supported platform evidence | Single-repository Linux demo |

Required foundation checks are schema validation, Rust formatting/tests/lint, frontend type/build checks, and relevant fixture integration tests. Native desktop compilation requires platform prerequisites. Real provider smoke tests require existing credentials/model access and are reported separately. Mac/Windows jobs provide compatibility evidence only when they have actually run.

Luuna's original code and documentation are MIT licensed. Derived component distributions retain separate upstream notices. The original `VALIDATION-REPORT.md` validates a documentation delivery; keep product evidence separate. Registry package publication, signed installers, remote access, and production release still require explicit operational decisions and evidence; [RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md](RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md) is the M8 report that links every requirement and acceptance scenario to what has actually run and names what blocks the v1 label.

PR 11 preservation follow-up: historical artifact filenames remain readable;
identity-changing rebinds withdraw manifest confirmation without deleting history;
new plan revisions cannot bypass live-work guards. These guards are transactional
runtime policy. The desktop exposes cumulative ticket usage and diff omissions.
An interrupted restore resumes its durable intent before SQLite can open or create
the main file, keeping original database files and sidecars together in backups.
